intro.heading: What the last three points actually cost
paragraphs: A 45 is not a harder version of a 40. It is a different purchase. At 38 or 40 a family is buying teaching: content that was never properly covered, a topic that was skipped, a habit of leaving Paper 2 half-finished. At 43 or 44 the teaching is already done. What is left is the margin between a strong answer and a complete one, and that margin does not respond to more hours in the same way. Understanding which of those two things you are buying is the single biggest determinant of whether IB score 45 coaching in the UAE is worth the money.

The arithmetic is unforgiving and worth stating plainly. Six subjects are graded one to seven, which caps the subject total at 42. The remaining three points come from the combination of the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge grades, awarded through the IB's published core-points matrix. A 45 therefore requires a seven in all six subjects and the full three core points, with no failing condition triggered anywhere. Confirm the current matrix and the current failing conditions with your child's IB coordinator, because they are revised and this page is not the IB.

That arithmetic changes where the money should go. Most UAE families chasing the top band spend on their child's weakest Higher Level subject, because that is where the school report draws attention. The cheaper point is almost always in the core. A student predicted 43 with one core point available is one well-supervised Extended Essay away from 44, and that supervision is six to ten hours of work spread over months, not two hours a week for two years. The subject point, by contrast, can absorb eighty hours and still not arrive.

UAE market rates make the comparison concrete. Published rates run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget end of the online platforms to AED 650 for a premium named tutor, with IB and IGCSE specialists sitting at AED 200-450 and above. Those are market figures, each attributable to a provider who published it, and they are set out in full further down this page. What none of the providers publish is the thing a parent at 43 actually needs: how many of those hours convert into a point, and at what stage they stop converting at all.

This page is built around that question rather than around a sales pitch. It sets out how the 45 is assembled, what the UAE market charges and who charges it, where the next point is cheapest from each starting profile, what a tutor may and may not touch on an Internal Assessment, how one-to-one online tuition compares with a home visit bought locally, and how to check that the person you are paying is permitted to teach privately in the UAE at all. It also says, in plain terms, where the honest answer is to stop paying.

ib-score-45-coaching.programmesIntro: Only one IB programme produces a score out of 45. The other two matter to a top-band attempt for a different reason: they decide how well prepared a student is when DP1 starts, and whether the first term is spent learning content or learning how the IB marks.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma is the only IB programme scored out of 45. Students take six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, and complete the three core elements: the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Subject grades run one to seven and are set by a mixture of externally examined papers and internally assessed work that is externally moderated.
programmes.countryNote: Across the UAE the Diploma is the smaller share of a large private-school market. In Dubai, KHDA recorded 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with IB programmes accounting for 7 per cent of that enrolment. The intake for 2026-27 adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. A thin DP cohort in one school is why top-band specialism is often found online rather than nearby.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme assesses against criteria rather than against papers, and reports on a one-to-eight scale per criterion. Students arrive in DP1 fluent in criterion language and inquiry, and often unfamiliar with timed, closed-book examination technique. That gap is the most common reason a capable MYP student posts a five in the first DP mock and a family starts looking for coaching.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools running MYP into DP usually transition in a single August, with the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies timetable continuing unchanged through both. For a student aiming at the top band, the useful work happens in the MYP5 summer: examination technique, Higher Level subject choice, and an honest look at whether Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL is the right route rather than the prestigious one.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is a genuine IB qualification and it is not scored out of 45. Diploma courses taken within it are still graded one to seven, so subject-level coaching works the same way, but the core-points arithmetic on this page does not apply.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer UAE schools offer the Career-related Programme than offer the Diploma, so families comparing the two are usually choosing between schools as much as between programmes. If your child is on CP and someone quotes you for 45-point coaching, that is a signal to ask what they think they are selling. The right question for a CP student is which Diploma courses are being taken and what each one needs.

ib-score-45-coaching.subjectsIntro: At the top of the scale the subject matters less than the component. A seven is usually lost in one identifiable place: a paper, a criterion, a topic. The notes below name where that tends to happen for UAE candidates rather than restating the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The Higher Level course carries Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper that rewards sustained reasoning rather than recall. Top-band candidates rarely lose marks on technique; they lose them on the unfamiliar opening of a Paper 3 question and on exploration criteria, where personal engagement and reflection are marked but seldom practised.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Applications and Interpretation is modelling-led and technology-heavy, and a seven depends on reading context accurately before touching the calculator. Students who switched from Analysis and Approaches mid-DP1 often carry an algebraic reflex that costs marks here, where the examiner wants interpretation of the model and a stated limitation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Physics sevens are won on the long-answer and data-analysis components rather than on multiple choice. The recurring loss for strong candidates is uncertainty treatment in the internal assessment and an unexamined assumption in an extended answer. Both are coachable in a handful of sessions once the specific pattern is identified from marked scripts.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics absorb most revision time, while the marks at the top end move on data-based questions and on the internal assessment's evaluation section. A candidate already at six usually needs criterion-level feedback on their own write-up, not another pass through the reactions of alcohols.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology rewards precision of command terms more than breadth. Strong UAE candidates frequently describe where the paper asks them to explain, and lose the seventh mark across many small deductions rather than one failure. Marking their own past-paper answers against the published criteria is the intervention that moves this.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and real-world evidence carry the grade, and Higher Level adds quantitative demands that catch out students comfortable with the theory. The internal assessment commentaries are the component where a top-band student most often leaves marks on the table through article choice rather than through analysis.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the Higher Level essay reward a controlled argument about a global issue, not a tour of the text. Candidates predicted six tend to be assessment-literate but under-rehearsed on the oral, where ten minutes of unstructured talk costs a band. Rehearsal with criterion feedback is the whole of the fix.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study response discipline decides the grade: tools applied to the stimulus, with a conclusion that answers the command term. Higher Level candidates lose marks by writing everything they know about a tool rather than the part that bears on the case. The internal assessment stands or falls on the research question.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Higher Level adds abstract data structures and resource management, where strong coders often under-perform because the paper wants explanation rather than implementation. The solution component is where sevens are decided, and it needs supervision on documentation and testing rather than help with the code.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Arabic language courses matter twice over for UAE candidates: once as a Group 2 subject graded one to seven, and once because Arabic is a mandatory school subject under KHDA requirements regardless of the licensed curriculum. Written productive skills and the individual oral carry the grade, and both are rehearsable.

ib-score-45-coaching.regionsTitle: Where our UAE students sit the Diploma
ib-score-45-coaching.regionsIntro: Which emirate a family lives in changes who regulates the school, who approves its fees and curriculum, and how deep the local pool of Higher Level specialists goes. The last of those is the practical reason top-band coaching in the smaller emirates tends to happen online.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA recorded 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25, with IB programmes at 7 per cent of enrolment. Three of the seven new schools opening for 2026-27 are IB.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which is why an external specialist is the normal route here.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK. The Diploma cohort per school is smaller than in Abu Dhabi city, so a student needing Physics HL or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL at top-band level will often find no local specialist free at the hour they can actually study.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fee and curriculum approval sitting with the emirate regulator is worth knowing before a family compares two schools' Diploma offerings.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman. The IB cohort is small and concentrated in a handful of schools, which makes evening online sessions the only realistic way to reach a subject-and-level specialist without a cross-emirate commute.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Competitor pages in this market mention the emirate essentially not at all, which tells you how thin local provision is.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Families here are usually choosing between a local school and a longer commute to Dubai or Sharjah, and the commute is exactly what a DP2 evening cannot absorb once the Extended Essay and internal assessment deadlines land.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The smallest private-school market of the seven emirates, and the clearest case for delivering specialist Diploma coaching over live video rather than waiting for a specialist to exist within driving distance.

schoolClusters.note: The deepest IB market in the country, and the one where top-band candidates most often sit in a cohort with several other students chasing the same grade. Named here as ecosystem context for families comparing where the Diploma is taught.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School - Arabian Ranches

At top-band level the session is usually half diagnosis and half rehearsal: find the component where the seventh mark is going, then practise that component against the published criteria until the pattern changes.

sections.heading: What a 45 is made of, before anyone quotes you a price
paragraphs: A 45 is six sevens plus the full three core points, with no failing condition triggered. That is the whole specification, and it is worth writing down before a single hour is bought, because it tells you immediately which points are still available to your child and which are already gone. A student with a five in one Standard Level subject in DP1 is not out of the top band, but the path there now runs through a two-grade lift in that subject, which is a different and more expensive purchase than the one most families think they are making.

The six subject grades are produced by externally examined papers plus internally assessed work that is marked by the teacher and externally moderated. Both halves can cost a seven, and they fail in different ways. Papers are lost to technique and timing. Internal assessments are lost to criteria: a research question that cannot be answered in the space available, an evaluation section that lists limitations without weighing them, a reflection that reports feelings rather than learning. The second kind is cheaper to fix because it is fixable once, in writing, before submission.

The three core points are awarded on the combination of the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge grades through the IB's published matrix, and a sufficiently weak result in either can also trigger a failing condition that removes the diploma entirely. Those rules are revised, so confirm the current matrix and failing conditions with your child's IB coordinator or on the IB's own assessment pages rather than taking them from any tutoring site, this one included. What does not change is the shape of the arithmetic: the core is three points out of forty-five decided by two pieces of written work, and it is the part of the diploma over which a student has the most control and the longest run-up.

sections.heading: What top-band IB coaching costs in the UAE, and who publishes those numbers
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote United States dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. The table below is the AED version, assembled from rates those providers published themselves plus Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. These are market rates, not IB Gram's price list. Our own figure comes out of a conversation about how many hours the point gap actually needs, which is the only responsible way to quote for a 44-or-45 attempt.

Read the table by what the hour buys rather than by the number. At the budget end, AED 45-150 an hour buys supervision and content catch-up from a tutor who may be a university student, and that is a reasonable purchase for a student at 32 who skipped a term. It is a poor purchase at 43, because the work left is criterion-level feedback on Higher Level components, and a tutor who has not marked at that level cannot give it. The middle band, AED 150-300, is where a properly qualified subject tutor sits. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200-450 and above.

The premium band deserves a specific warning. AED 500-650 an hour is a defensible spend on a narrowly defined problem: one Paper 3 technique, one internal assessment criterion, one oral rehearsal. It is rarely a defensible weekly habit over two years, and the arithmetic of IB DP HL tutoring rates at that level is brutal once multiplied by eighty weeks. Be sceptical of anyone selling examiner status as a general advantage rather than as a specific skill, and more sceptical still of any page that attaches a grade to a price. Nobody can sell you a point.

sections.heading: The marginal point: where the next point is cheapest from each starting profile
paragraphs: Hours do not convert into points at a constant rate. The first ten hours spent on a subject a student has genuinely not understood can move two grades. The eightieth hour spent on a subject where the student already answers correctly but slightly incompletely may move nothing at all. This is the single piece of analysis the UAE tutoring market does not publish, and it is the one a family at 43 needs before signing up to a weekly slot for eighteen months.

The table below is a planning tool, not a promise, and it is built from the shape of the assessment rather than from any claim about outcomes. Read down the left column to your child's current prediction, then read the right-hand column first. In most profiles there is something cheaper than hours: a set of marked scripts nobody has read properly, a research question that needs narrowing, a Paper 2 timing habit that costs eight marks an hour. Those cost a conversation and a fortnight of discipline.

Two profiles deserve particular attention. A student predicted 40-42 with a core point still in play is in the best position on the table, because core supervision is the lowest-cost point available anywhere in the diploma. A student predicted 44 with both core points already secured is in the worst, not because they are weak but because there is nothing cheap left: the remaining point sits in a component where they already perform well, and buying it means a large number of hours with a low conversion rate. The honest advice at that point is to protect sleep, protect the deadlines, and stop paying.

sections.heading: The three core points are the cheapest points on the board
paragraphs: The Extended Essay and TOK core points are worth three of forty-five, which is the same weight as moving three subject grades. They are decided by two pieces of written work with deadlines a student knows a year in advance, and they are the only part of the diploma where a candidate controls both the question and the timetable. Despite that, the Extended Essay and TOK core points are the part of the Diploma UAE families most often buy support for last, usually in the term when the draft is already due.

Length limits are the practical constraint and the most common cause of a lost band. A research question that would need twelve thousand words to answer properly cannot score well in four thousand, however good the student is, and no amount of later editing rescues it. The same applies to the TOK essay on a prescribed title and to the exhibition with its three objects: each has a published limit, and each rewards an argument sized to that limit. Confirm every figure in the table below against the current subject guide your child's school issues, because the guides are revised.

What supervision looks like here is narrower than people expect. The useful sessions are a question-design session before any drafting, one round of criterion-by-criterion Internal Assessment feedback or essay feedback on the student's own draft, and a reflection session before the final submission. That is six to ten hours across several months. At market specialist rates of AED 200-450 and above, that is a defined and modest spend for a point that is genuinely available, which is why it belongs at the front of a top-band plan rather than at the end.

sections.heading: Where UAE families waste money chasing a 45
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake is buying hours in six subjects at once. It feels thorough and it is the standard response to a report card with three sixes on it, but it produces a student with no free evenings, six sets of homework from six tutors, and less time for the timed practice that actually moves a Higher Level grade. A top-band plan is narrow by design: two components at a time, with everything else held steady by the school.

The second is paying for teaching when the problem is marking. A student predicted six in Biology who describes where the paper says explain does not need the content taught again. They need twenty of their own answers marked against the criteria with the deduction named each time. Many families pay a premium hourly rate for a tutor to re-present material the student already knows, because re-teaching is what a tutoring session looks like and marking is not. Ask explicitly for marked work to come back, in writing, after every session.

The third is late buying. Core supervision purchased three weeks before a deadline can tidy a draft; it cannot change a research question. Subject coaching started six weeks before the May session can fix timing and technique, which is real, but it cannot build two years of content. Both are worth doing and both cost more per point than the same money spent a year earlier. The fourth mistake is paying anything at all to a provider who offers to produce the work: that is an academic-honesty breach, it is an expulsion risk for the student, and it is sold openly in this market at four-figure AED prices.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, offers and the point where 45 stops mattering
paragraphs: Universities make offers against predicted grades, not against final scores, which means the number that governs your child's destination is decided well before the May session. For most courses the offer sits in a band rather than at a point: a conditional offer of 38 with sixes in Higher Level subjects does not become better because the candidate finishes on 45. Knowing where the offer threshold sits is therefore the first piece of information a family should gather, because it tells you whether the last two points are worth buying at all.

Subject prerequisites bite harder than the total. A student with a 44 and the wrong mathematics route can be ineligible for a course that would have accepted 38 with Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL. Engineering, economics and most quantitative sciences specify the route, and the decision is made in DP1 when nobody is thinking about admissions. IB predicted grades also feed scholarship decisions at several UAE institutions, which is the one place where the difference between 42 and 45 does translate into money.

There is a separate regulatory step that has nothing to do with rank. Students using a UAE school certificate for local admission go through Ministry of Education equivalency, and the published requirements differ by curriculum. For the British track the Ministry requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. No IB points threshold for MoE equivalency should be taken from any tutoring page, including this one. Verify it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an internal assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay
paragraphs: This is the boundary that decides whether coaching helps your child or ends their diploma. IB academic-honesty rules require that assessed work is the student's own, and a breach is investigated as malpractice with consequences that fall on the student rather than on the tutor. One provider visible in this market sells finished Internal Assessments at a four-figure AED price. That is not a cheaper route to a 45; it is the fastest available route to losing the diploma entirely.

The line is not blurry, and it is easy to state. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what a criterion is asking for, ask questions that make a student's reasoning visible, read a draft the student has produced and say where it falls short of the criteria, and rehearse an oral. A tutor may not become an author of any part of the submission, supply wording for it, re-work a paragraph into its final form, or hand over a model answer for adaptation. The school supervisor remains the person who signs the work off and attests to its authenticity.

A practical test helps families police this without expertise in the subject. After a session, ask your child to explain the change they made and why the criterion required it. If they can, the session was teaching. If the document improved and the explanation did not, something went wrong. Keep the drafts. A supervisor who can see a sequence of the student's own drafts has everything needed to sign the work off, and a student who can talk through their own reflection has nothing to fear from a viva.

sections.heading: One-to-one online tuition against a home visit, for a top-band attempt
paragraphs: Home tutoring is a real and large part of the UAE market, and the honest version of what it costs is in the rate table above: AED 180-500 an hour for a one-to-one visit, with travel priced into the hour, and monthly packages of AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour sessions. The hidden cost is not money. It is the fact that the tutor pool shrinks to whoever is willing to drive to your address inside your window, which in practice means a capable generalist rather than a Chemistry Higher Level specialist.

IB Gram does not arrange home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. We deliver this as one-to-one online tuition over live video, and the case for that is strongest exactly at the top of the scale. A student predicted six in one Higher Level component needs the person who knows that component, not the person who lives nearby. Removing the drive also removes the constraint that pushes sessions into the worst hour of a UAE school evening, after a school run and before homework.

The screen is also a better working surface for this kind of work than a dining table. A marked script shared on screen, annotated live and saved afterwards, is a document the student can re-read the following week; a conversation over a paper copy is not. For a travelling family the continuity argument settles it: the same online IB tutor in the UAE stays with the student across a summer abroad and a change of address, and a two-year diploma cannot afford to restart its coaching relationship in DP2.

sections.heading: Checking that the person you are paying is permitted to teach privately in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any page quoting a figure with suspicion. MoHRE's own service page is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligibility is wider than most parents expect. The permit is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. That breadth is why the permit alone tells you little about teaching quality at Higher Level: a permitted tutor may be a sixteen-year-old or a head of department. Ask the permit question and the marking-experience question separately, because they are different questions with different answers.

There is one further distinction worth holding onto. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: it requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no regulator approval of any kind and claims none; we are a matching platform, not a licensed institute, and there is no UAE centre to visit. In Abu Dhabi, note that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, so the tutor your child already knows from the classroom is usually not an available option.

sections.heading: Coaching cost in context: school fees, the two-year plan and what you are really buying
paragraphs: Tutoring is usually the second education line in a UAE household budget, and it is the one with no published price list. The first line is more stable than it has been for years: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. The KHDA private school fee freeze is the right anchor for a conversation about what a coaching plan should cost, because it fixes the larger number while you decide the smaller one.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Multiply the specialist band across two subjects and twenty teaching months and the two-year figure becomes large enough to deserve the same scrutiny as a school fee. The useful discipline is to price the plan against the point gain you are actually buying rather than against a monthly feeling of doing something.

That is why our own conversation starts with the gap rather than with a rate. If a student is predicted 43 with a core point available, the plan is small: a core supervision block and one weekly subject hour, reviewed after the next mock. If a student is predicted 38 with two weak Higher Level subjects, the plan is larger and longer and the point arithmetic is better. If a student is predicted 44 with both core points secured, the honest recommendation is a short diagnostic block and then nothing, and we will say so rather than sell a schedule.

sections.heading: The UAE week: mandatory subjects, Ramadan and how much study time a 45 attempt really has
paragraphs: A top-band plan is a plan about a week, and the UAE week has fixed commitments that no competitor page in this market mentions. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires that those requirements be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. They are timetabled hours, they are assessed, and a Diploma revision plan has to work around them rather than pretend they are not there.

The organisational rules matter for planning too. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with schools free to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met and a minimum of twenty-five minutes advised for any mandatory subject lesson. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic need appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects any different or additional content needs prior permission from the Ministry of Education.

Ramadan reshapes the rest. School hours shorten, the productive part of the day moves, and a 5pm session that worked in January becomes the worst hour of the day. Families on a top-band plan usually move sessions to a post-Iftar slot for the month, keep the frequency and shorten the length, and accept that one week of the month is for consolidation rather than new material. Because lessons are delivered online in Gulf Standard Time, that shift is a scheduling change rather than a renegotiation with someone who has to drive. Plan it in advance: the Diploma deadlines do not move for the calendar, so the calendar has to be absorbed by the plan.

process.title: A short call about the gap, not the rate
process.description: We start by asking what the current prediction is, which components the marks are going in, and what the university offer actually requires. That conversation usually narrows a vague request for 45-point coaching into two named components. If the answer is that nothing worth buying is available, we say so on the call.

process.title: One free trial lesson
process.description: A single lesson with the proposed specialist, booked before any payment and with no package attached. For a top-band attempt the trial should use the student's own marked script rather than a generic diagnostic, so bring the last mock and the examiner comments. You decide afterwards whether the match is right.

process.title: A written plan with a target per component
process.description: We set out which components we are working on, how many hours a week, what the student does between sessions, and what the review point is. The plan names the components rather than the score, because components are what a tutor can influence and a final score is not something anyone can promise.

process.title: The weekly cycle: teach, practise under time, mark, name the error
process.description: Each session teaches a narrow thing, sets timed practice, and returns marked work against the criteria wording with the deduction named. A short written note goes out after every session so the student can re-read it. The running list of repeat errors is the document that tells you whether the money is working.

process.title: Review against the next mock, then decide again
process.description: After the next set of mocks we compare the marked evidence with the plan and change it, shrink it or stop it. Shrinking and stopping are normal outcomes near the top of the scale, and a provider who never recommends either is not reading the marginal-point arithmetic honestly.

Three of the most visible pages in this market publish no price at all. You cannot judge value against a figure nobody will state.

whyPoints.title: Specialism by component, not by subject

whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, review and give feedback on work the student has produced. They never author part of a submission or supply wording for one. The boundary is stated at the first core session, and it is a genuine difference from the providers in this market selling finished coursework.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you when to stop paying
whyPoints.description: A student predicted 44 with both core points secured has nothing cheap left to buy, and we say that rather than sell a schedule. The marginal-point table on this page is the same analysis we use internally, which is why it is published rather than kept for the sales call.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, IB or Cambridge approval and claims none. There is no UAE centre. No score, grade or improvement is promised anywhere on this page, and any statistic we cannot produce the underlying data for is simply absent.

faqs.question: What does a 45 in the IB Diploma actually require?
faqs.answer: A seven in all six subjects, which caps out at 42, plus the full three core points awarded on the combination of the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge grades, and no failing condition triggered anywhere. That is the complete specification. It means a single six in one Higher Level subject caps the total at 44, and it means the core is worth exactly as much as three subject grades. The core-points matrix and the failing conditions are revised periodically, so confirm the current version with your child's IB coordinator or on the IB's own assessment pages rather than taking them from a tutoring site.

faqs.question: How much does IB score 45 coaching in the UAE cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates for IB specialists in the UAE run AED 200-450 and above per hour, per Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. Budget platforms start lower, from AED 45-65 at EdFlik and AED 33-52 at Tutopiya, but that band rarely buys criterion-level Higher Level feedback. Those are market figures, not our price list. We quote after a conversation about how many hours the point gap genuinely needs.

faqs.question: Which point is the cheapest one left if my child is predicted 42?
faqs.answer: Usually a core point. If either the Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge still has a band in play, six to ten hours of supervision spread across months is the lowest-cost point available in the whole diploma, because the student controls the question and the timetable. A subject point from six to seven can absorb many times that number of hours with a lower conversion rate. Check the core first: look at the predicted EE and TOK grades, find out which combination your child is currently on, and only then decide whether subject hours are worth buying.

faqs.question: Can coaching move a predicted 41 to a 45 in the final six months?
faqs.answer: Nobody can promise that, and a provider who does is telling you something useful about themselves. What six months can realistically change is technique, timing and the core. A student predicted 41 with one core point available and two Higher Level components failing on specific, identifiable errors has a genuine path to 43 or 44. Closing four points in six months requires grade lifts in several subjects at once, which is a much larger claim. Ask for the marked evidence behind any projection, and plan against components rather than against a target number.

faqs.question: Is it better value to coach six subjects or the two weakest components?
faqs.answer: Two components, almost always. Six simultaneous tutors produce six sets of homework, no free evenings and less time for the timed practice that actually moves a Higher Level grade. A narrow plan also makes the spend legible: you can see whether one component improved, whereas six parallel plans make it impossible to know what the money bought. At the top of the scale the work is diagnostic rather than broad, so the question is which two components are leaking marks, not which subjects look weakest on the report.

faqs.question: Do UAE universities care about the difference between 42 and 45?
faqs.answer: For admission, usually not much. Offers are made against predicted grades and sit in bands, and a conditional offer with specified Higher Level grades does not improve because the final total is higher. Where the difference does matter is scholarship banding at several UAE institutions, which can be sensitive to the total. Subject prerequisites matter more than the total almost everywhere: the wrong mathematics route can make a 44 ineligible for a course that would have accepted 38. Find the threshold and the prerequisites before you decide whether the last points are worth buying.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legally and honestly help with on an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain what a criterion is asking for, question the student's reasoning, read a draft the student has produced and say where it falls short, and rehearse an oral component. A tutor may not become an author of any part of the submission, supply wording, re-work a paragraph into its final form, or hand over a model for adaptation. The school supervisor signs the work off. A simple parent test: after a session, ask your child to explain the change they made and why the criterion required it. If they cannot, something went wrong.

faqs.question: How do we check that a UAE tutor holds the private tuition work permit?
faqs.answer: Ask to see it. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, where the service is listed as private tutor licensing with a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Ask the permit question and the marking-experience question separately: eligibility extends to university students and to school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

faqs.question: Does a top-band attempt need Mathematics Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the destination, not on the score. Engineering, physical sciences and competitive economics courses generally specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and the wrong route closes those doors regardless of the total. Liberal arts, many business programmes and much of North American admission accept Applications and Interpretation. The decision is made in DP1, when nobody is thinking about admissions, which is why it is worth checking the prerequisites of three or four target courses before the choice is locked rather than after the first mock.

faqs.question: How do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect a study plan?
faqs.answer: They are timetabled, assessed hours that a revision plan has to accommodate. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requiring implementation from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and separate classes are required for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. In practice they fix how many usable evenings a DP2 week contains, which is the number a coaching plan is actually built on.

faqs.question: Should sessions move during Ramadan, and how?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. School hours shorten, the productive part of the day moves, and an afternoon slot that worked in January becomes the least useful hour of the day. The pattern that works is to shift to a post-Iftar slot, keep the weekly frequency, shorten each session, and treat one week of the month as consolidation rather than new material. Because lessons are delivered online in Gulf Standard Time, that is a scheduling change rather than a renegotiation with someone who has to travel. Agree it a few weeks in advance, because submission deadlines do not move for the calendar.

faqs.question: Why is this delivered online rather than by a tutor coming to our villa?
faqs.answer: Because specialism beats proximity at the top of the scale, and because of what travel does to both the rate and the timetable. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Market rates of AED 180-500 an hour for a local visit have the drive priced in, and the available pool narrows to whoever will travel inside your window. One-to-one online tuition over live video keeps the whole specialist pool open, lets sessions sit in the student's sharpest hour, and makes screen-shared marked scripts a document the student can re-read.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for the component we need?
faqs.answer: We say so, and we tell you the honest alternatives rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Niche requirements are where this bites: Further Mathematics, Philosophy, Arabic A and some Higher Level language combinations have thin coverage inside the UAE. Where no UAE-based specialist is available at the hour your child can study, the lesson is delivered over live video by a specialist outside the UAE, and we tell you that before you book. If nothing suitable exists at all, the right answer is a short wait or a different plan, not a worse match.

faqs.question: Does the Extended Essay have to be in the same subject as a Higher Level choice?
faqs.answer: It does not have to be, and for a top-band attempt the practical considerations usually outweigh the theoretical freedom. An essay in a Higher Level subject means the student is researching inside content they are already studying, which saves reading time in the most compressed year of the diploma. An essay in a Standard Level or unfamiliar subject can produce a fresher question but costs hours a 45 attempt rarely has spare. Check your school's own guidance too, since supervisor availability by subject is often the real constraint rather than IB rules.

faqs.question: What should we send when asking for a quote for top-band coaching?
faqs.answer: Send the current predicted grades by subject and level, the most recent mock papers with the examiner or teacher comments still on them, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge position, the university courses being targeted with their stated requirements, and the two or three hours in the week that are genuinely free. With those, a quote can name components and hours. Without them, any figure you receive is a guess dressed as a price, which is exactly how families end up paying for six subjects when two components were the problem.

ib-score-45-coaching.closingHeading: Start with the gap, not with the rate
ib-score-45-coaching.closingBody: If your child is already near the top of the scale, the useful first step is not booking hours. It is working out which points are genuinely still available and what each one would cost. Bring the latest mock papers with the comments on them, the predicted grades, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge position. We will tell you which two components are worth working on, what the market charges for that kind of work in AED, and whether the honest answer is a short block, a weekly hour, or nothing at all. Lessons run as one-to-one online tuition over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, and the first one is a free trial with no package attached.

For an option-form conversation, ask for the tutor who teaches the subject your child is least sure about rather than a general adviser. Every session runs online.

intro.heading: Six subjects, one form, and a window that closes in September
paragraphs: An IB Diploma is six subjects, one from each of six groups, with three taken at Higher Level and three at Standard Level. Alongside those sit Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. In most UAE schools the choice is made on an option form during the second half of Year 11, often in February or March, before IGCSE or MYP results exist. That sequence is the single biggest source of regret we hear about: families choose on a predicted grade, results arrive in August, and the form is already filed against a timetable that has been built around it.

The option form is not a wish list. Schools group subjects into blocks so that a timetable can be built, and a block that contains Physics, Economics and Visual Arts allows exactly one of those three. Two Higher Levels that look obvious on paper can sit in the same column and cannot both be taken. The first job of any useful subject-selection conversation in the UAE is therefore to read the school's own blocks, not a generic list of IB subjects.

After the form, there is a short grace period. Most IB schools allow a level change, and sometimes a subject change, in the first four to six weeks of DP1, provided the receiving class has capacity and the student has not missed too much. The deadline for registering candidates with the IB falls later in DP1, and after that point a change becomes a formal matter between the school's Diploma coordinator and the IB, not something a parent can arrange in a meeting. Nobody publishes those internal dates in a single place, so the school's coordinator is the only reliable source for your child's cohort.

There is a second layer in the UAE that families moving from Europe or Asia do not expect. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires schools to run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Those periods come out of the same week as six Diploma subjects. A DP1 timetable with three Higher Levels and a full mandatory-subject load is a genuinely heavy week, and that arithmetic belongs in the option-form decision rather than in a crisis conversation in November.

What this page gives you is the decision in order: what each group contains and where it constrains the next choice, the calendar counted backwards from the May session, how the Higher Level load actually lands across a fortnight, and what a university admissions office reads first in the six. Where a figure is quoted it is attributed. Where a date depends on your child's school or on the IB itself, the page says so rather than inventing one.

ib-subject-selection-guidance.programmesIntro: Subject choice is a Diploma Programme problem, but the groundwork is laid earlier and there is an alternative route most UAE families are never shown. These four blocks are the ones that matter to an option-form decision.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, assessed against four criteria per subject on a 1-8 scale, with the Personal Project in MYP 5. MYP does not tier subjects into Core and Extended the way IGCSE does, so a student arrives at the option form without a public grade that signals Higher Level readiness. The criterion profile is the evidence instead: a student scoring 7 and 8 on Criterion C in Sciences is a different proposition from one carrying those marks on Criterion A alone.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run an IB continuum, so MYP 5 students move into DP1 inside the same building and the same option blocks they have been timetabled against for years. That continuity is an advantage at option time, because the MYP subject teacher who writes the readiness comment is also the person who will teach DP1.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each graded 1-7, with up to three further points from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Higher Level courses carry 240 recommended taught hours against 150 at Standard Level, and that difference is where the extra content, the extra paper and most of the workload sit. The level decision is usually harder than the subject decision.
programmes.countryNote: The Diploma accounts for a minority share of enrolment in Dubai private schools, where UK curricula dominate, which means an IB student in the UAE is often the only Diploma candidate in a friendship group sitting IGCSEs and A-Levels. Option-form advice borrowed from an A-Level family rarely transfers, because A-Level allows three subjects and the Diploma requires six.

programmes.name: The DP Core: TOK, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge runs across both years and is assessed by an exhibition and an essay. The Extended Essay is an independent research piece in a subject the student has usually studied, and the two components together contribute up to three points on the Diploma. CAS is not graded but must be completed. The Core is the part of the Diploma that families forget to budget time for at option stage.
programmes.countryNote: The Extended Essay subject is chosen in DP1, and a student who picked a Group 4 subject only at Standard Level sometimes finds the essay they want to write needs Higher Level content they have not met. Thinking about a likely Extended Essay subject while the option form is still open costs nothing and occasionally changes a level decision.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning element, personal and professional skills, and a language development component. It exists for students whose strengths are concentrated rather than spread across six groups, and it produces a different certificate from the full Diploma rather than a weaker version of it.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is offered by a small number of UAE schools, so for most families it is a reason to ask the question rather than a live option. Where it is available, it changes the option-form conversation entirely: the question stops being which six and becomes which two or three, in depth.

ib-subject-selection-guidance.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects UAE families most often reopen after the option form has been filed. Each note says what the choice actually commits a student to, rather than what the subject is called.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus, algebraic proof and function behaviour, examined without a calculator in one paper at both levels. The Higher Level course is the standard prerequisite for engineering, physics and most economics degrees that teach with calculus. Students who chose it because it sounded stronger, rather than because a destination demanded it, make up a large share of mid-DP1 level changes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-permitted problem solving, with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout. The Higher Level course is a demanding statistics qualification and is accepted for many business, psychology and design degrees. The error families make is treating it as the easier maths rather than a different maths.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, thermal physics and the Higher Level additions in wave behaviour and quantum effects, plus a scientific investigation. Physics Higher Level paired with Mathematics: Applications rather than Analysis is survivable but awkward, because several derivations assume calculus the student has not been taught.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity, energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms, with Higher Level extending into further mechanism detail and quantitative work. It is the usual non-negotiable for medicine and most life-science degrees, which makes it the subject where a Standard Level choice at option stage closes doors quietly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, molecular biology, genetics, ecology and physiology, with Higher Level adding depth across every theme rather than new ones. The volume of precise terminology is the workload, not the conceptual difficulty, and students who read Biology as the light science are the ones surprised in DP2.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy, assessed partly through commentaries on published articles. Higher Level adds quantitative questions and a third paper. It is a popular Group 3 choice in the UAE because it reads as business-adjacent, and it is more diagram-dependent than most families expect.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, human resources, finance and operations, with Higher Level extending the content and the internal assessment. It rewards clear application to a real organisation, which suits students who can write about a specific company rather than recite theory. It is not a substitute for Economics where a degree names Economics.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Non-literary texts studied alongside literary works, with an individual oral, a paper on unseen texts and, at Higher Level, an essay on a studied work. For students whose first language is not English, the Higher Level paper on unseen non-literary texts is the component that separates grades, because it cannot be revised for by content.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic as an additional language, assessed through productive and receptive skills across five prescribed themes. It is the Group 2 route most non-Arab students in the UAE take, and prior exposure through a school's mandatory Arabic periods is uneven, so a realistic placement conversation before the form matters more here than in any other group.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A prescribed subject with source work, two world history topics, and at Higher Level a regional option plus an additional paper. The historical investigation is a genuine piece of research with a strict word limit. Students choosing History to avoid a science usually underestimate the reading load across two years.

ib-subject-selection-guidance.regionsIntro: Who regulates your child's school changes what an option form has to satisfy and who you escalate to if a promised subject does not run. These are the seven emirates and the authority that governs private schools in each.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Dubai holds the largest concentration of Diploma schools in the country, so option blocks here are usually wide and the constraint is timetable clash rather than subject availability.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
regions.note: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Diploma provision is concentrated in a smaller number of schools than Dubai, so a niche Group 6 or Group 2 choice is more often answered with a school-supported self-taught arrangement.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval sitting with the regulator means a school cannot simply add a Diploma subject mid-year because demand appeared.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and also approves curricula and assessment methods. Diploma options here are the narrowest in the country, and families frequently build a choice around what one school can actually timetable.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman. Families often commute to Dubai or Sharjah for Diploma provision, which puts a hard floor under how late an evening session can start on a school night.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Diploma candidates are few, and a student here is frequently the only one in a year group taking a particular Higher Level, which makes online one-to-one support the practical route to subject-specific teaching.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The east coast returns almost no mentions in published tutoring directories, so parents searching for a specialist in a named Higher Level subject locally will usually find nothing and should plan around live online teaching from the outset.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB continuum and Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: Schools running the Diploma, several of them across the full continuum from the Primary Years Programme upwards. Students moving MYP 5 to DP1 inside one of these have the advantage of a subject teacher who already knows their criterion profile before the option form is signed.

Diploma provision in the capital sits across a smaller group of schools, with several British-curriculum schools offering the Diploma as a sixth-form alternative to A-Levels. That dual offer makes the Year 11 option conversation a two-part decision: which qualification, then which six subjects.
schools: Repton Al Barsha and Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: A handful of schools offer the Diploma north of Dubai, and option blocks are correspondingly tighter. Where a school cannot run a chosen Higher Level, the realistic answers are a school-supported self-taught course, a different subject in the same group, or a change of school.
schools: The American School of Creative Science

ib-subject-selection-guidance.modesIntro: Option-form support is a short, specific piece of work, and it is not the same as weekly teaching. These three formats cover what UAE families actually ask for between February and November of DP1.

modes.title: Pre-choice subject trial
modes.description: A single online lesson in the subject your child is least sure about, pitched at Higher Level content from the start of the course rather than at revision of what they already know. The point is to produce evidence: what happened when the student met an unfamiliar Higher Level problem, and whether the gap is knowledge, method or pace.
bullets: One subject, one lesson, Higher Level material from week one of DP1
A written note afterwards naming what was fluent and what was not
Runs before the option form closes, not after
Delivered online, timed to Gulf Standard Time

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through DP1 and DP2
modes.description: Ongoing teaching in one or two subjects, following your child's own school scheme of work and internal deadlines rather than a parallel syllabus. For a student carrying three Higher Levels and a full mandatory-subject load, one well-chosen weekly session in the heaviest subject does more than three shallow ones.
bullets: Same tutor across both Diploma years where availability allows
Work paced to the school's own assessment calendar
Command-term and mark-scheme practice from the start, not in DP2
Sessions over live video, with shared screen and annotated working

modes.title: Six-week diagnostic block in early DP1
modes.description: A short, defined block of sessions inside the window where a level change is still administratively possible. It exists to answer one question honestly: is this Higher Level the right level, or is the student better placed at Standard Level with the time reinvested in the Core and the other two Higher Levels.
bullets: Starts in the first weeks of DP1, while a change is still open
Ends with a plain recommendation, including when that is to step down
Covers the specific topics the school has already taught
Written up so the Diploma coordinator can act on it

sections.heading: What IB subject selection guidance actually decides
paragraphs: IB subject selection guidance in the UAE decides four things at once, and families usually arrive thinking it decides one. It decides which six subjects a student studies, which three of those sit at Higher Level, which Extended Essay subjects stay available, and which university courses remain reachable two years later. Those four are entangled. A Standard Level Chemistry choice made because the timetable was tight removes most medical routes before DP1 has started, and no amount of later teaching reopens it.

The decision is also made with worse information than any other academic decision of the two years. In most UAE schools the form is signed in February or March of Year 11, which means it rests on predicted grades rather than IGCSE or MYP results. A student predicted a 6 in MYP Sciences who finishes with an 8 has over-chosen conservatively; one predicted an 8 who finishes with a 6 has a hard autumn ahead. The grace window in early DP1 exists precisely because schools know this.

What a useful conversation produces is not a recommendation about which subjects are good. It is a short list of the specific constraints in play for one student in one school: the blocks, the mandatory-subject load, the likely Extended Essay direction, the destination requirements that are genuinely non-negotiable, and the two or three choices that are genuinely open. Everything else on an option form is settled by those constraints before anyone expresses a preference.
The rest of this page works through that in order. It is a calendar first, because in the UAE the timing is what families get wrong, and a subject guide second.
bullets: Four decisions, not one: subjects, levels, Extended Essay range, destination range
Made in February or March of Year 11, before results exist
The early-DP1 window is the school's correction mechanism for that timing
Constraints come first; preferences choose between what is left

sections.heading: The six groups and the constraint each one carries
paragraphs: A Diploma student takes one subject from each of Groups 1 to 5 and then a sixth, which is normally a Group 6 arts subject or a second subject from Groups 1 to 4. That last substitution is the part most option booklets explain badly, and it is the single most useful piece of flexibility in the structure. A student who wants three sciences takes a second Group 4 subject in place of Group 6, which is permitted, and the real limit is whether the school can timetable it.

Each group carries a different kind of constraint. Group 1 is settled by language of instruction and rarely argued about. Group 2 is settled by prior exposure, and in the UAE that exposure varies wildly between a student who has had mandatory Arabic since Year 1 and one who arrived in Year 10. Group 3 is where most genuine choice sits, and where a wrong pick costs least. Group 4 is where destination requirements bite hardest. Group 5 is a binary route choice with long consequences. Group 6 is where the timetable usually forces the hand.

The table below sets out each group with the option most commonly available in UAE schools and the constraint that decides it. Read it against your own school's option booklet rather than instead of it, because block structures differ between schools in the same emirate and change between cohorts. A pairing that ran for last year's DP1 group is evidence that the school can timetable it, not a promise that it will again this year, and the coordinator will tell you which of the two you are looking at if you ask directly.

sections.heading: The option-form calendar, counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Work backwards and the subject-selection problem becomes a scheduling problem. The final examinations for a student starting DP1 in August sit in the May session of the second year, nearly two academic years later. Between those two points are a set of deadlines, most of them internal to the school, and each one closes something that was open before it.

The IB does not publish a public option-form deadline, because there is none: that date is set by each school's timetabling cycle. What the IB does set is the candidate registration deadline in DP1, after which a subject or level change becomes a formal amendment rather than an administrative one. Schools build their own internal cut-off several weeks earlier so that the coordinator can submit a clean registration. Ask for both dates by name.

On examination dates themselves this page is deliberately silent. The IB's own assessment pages block automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and publishing one that later proves wrong would be worse than publishing none. Confirm your child's session window and results date with the school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org, and treat any date you read on a tutoring website, including the windows quoted by competitors, as unverified until you have.

One further note on reading the table. The milestones in the left column are sequential, but the evidence that should inform each one arrives out of order: results land after the form is filed, and the first genuinely useful assessment of Higher Level readiness arrives after the change window has already started counting down. Families who plan for that inversion, by testing the uncertain subject before the form and again in week three of DP1, get two chances at the same decision instead of one.

sections.heading: Three Higher Levels: how the load actually lands
paragraphs: A Higher Level course carries 240 recommended taught hours against 150 at Standard Level. Three Higher Levels and three Standard Levels therefore amount to roughly 1,170 hours of taught content across two years, before Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Expressed per week across a 36-week year, that is the whole of a school timetable with nothing spare, which is why the Diploma feels different from three A-Levels within about six weeks of starting.

The load is not evenly distributed, and that is the part worth planning for. Higher Level sciences front-load content and back-load the investigation. Mathematics at either Higher Level accumulates: a weak fortnight in differentiation is still a problem in DP2. Group 1 and Group 3 subjects spread their demand across continuous reading and writing that does not show up as homework. The Extended Essay lands in the middle, in the same term as the first serious internal assessments, and students who chose three content-heavy Higher Levels meet all of it at once.

This is where the Standard Level decision earns its keep. Dropping one Higher Level to Standard Level frees roughly 90 taught hours and, more usefully, removes one additional paper and one layer of extension content. Families read that as lowering ambition. In practice a student with two strong Higher Levels, three solid Standard Levels and a well-run Extended Essay often finishes with a better total than the same student spread thin across three Higher Levels, and most university offers name one or two Higher Level subjects rather than three.

The honest version of this advice has a limit. Where a destination names three Higher Level subjects, the arithmetic above does not apply, and the right conversation is about support and sequencing rather than about reducing the load.
bullets: 240 taught hours at Higher Level against 150 at Standard Level, per subject
Roughly 1,170 taught hours across the six, before the Core

sections.heading: Where a wrong subject choice shows up, and when it is still fixable
paragraphs: A wrong choice announces itself on a predictable schedule. In the first three weeks the signal is pace: the student follows the lesson but cannot start the homework alone. By week six it is the first assessed piece, where a mark two or three grades below the predicted level is information rather than a bad day. By the end of DP1 it is the internal assessment, which in most Group 4 and Group 5 subjects requires the student to design something independently and exposes a shaky content base immediately.

The fixable window maps onto the first of those signals and barely onto the second. A level change in week five is a conversation with the coordinator. The same change in February of DP1 means the student joins a Standard Level class that has covered different material and sat different assessments, and it may need an amendment to the IB registration. A change in DP2 is usually not possible at all, and the realistic options become targeted teaching, a tighter internal assessment and accepting a lower grade in one subject while protecting the other five.

Which is why the diagnosis matters more than the diagnosis being comfortable. Three different problems look identical in week four. A content gap from Year 11 is quick to close with focused teaching. A method gap, where the student knows the material but cannot structure an answer to a command term, takes longer but responds well. A genuine level mismatch, where the abstraction required is beyond what the student can currently hold, does not close with more hours, and pretending otherwise costs a family a year of sessions and a grade anyway.

A tutor who has taught the subject at Higher Level can usually tell these apart inside two lessons. The test is whether the recommendation that comes back includes the possibility of stepping down, because an adviser whose answer to every diagnosis is more tutoring is not diagnosing.
bullets: Week three signal: follows the lesson, cannot start the homework
Week six signal: first assessed mark two or more grades below prediction
End of DP1 signal: cannot design the internal assessment independently
Content gap, method gap and level mismatch look identical and need different answers

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit outside the six
paragraphs: Every option-form conversation in a Dubai private school happens inside a constraint that families arriving from outside the Gulf do not know about. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's published requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Those periods are timetabled alongside the six Diploma subjects, not instead of one of them.

The organisational rules are specific and worth knowing, because they explain why a timetable looks the way it does. KHDA requires that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

Two consequences follow for subject selection. The first is arithmetic: a DP1 week containing three Higher Levels plus mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies periods has very little slack, and that is the week in which the Extended Essay is supposed to start. The second concerns teaching material. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so support in these subjects means working with the school's own prescribed material rather than importing an alternative scheme.

sections.heading: What an admissions office reads first in the six
paragraphs: Universities do not read six subjects equally. They read the subjects their own course names, at the level it names them, and then they read the total. A student with three strong Higher Levels in the wrong three subjects is in a weaker position than one with two Higher Levels in the right two, which is why destination requirements belong at the start of the option-form conversation rather than at the end of DP1.

The patterns differ by system rather than by individual university. British offers are usually written as a total points score with named Higher Level grades attached, so one Higher Level subject can be the whole of an offer. North American admissions read the transcript as a whole and weight the overall profile, the essays and the testing picture, so a single Higher Level choice carries less determinative weight but a missing prerequisite for a specific major still bites at course registration. Continental European systems, particularly the Dutch and the German, tend to specify subject combinations precisely and admit or reject against them mechanically.

For UAE destinations, the governing process is equivalency rather than admission alone. The Ministry of Education sets out what each curriculum must show, and the published British-track requirements are specific: proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, plus five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five. No equivalent points figure for the Diploma has been read on a Ministry source for this page, so none is published here. Verify the current Diploma requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before you plan around it.
