igcse-february-march-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: A February-March entry only exists on one of the qualification routes below, and the route your child is on is decided by the department rather than the school as a whole. Read these against your child's actual syllabus codes, which appear on the statement of entry the exams officer issues once the entry has been accepted.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is the two-year qualification most UK-curriculum schools in the UAE teach in Years 10 and 11. Subjects carry four-digit syllabus codes: 0580 maths, 0620 chemistry, 0625 physics, 0610 biology, 0500 first language English. Most subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C or 5 and Extended reaching A* or 9. Cambridge runs the qualification in a June series and a November series, and publishes a separate March series with papers in early February.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates each UAE exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable your child sits is the one for that zone rather than a global one. Whether the March series is open at your centre is a decision made by the school's exams officer, usually in the autumn term, and it can be open for some subjects and closed for others. Ask for the statement of entry and the zone timetable in writing.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses codes beginning 4: 4MA1 maths, 4PH1 physics, 4CH1 chemistry, 4BI1 biology. Assessment is almost entirely by written paper, with practical skills examined on paper rather than by coursework in most sciences. Pearson International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, with provisional timetables published ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027. There is no February-March series on this board.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE families this is the single most common source of confusion about February exams. A parent hears from another family at the school gate that papers start in February, assumes it applies to their child, and discovers in December that the department is an Edexcel department with a May entry. June 2026 Pearson results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Cambridge O Level sits alongside IGCSE in some UAE schools, particularly those serving families from South Asia where the qualification has a long history. Content overlaps heavily with IGCSE but assessment differs in places, including the treatment of practical science and the availability of coursework components. Cambridge runs O Level in the same June and November series as IGCSE and includes it in the March series arrangements published for that series.
programmes.countryNote: If your child is on O Level rather than IGCSE in the UAE, the paper numbers and the mark schemes a tutor works from are not interchangeable with the IGCSE versions, even where the topic list looks identical. Confirm the four-digit code on the statement of entry before the first lesson. A tutor working from the wrong code will teach content that is on the syllabus but not on the paper your child sits.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint
programmes.description: Checkpoint tests sit below IGCSE and are used by schools to set tiers and groupings before Year 10 begins. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which is a different calendar from the IGCSE series and a frequent source of crossed wires in UAE parent groups. Checkpoint results carry no university or equivalency weight; their value is diagnostic and internal to the school.
programmes.countryNote: A March Checkpoint test is not a February IGCSE paper, and the two are often confused in UAE school newsletters because both fall in the same part of the year. The practical link is tiering: a weak Checkpoint result in maths frequently leads a Dubai or Abu Dhabi school to place a child on Core rather than Extended, which caps the achievable IGCSE grade two years later. That is the point at which Year 9 support changes an outcome.

igcse-february-march-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: Subjects below are listed with the syllabus codes a UAE exams officer uses, because a February entry is made against a code and not a subject name. Where Cambridge and Pearson differ materially the difference is stated. Ask the exams officer which code appears on the statement of entry before any tutoring starts.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Cambridge IGCSE 0580 maths examines across two papers at each tier, with no coursework. Marks go missing in bearings, compound interest set out without working, histograms with unequal class widths, and the final structured question where candidates stop after part (a). Extended is capped at a higher grade than Core, so tier confirmation matters more than any revision plan.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken by UAE students heading for A Level maths or IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches. Content runs ahead of 0580 into calculus, logarithms and kinematics. The common failure is treating it as harder 0580 revision rather than a separate syllabus with its own command terms and its own expectations about exact-form answers.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism dominate the lost marks, followed by any question asking for a described experiment with a named control variable. Cambridge 0625 includes an alternative-to-practical route; Pearson 4PH1 examines practical skills inside written papers. A tutor must know which of the two your child sits before planning a single lesson.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables are where grades are made. The February run punishes any student who has memorised tests without understanding what the observation proves. Organic chemistry nomenclature is reliable mark territory and is usually the fastest recoverable topic in a six-week block.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The content volume is the problem, not the difficulty. Marks are lost on definitions that must be stated precisely, on osmosis questions answered in loose language, and on extended-response questions where candidates write everything they know instead of answering the command term asked.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: Taken by UAE students who need science breadth without three separate entries. The syllabus is a reduced selection from the three single sciences, which makes past paper choice the whole skill: a tutor pulling questions from 0625 that are not on 0653 wastes a February week the student cannot get back.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, with speaking endorsement
subjects.description: The most common English entry in UAE private schools. Reading comprehension marks hinge on lifting the exact words the question needs; writing marks hinge on register and task fulfilment rather than vocabulary display. Speaking is assessed separately and is usually arranged by the school well before the written papers.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the composition paper reward control of structure over length. Marks disappear when a candidate writes a narrative with no shape or answers a directed-writing task in the wrong voice. February preparation here is almost entirely timed practice with line-by-line feedback on the student's own writing.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries a large share of the marks, and most lost marks come from unlabelled axes or a curve shifted in the wrong direction. Data-response questions reward reading the table before writing. Gulf examples work well in evaluation answers and are often the differentiator at the top end.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: The syllabus is accessible; the marking is not forgiving. Candidates lose marks by defining terms instead of applying them to the case study, and by ignoring the business context given in the stem. Evaluation questions need a judgement with a stated reason, which is a skill rather than a body of content.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / 0984)
subjects.description: Paper 1 theory marks fall away on binary and hexadecimal conversion and on network topics described loosely. Paper 2 rewards pseudocode written to the Cambridge conventions rather than in a programming language the student happens to know. Trace tables are the highest-yield topic for a short February block.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508)
subjects.description: Sat by Arab students in UAE private schools alongside the mandatory Arabic the regulator requires, which are two different things on a timetable. Support here is literary analysis and formal written register rather than conversational fluency, and it runs in Standard Arabic throughout.

igcse-february-march-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: A February-March entry looks different in each emirate, because the authority approving the school, the number of Cambridge centres nearby and the evening travel reality are all different. The notes below are about the exam and regulatory position in each place rather than about neighbourhoods.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Dubai had 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools in 2024-25, with 37 per cent of enrolment on a UK curriculum and 17 curricula licensed in total. That density means a February entry refused at one school may be available at another, and KHDA publishes inspection reports and a school listing you can read before asking.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and is named by almost none of the tutoring sites competing for this search. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff also bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which changes who you may legitimately hire in January.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain sits under ADEK rather than a separate authority, so the regulatory answer is the same as Abu Dhabi city while the practical one is not. Fewer Cambridge centres means less choice of series, and the drive to a neighbouring centre is long enough that an online tutor removes a real constraint on evening timing.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Assessment arrangements therefore sit inside SPEA's approval remit, which is worth knowing before a parent asks a Sharjah school to open a series it has not applied for.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority, so inspection reports and policy documents live on moe.gov.ae. The practical consequence for a February entry is that questions about assessment arrangements go to the school and then federally, with no local regulator in between.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like SPEA, approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. RAK is one of three emirates that returned zero mentions across the whole competitor corpus researched for this project, which tells you how little published guidance a RAK parent has to work with.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Centre choice is narrow on the east coast, and a family whose school does not open the February series is realistically choosing between the June entry and a long drive. Online lessons are the only form of specialist support that does not add that drive to the week.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Umm Al Quwain also sits under the federal Ministry of Education. The emirate has the smallest private-school base in the country, so subject specialists at IGCSE Extended level are genuinely scarce locally. This is the clearest case in the UAE for matching a child to a tutor by syllabus code rather than by postcode.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's UK-curriculum sector is the largest single curriculum group in the emirate and the main source of February-series questions. Schools in this group differ on which board each department uses, so two children at the same school can be on Cambridge and Edexcel in different subjects. KHDA publishes inspection reports for all of them.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain schools
schoolClusters.note: Students we support in Abu Dhabi sit IGCSE in schools regulated by ADEK, where the staff ethics rules on private tutoring are tighter than most parents realise. Evening availability is the binding constraint here rather than tutor quality, which is why Gulf Standard Time scheduling matters more than proximity.

Schools here answer to SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Fewer Cambridge centres per emirate means series choice is narrower and the June entry is the default more often than in Dubai.

sections.heading: What a February-March IGCSE entry actually is
paragraphs: A February-March IGCSE entry means Cambridge's March series. For 2027 the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027. Final entries were due at the centre on 27 November 2026, forecast grades on 27 February 2027, results arrive on Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027 and certificates in late June. If your child is on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, there is no February-March series at all: that board runs May/June and November only.

This matters because the phrase parents search and the thing schools do are not always the same. A family hears about February papers, assumes it is a standard option, and finds in December that their school never applied. Cambridge's own exam administration guidance describes the June and November series as the regular pattern for IGCSE and O Level, and publishes the March series dates separately. Whether the March series is open at a given UAE centre, and for which subjects, is decided by that centre.

There is a second layer that catches families out: zone allocation. Every Cambridge exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and there is a separate version of the timetable for each. Cambridge states that it is essential for a centre to use the correct version for its zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam when the wrong version has been used. A parent reading a timetable found through a search engine may be reading a different zone's paper times. Ask the exams officer which zone the centre sits in and work only from that timetable.

The practical test is short. Get the statement of entry. It names the board, the four-digit or four-character syllabus code, the tier and the series. Everything else on this page follows from those four facts, and a tutor who starts work without them is guessing.

sections.heading: Who decides the series, and who regulates the school
paragraphs: Two different decisions get confused. Cambridge decides when the series runs and when entries close. The school decides whether to open it. The emirate regulator licenses the school and, in two emirates, approves assessment methods as part of that licence. None of those three bodies is you, which is why the useful conversation is with the exams officer rather than with the class teacher.

The UAE regulator map has five entries and is published on u.ae. Dubai: the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain: the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah: the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Ras Al Khaimah: the Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah: the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in those three emirates.

The detail worth carrying into a meeting is that Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A Sharjah school cannot treat an exam-series change as a purely internal matter, because assessment methods sit inside what SPEA approves. In Dubai and Abu Dhabi the licensing framework is similar in spirit even where the published wording differs, and the federal baseline behind all of it is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

IB Gram holds none of these licences and claims none. We are an independent tutor-matching platform with no UAE premises, which means we are outside this regulatory structure rather than inside it. What we can do is explain it accurately, point you at the authority's own page, and make sure the tutor your child works with knows which board and code the school has actually entered.

sections.heading: The March 2027 calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: Read a session calendar forwards and it looks like a list of dates. Read it backwards and it becomes a plan, because every milestone has a thing that must already be true by the time it arrives. The table below counts the March 2027 series backwards from the certificates to the entry, using the dates Cambridge publishes in its key-dates document for the March series.

One feature of that calendar surprises every parent who sees it for the first time: forecast grades were due on 27 February 2027, which is after the exam period opened on 3 February. That ordering tells you what a forecast grade is for. It is an administrative submission the centre makes to Cambridge, not a prediction that should be argued over or used to set a revision target. Families who spend January lobbying a department over a forecast grade are spending the most valuable four weeks of the year on the one number that will not change an outcome.

The second feature is the length of the gap between the papers and the results. Papers finish on 4 March 2027; results reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. That is a ten-week wait during which the June series entry window for any resit also moves. The decision a family should make in early March, not late May, is what happens if one subject goes badly, because by the time the result arrives some options have narrowed.

Dates for the IB Diploma are deliberately absent from this page. The IB's own assessment pages could not be verified by automated checking for this project, so no IB session or results date is published here. If your child sits both IGCSE and a later IB programme, confirm every IB date with the school's IB coordinator or ibo.org directly.

sections.heading: Ramadan, study leave and the UAE academic year
paragraphs: Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier in the Gregorian calendar each year, which places it across February and March for several years to come. For a February-March exam series that is not a scheduling footnote; it is the central fact of the revision period. Confirm the actual dates against your school's published calendar, which is set locally and announced each year rather than fixed in advance.

What changes in practice is the shape of the day rather than the amount of work. School hours shorten in Ramadan at most UAE private schools. Energy is lowest in the late afternoon, which is exactly when a conventional after-school tutoring slot falls. Families who fast move lessons to after Iftar, and the sessions that work are shorter and more frequent rather than the same ninety minutes pushed later. A 45-minute paper-marking session at 9.30pm achieves more than a tired 90 minutes at 5pm.

Online delivery is what makes that timing workable at all. A 10pm lesson that requires nobody to travel is a different proposition from one that requires a 25-minute drive in each direction at the end of a fasting day. This is the clearest case on the whole page for the format: a family in Al Ain or Fujairah can hold a specialist 10pm slot with a tutor who is not within driving distance, and hold it reliably every week, because the only thing that has to arrive on time is a video call.

Study leave is the other calendar item to pin down early. Schools decide independently when Year 11 teaching stops and revision leave starts, and the date is not always published far ahead. A family planning a January block of paper practice needs that date before booking hours, because study leave frees up mornings that were previously unavailable and is the cheapest extra capacity in the whole plan.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies do not pause for papers
paragraphs: Every UAE parent planning a February entry eventually runs into the mandatory subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. These lessons sit on the same timetable as 0580 maths and compete for the same evening hours at home.

KHDA's guidelines are specific in ways that matter to anyone arranging support. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies runs in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs.

Two further rules shape what a tutor may legitimately do. Schools must ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have the appropriate approval from KHDA to teach these subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. A tutor cannot bring in their own Islamic Education material or a parallel Arabic scheme of work. Support in these subjects means working through the school's own set material and the language skills behind it.

The federal baseline sits underneath all of this: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. KHDA's instructional-time rules are calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency after a February result
paragraphs: A February-March result is a Cambridge result and carries the same weight as a June one. The question that follows is what the UAE Ministry of Education counts when a family later needs a secondary certificate recognised, and the published British-track rule is specific enough to be worth stating exactly. Students on the British track must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

The exclusion in that rule is the part most families get wrong. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. One tutoring site currently ranking for UAE searches states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. If a subject list has been built around the wrong number, a February entry may be solving a problem the family does not have while leaving a real gap unfilled.

For families on the American track the published requirements are different again: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics via at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No IB points threshold appears in the source read for this page, so none is published here. Any figure for IB equivalency should be read on moe.gov.ae or at the emirate attestation authority before a family relies on it.

Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not a service a tutoring platform performs. IB Gram does not file equivalency applications, cannot influence an outcome and does not describe tutoring as a step in the process. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and anyone suggesting otherwise is creating urgency that the regulation does not support. Verify your own case at the official channel.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks go missing in a compressed February run
paragraphs: A February entry compresses the final phase of a two-year course into the autumn term. There is no spring to recover in, which changes where the marks go. The losses are rarely about unknown content; they are about unpractised execution under a timer, and they repeat so predictably across subjects that a marked mock paper usually tells a tutor more in one hour than a parent's description does in three sessions.

In maths 0580 and 4MA1 the pattern is bearings, compound interest written without working, histograms with unequal class widths, and the final structured question abandoned after part (a). In physics 0625 and 4PH1 it is electricity and electromagnetism, and any question requiring a described experiment with a named control variable. In chemistry 0620 and 4CH1 it is moles arithmetic, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables, where students have memorised the test but cannot state what the observation proves. In biology 0610 and 4BI1 the content volume is the problem rather than its difficulty, and precise definitions carry more marks than a wider reading of the topic.

The command terms are the second systematic loss and the cheapest to fix in six weeks. Describe, explain, compare, evaluate and justify each ask for a different structure, and a student who answers all five the same way loses marks in every subject at once. Working through five past paper questions sorted by command term rather than by topic is often the single highest-yield hour in a February block.

The third loss is timing, and it is specific to this series rather than general. Papers sit close together in a four-week window, so a student who has only ever done untimed topic exercises meets three papers in six days with no practised pacing. Sitting a full paper under exam conditions, then marking it against the published mark scheme, is what converts knowledge into marks. The mark scheme is referenced and read at the official source; it is not reproduced or supplied as a download.

sections.heading: What February-March preparation costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. The table below is market data in dirhams, attributed to whoever published each figure, read in October 2026. It is not an IB Gram price list. Our own position is a trial lesson first, free of charge, one per subject, and a quoted rate after the subject, tier and number of weeks are known.

The bands are wide for a reason, and the reason is useful. A budget online hour and a specialist hour are not the same product sold at different prices; they buy different things. The lower band buys topic explanation. The upper band buys someone who has marked the paper your child is sitting and can say which four topics are costing marks. For a February entry with eight weeks left, the second is usually better value per dirham even though it costs more per hour, because there are not enough weeks left to waste on general revision.

In-home rates in this market carry travel inside them. Bestimate's Dubai figures put home visits at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online tutor. That gap is substantially unpaid travel time being priced into the hour. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE at any price; home visits are a service we offer only in India. What the online format buys a UAE family is tutor choice by syllabus code rather than by driving distance.

One more cost note on timing. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is outside that freeze and is priced by the market, so a family budgeting for a February entry should treat the hourly figure as the variable and the number of weeks as the thing to decide early.

sections.heading: Permits, your child's own teachers, and who may legally tutor
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the position is clearer than most tutoring websites make it sound. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 regarding the introduction of private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here; a figure circulating online as a specific dirham penalty could not be verified against any official source. MoHRE's own service page for the permit is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. That is the route to check, and a parent may simply ask a tutor to show the permit in the app.

The rule that reshapes a January plan in Abu Dhabi concerns your child's own teachers. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's school. This is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK document before being relied on, but the direction is unambiguous. Hiring your child's own subject teacher privately is not the shortcut it appears to be.

A tutoring business with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. In Dubai it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE premises and makes no claim to approval from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Any tutoring site telling you its tutors carry a regulator's seal of approval is making a claim you should ask it to evidence.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the deadline is three weeks away
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but where coursework or a practical component exists the honesty boundary is identical and it is the point at which a tutoring market splits in two. A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has written. A tutor does not write, draft, complete or produce any part of an assessed piece. One site ranking for UAE tutoring searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that is a malpractice trigger for the student, not a service, and it is the reason this boundary is stated on every page we publish.

What that looks like in a session three weeks before a deadline is concrete. A tutor may read a draft and say the conclusion does not follow from the data, that the method section omits the control, that the graph axes are unlabelled, or that the argument repeats itself in paragraphs four and six. A tutor may ask the questions that make a student notice those things unaided. A tutor may not rewrite the paragraph, supply the missing sentence, or hand over a worked version to copy from. If a parent cannot tell from the finished piece which parts the tutor wrote, the boundary has already been crossed.

Materials carry the same line. We reference IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables, cite the official URL and link out to it. We do not reproduce them, host them or supply them as downloads. Reproducing an examination board's material is a copyright matter, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure for the school as well as the student. A tutor who offers a bundled drive folder of papers is offering something they are not entitled to distribute.

The practical benefit of saying this out loud is that it gives a parent a usable test. Ask a prospective tutor directly what they will do with a draft. The answer separates teaching from ghostwriting faster than any credential check, and in a February run, when pressure is highest and the temptation strongest, it is the question most worth asking in the trial lesson.

sections.heading: Online, in the room, or in a group before a February paper
paragraphs: Parents ask whether online tutoring really works for a child who learns better face to face, and the honest answer depends on what the last six weeks need to achieve. For a February entry the work is marked past papers, mark-scheme analysis and timed practice. All of that is screen work: the paper is shared, the annotation happens live, the recording is available afterwards. The format costs nothing in that mode and buys something significant, which is choice of tutor.

The constraint it removes is geography. A child in Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain sitting Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Extended has a very small local pool of tutors who have taught that exact tier. Online, the pool is every tutor who has, in any time zone that can hold a Gulf Standard Time evening slot. For a scarce combination such as Additional Mathematics 0606 or Computer Science 0478 Paper 2, that is the difference between a specialist and whoever is available.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address. Home visits are a service we offer only in India, and every UAE lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video. We would rather say that plainly than let a parent discover it after booking, and the table below compares the options on their merits so you can judge the trade honestly. Where a family genuinely needs an adult physically present with a younger child, the in-room option exists in this market at the rates shown and we will say so.

Availability is the last thing to be honest about. If no tutor covering your child's subject, tier and board has a free slot at a workable Gulf Standard Time hour, we say so and give an expected timeframe rather than filling the slot with someone who teaches the subject but not the paper. Four weeks before a February series that answer is unwelcome, which is exactly why it has to be true.

process.title: Send the statement of entry
process.description: Board, syllabus code, tier and series, as the exams officer issued them. Four facts, one screenshot. Everything after this depends on them, and a February plan built on a guessed code teaches content that is on the syllabus but not on the paper. If the statement has not been issued yet, ask the school which series it has entered and get the answer in writing.

process.title: Send one marked mock paper
process.description: The most recent timed paper, with the marks on it. A marked script shows which topics are costing marks and which are solid, which a conversation about how the term has gone cannot do. If no timed paper exists yet, the trial session produces one. Untimed topic exercises are not a substitute at this stage of the year.

process.title: Trial lesson on one paper
process.description: Free of charge, one per subject, before any block of hours is booked. The tutor works through the paper with your child and sends a written list of the topics actually losing marks. You get that list whether or not you book anything further, and some families reasonably decide on the strength of it that tutoring is not needed.

process.title: Fix the weeks and the slot
process.description: Count the teaching weeks left to the exam window, subtract study leave and the Ramadan weeks, and book against what remains rather than against a round number of hours. Slots are held in Gulf Standard Time and set for the whole block, including the post-Iftar timing if the family fasts, so the hour does not move week to week.

process.title: Decide the March question before results
process.description: Papers finish on 4 March 2027 and results reach centres on 13 May. Agree in early March what happens if one subject goes badly, because the June entry window moves during that gap. A plan made in March is a choice; the same plan made in late May is whatever is still available.

whyPoints.title: We tell you who controls the entry
whyPoints.description: The series, the tier and the zone timetable are decided by Cambridge and your child's exam centre, not by a tutoring platform. Saying that plainly is more useful than implying we can influence any of it. What we can do is make sure the tutor works from the right code, the right tier and the right board from the first session onward.

whyPoints.title: Dirham figures, attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: Market rates on this page are in AED, read in October 2026, and attributed to whoever published them. None of them is presented as our price list. Three of the six competitor pages researched publish no price at all and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family actually pays in.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claimed that we do not hold
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no permit or accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, operates no UAE premises, and says so. We explain what each body governs and link to its own page. Anyone claiming a regulator's seal for private tutors should be asked to produce the permit number.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line on assessed work is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback. A tutor does not write, draft or complete any part of a piece that must be the student's own work. We reference board materials at their official source and link out rather than reproducing or distributing them. Both positions are published so you can hold us to them.

whyPoints.title: Online, in Gulf Standard Time, and said upfront
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. Home visits are a service we offer only in India. Slots are held in Gulf Standard Time and can run after Iftar during Ramadan, which is the timing most February revision weeks actually need, and nobody loses forty minutes to an evening drive at either end.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed, not papered over
whyPoints.description: If no tutor covering your child's subject, tier and board is free at a workable hour, we say so and give a timeframe rather than filling the slot with someone who knows the subject but not the paper. Four weeks before a February series that is an unwelcome answer, which is precisely why it is the one we give.

faqs.question: Who actually decides whether our child can be entered for the February March series?
faqs.answer: The exam centre does, which in almost every UAE case is the school. Cambridge publishes the March series and sets the deadlines - final entries for the 2027 series were due 27 November 2026 - but whether a centre opens that series, and which subjects it opens inside it, is the centre's decision through its exams officer. A parent cannot submit an entry independently. The practical step is to email the exams officer, ask which series the school has entered your child for, and ask for the statement of entry showing the board, syllabus code, tier and series in writing.

faqs.question: Does KHDA, ADEK or SPEA have any say over which exam series a private school enters?
faqs.answer: Indirectly, and more in some emirates than others. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai and ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority goes further: SPEA and the Department of Knowledge approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Assessment arrangements therefore sit inside the licence rather than outside it. None of these bodies enters an individual candidate, so the conversation about your child's series still starts and usually ends with the school.

faqs.question: Our school will not open a February entry. Can we use a different centre in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Some Cambridge centres accept private candidates for subjects their own students do not take, and Dubai's 227 private schools mean more centre options there than in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain. Two things decide it: whether the centre accepts external candidates for that subject in that series, and whether the entry deadline has passed. Both are answered by contacting the centre directly. A tutoring platform cannot arrange an entry on your behalf and anyone implying otherwise is selling something they do not control.

faqs.question: Which authority approves the curriculum and fees at a school in Ras Al Khaimah or Fujairah?
faqs.answer: They are different. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in that emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fujairah has no emirate-level authority of its own: the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Fujairah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain. For a RAK parent that means fee and assessment questions go to the Department of Knowledge; for a Fujairah parent they go to the school and then federally to moe.gov.ae. Almost no tutoring site in the UAE names either body, which is why parents in these emirates get vaguer answers than they deserve.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons stop while February papers are running?
faqs.answer: Generally not, and that is the scheduling problem nobody warns parents about. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA required its arrangements to be in place from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. These lessons keep their timetable slots and their internal assessments while exam papers are being sat. Build the February plan around a week that still contains them rather than a hypothetical week in which the only subjects left are the examined ones.

faqs.question: Will a February March IGCSE result be accepted for UAE equivalency later on?
faqs.answer: A March-series result is a Cambridge IGCSE result and counts the same as a June one. The published British-track rule is that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and separately show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority, because equivalency is a Ministry process and no tutoring platform performs or influences it.

faqs.question: Is a teacher from my child's own school allowed to coach him through a February entry?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi, no. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's school. This is press-reported, so confirm it against the current ADEK document, but the direction is clear enough that hiring your child's own subject teacher privately is not the convenient shortcut it looks like. An independent tutor working from the same syllabus code avoids the question entirely.

faqs.question: Does the tutor we hire for February need anything from MoHRE before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which introduced private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you. Ask a tutor to show the permit in the MoHRE app.

faqs.question: Our school wants a forecast grade signed at the end of February. What is it for?
faqs.answer: It is an administrative submission the centre makes to Cambridge. For the March 2027 series forecast grades were due on 27 February 2027, which falls after the exam period opened on 3 February. That ordering is the clue: a forecast grade cannot be a revision target if it is submitted while the papers are already being sat. Families who spend January arguing with a department over a forecast figure spend the most valuable weeks of the year on the one number that will not change the outcome. Use those weeks on marked timed papers instead.

faqs.question: What do UAE families pay per hour for February March IGCSE support?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run roughly AED 45-150 for budget online or university-student tutors, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180-500 for a tutor physically present with travel priced in, and AED 200-450 or more for an IGCSE, IB or A-Level specialist. Monthly packages of AED 799 online for eight sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 in-home for four two-hour sessions are also published in this market. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson, once subject, tier and weeks remaining are known.

faqs.question: Can a tutor send us Cambridge mark schemes and a past paper pack to keep?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who offers it. We reference syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables, cite the official URL and link out to cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com. We do not reproduce them, host them or supply them as downloads. Reproducing a board's material is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure for the school as well as the student. In a session the tutor works from the official source live, which gives your child the same material with none of that risk attached.

faqs.question: Ramadan lands across the February March window. How should a revision week be built?
faqs.answer: Shorter sessions, more of them, after Iftar. Ramadan shifts around eleven days earlier in the Gregorian calendar each year, so it sits across this exam window for several years to come; confirm the exact dates against your school's own calendar. School hours shorten, and energy is lowest in the late afternoon when a conventional after-school slot falls. A focused 45 minutes marking one paper section at 9.30pm beats a tired 90 minutes at 5pm. Online delivery is what makes a late slot workable at all, because nobody travels at either end of it.

faqs.question: Does a school's published inspection band tell us anything about February results?
faqs.answer: Less than parents hope. An inspection band is a judgement about a whole school across many measures; it is not a prediction for one candidate in one subject in one series. The report is still worth reading for what it says about specific departments, teaching quality in the subject you care about and progression at the top end, and KHDA publishes Dubai reports openly while ADEK and SPEA publish for their own emirates. Use it to shape the questions you ask the head of department, not as a forecast for a single February paper.

faqs.question: We relocate from Sharjah to Abu Dhabi in January. Does the February entry survive?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the centre rather than the emirate. The entry sits with the Sharjah centre that submitted it, and that centre has an allocated Cambridge zone with its own timetable. Moving house does not move an entry. Ask both schools three things in writing: whether the original centre will still host your child for the papers, whether the new school is a centre for those subjects in that series, and whether the deadline for any transfer has passed. Lessons themselves continue unaffected, because they run online and the slot does not depend on which emirate you sleep in.

faqs.question: No tutor in the UAE covers the subject we need for February. What then?
faqs.answer: We say so and give you a timeframe. For scarce combinations such as Additional Mathematics 0606 or Computer Science 0478 Paper 2, the honest options are a specialist in another time zone who can hold a Gulf Standard Time evening slot, a later start with a better-matched tutor, or no match at all for that series. What we will not do is fill the slot with someone who teaches the subject but has never worked the paper and tier your child is entered for. Four weeks out that answer is unwelcome, which is why it needs to be accurate.

faqs.question: How is an online lesson in February different from one in October?
faqs.answer: The content of the hour changes completely. October sessions build understanding and fix the topics a term has exposed, with homework between lessons. February sessions are triage: the student sits a timed paper alone, the tutor marks it against the published mark scheme, and the session covers only what was lost. Nothing already secure is revisited. Sessions get shorter and more frequent, timing is rehearsed paper by paper, and the written summary after each one lists topics rather than impressions, because there is no spare week left to spend on the wrong thing.

igcse-february-march-exam-preparation.closingHeading: Start with the statement of entry, not with a search for a tutor
igcse-february-march-exam-preparation.closingBody: Four facts decide everything on this page: the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series. Email your child's exams officer and get them in writing. If the answer is Cambridge and the March series, the exam window is 3 February to 4 March 2027 and the plan is marked timed papers from January, arranged around study leave and Ramadan. If the answer is Pearson Edexcel, there is no February series and you are planning for May. Send us the statement of entry and the most recent marked mock paper, and the trial lesson will tell you which four topics are actually costing marks. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

igcse-home-tuition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE at Core and Extended tier across Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel syllabuses. Each profile names the syllabus codes they have taught and the papers they set practice on. Pick two, request a free trial lesson with both, and compare how each one handles the same past-paper question.

intro.heading: Start with the date on the entry form, not with the subject
paragraphs: Most searches for IGCSE home tuition in the UAE happen in one of two weeks of the year: the week January mock results come home, and the week in April when a parent counts the Fridays that are left. Both are late. Not fatally late, because a Year 11 student can still move several grades in twelve weeks of structured work. But late enough that the decisions with the longest reach have already been taken by somebody else. The tier on the entry form is fixed. The subject count is fixed. Any coursework mark is largely banked.

The useful opening question is not how to find a tutor. It is which series your child is sitting, and what should already be done. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with a March series used by centres in some regions, and Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November each year. Those are the only clocks that matter. Your child's centre sits in one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that the zone decides which version of the timetable applies.

So this page is organised as a countdown rather than a brochure. It starts at paper one and walks backwards: the final entry deadline, the forecast-grade form, the coursework and practical windows, the twelve-week revision block, results day and the two short windows that follow it. Each milestone names who sets it, because roughly half are set by the board and half by your child's own school, and a parent who confuses the two tends to miss the one that could still have been acted on.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE home tuition as one-to-one online tuition. There is no visiting-tutor service anywhere in the Emirates; household visits are something we run only in India. That is said here rather than discovered in week three, and the first table below puts the two formats beside each other on price, travel and the size of the pool a family gets to choose from. For scale: market rates for a visiting tutor in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour once travel is inside the price, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, on figures published by Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table and by agencies including Unitors.

Nothing here assumes anything about your child's school except that it is a private school in the UAE. That means it answers to KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, or the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those bodies touch a tutoring plan in two concrete ways. They set the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons that share your child's week with physics revision, and in Dubai and Abu Dhabi they publish inspection reports you can read before deciding whether the gap sits with your child or with the teaching.
bullets: Cambridge's final entry deadline for the March 2027 series fell on 27 November 2026, roughly ten weeks before the first paper.
Forecast grades for that same March series are due on 27 February 2027, after the exam period has already opened.
Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs to 19 November 2026; its June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026.
Core and Extended is a tier chosen on an entry form, not a difficulty setting a tutor can adjust in April.
Every lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram runs no visiting-tutor service in the Emirates.

igcse-home-tuition.programmesIntro: IGCSE is one qualification with two main examining boards in the UAE and two tiers inside most of its subjects. The four routes below are the ones a UAE family actually meets, and each carries its own calendar. Find the one your child's school uses: the syllabus numbering tells you the board, and the board tells you which timetable, which entry deadline and which results date apply to your house.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The four-digit syllabus codes starting 0 are Cambridge: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English. Most sciences and mathematics are tiered, so a candidate is entered either for Core papers or for Extended papers, and the entry fixes which. Assessment is almost entirely by terminal written paper, which is why the revision block before the series carries so much of the grade and why the entry deadline matters more than parents expect.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the wrong zone timetable is the centre's risk, since it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper. Ask your child's exams officer, in writing, which zone the school sits in and for the zone-correct timetable PDF. UAE centres also have access to the March series as well as June and November, which widens the resit options a family has.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The codes beginning with a digit and two letters are Pearson: 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PM1 Further Pure Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. Grading runs on the 9 to 1 scale. Several Pearson subjects are available in a modular shape, where a unit can be sat in an earlier series and carried forward, which changes a revision plan completely: some of the marks are already on the table before Year 11 begins.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes International GCSE series in May/June and November, and its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the next day; the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables for future series, including International GCSE November 2027, so a UAE family should plan from the live official PDF rather than from a date copied off a tutoring page.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The two years before IGCSE are where the arithmetic, algebraic fluency and written structure that IGCSE papers assume are either built or quietly skipped. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and those results are a far better predictor of an IGCSE grade than a school report, because they are externally marked against a published standard rather than against the rest of the class.
programmes.countryNote: In a UAE school a Year 9 Checkpoint result arriving in May or October is the cheapest early-warning signal a family will get. A weak Checkpoint mathematics mark in October of Year 9 is four school terms of runway before the first IGCSE paper, at a tutoring cost roughly a third of what the same gap costs to close in the February of Year 11. Most families only discover this after the expensive version.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level
programmes.description: The qualification many UAE IGCSE students move into, sat in the same June and November series pattern and in the same zone system. It matters at the IGCSE stage for one reason: sixth-form entry conditions are written in IGCSE grades, usually as a minimum in the subject plus a minimum in mathematics or English. The grade a Year 11 needs is therefore not an abstract target but a published number on a school's own admissions page.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. That makes AS and A Level choices part of the same paperwork chain as the IGCSE grades, and worth sketching out before the Year 11 options form is signed.

igcse-home-tuition.subjectsIntro: Subjects are listed by syllabus code because that is the unit of work a tutor actually prepares for. 0580 and 4MA1 are both called IGCSE Mathematics and they are not the same paper, the same mark scheme or the same tier structure. Tell us the code from your child's exam entry or the front of their past-paper booklet and the match becomes a straightforward question.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 Cambridge, 4MA1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Extended papers carry algebraic manipulation, functions, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles and probability trees that Core does not reach. Marks go missing in the same three places every series: unsimplified algebraic fractions, bearings questions where the diagram is never drawn, and multi-step problems abandoned halfway because no working was written down. Method marks are recoverable without the right answer, and most students do not know that.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics (0606, 4PM1)
subjects.description: The bridge subject for anyone heading to A Level Mathematics or an engineering route. Calculus, binomial expansion, logarithms and vectors appear here before they appear in the sixth form. The usual failure is treating it as harder 0580 rather than as a different habit: these papers reward setting up a problem symbolically before touching a calculator, and students trained on numerical substitution stall in the first five minutes.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 Cambridge, 4PH1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism are where the Extended tier separates from the Core, and where a UAE cohort usually loses the most marks. Circuit questions require reasoning about potential difference rather than recall. The practical paper and the alternative-to-practical paper test graph plotting, anomalous-result identification and precision of apparatus description, all of which can be practised on paper and all of which are routinely left until the final month.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 Cambridge, 4CH1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry, then organic chemistry, in that order of difficulty for most candidates. The recurring loss is in calculation presentation: an answer given without units, to the wrong number of significant figures, or with the limiting reagent never identified. Qualitative analysis questions on ion tests are nearly free marks and are nearly always under-revised because they feel like memorisation rather than chemistry.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 Cambridge, 4BI1 Pearson)
subjects.description: The content volume makes this feel like a reading subject, which is the trap. Extended papers ask for explanation chains, so a student who writes that stomata close in heat without linking water loss, guard-cell turgor and gas exchange gets one mark where three were available. Transport in plants, osmosis practicals and genetic-cross notation are the three topics most worth timetabling early.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Common in UAE schools where a student takes sciences as one or two blocks rather than three separate subjects. The syllabus is a selected subset of the three single sciences, which means a tutor who teaches it from the single-science specification will cover material that is not assessed. Checking the exact syllabus code before the first lesson prevents paying for several hours of content your child will never be examined on.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500 Cambridge, 4EA1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended-response questions carry the bulk of the grade, and both are assessed on structure and register as much as on content. Most marks are lost by students who summarise rather than analyse, and by students who write long. A timed-planning routine, practised weekly from October, moves this subject more reliably than any amount of vocabulary work.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510, 0511)
subjects.description: Widely taken across UAE schools and often the subject that quietly decides a sixth-form or equivalency outcome. Reading comprehension questions reward precise lifting of the relevant phrase rather than paraphrase, and the writing tasks are marked against register, audience and task fulfilment. Speaking components are assessed internally by the school, so the school's own window, not the board's, sets that deadline.

subjects.name: Economics (0455 Cambridge, 4EC1 Pearson)
subjects.description: Diagram-led. A supply and demand diagram with unlabelled axes or no shift arrow earns nothing, however good the prose around it. Students who revise definitions and neglect diagram drills tend to plateau around the middle grades. Data-response questions also require quoting figures from the extract, which is a technique rather than knowledge and takes about three sessions to fix.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450 Cambridge, 4BS1 Pearson)
subjects.description: The case-study paper rewards application to the named business, and generic answers about motivation or cash flow score in the lowest band regardless of accuracy. Evaluation marks go to candidates who commit to a judgement and justify it. Ratio and break-even calculations are a dependable source of marks for a student who finds the written side harder.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478 Cambridge)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and the theory of data representation. Students who code confidently in Python often lose marks because the paper wants Cambridge pseudocode conventions, not working code. Binary and hexadecimal conversion, logic gates and the fetch-execute cycle are high-frequency, low-cost topics that reward deliberate drilling in the twelve weeks before the papers.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First and as a Foreign Language (0508, 0544)
subjects.description: Taken alongside the international curriculum in UAE schools and examined in the same series as every other IGCSE. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, so a tutor must be matched to the correct pathway rather than to the subject name alone.

igcse-home-tuition.regionsIntro: The emirate your child's school sits in changes three practical things: which authority publishes the inspection report you can read, who approves the school's curriculum and fees, and how crowded the early-evening tutoring slot is locally. Delivery itself is identical everywhere, because lessons are one-to-one over live video. The notes below are about calendars and oversight, not about travel times.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees the quality of private education in the emirate, and its mandatory-subject requirements applied from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Dubai had 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with 37 per cent on a UK curriculum, which is why Cambridge and Pearson entry deadlines dominate the local calendar.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, as press-reported in 2026, so the convenient option a parent is sometimes offered is the one to decline.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller British-curriculum cohort than Abu Dhabi island. That matters at entry time rather than at lesson time: fewer local centres means fewer alternatives if a subject is dropped from a timetable, so confirming the entry list with the exams officer in November is worth more here than almost anywhere.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval sitting with the regulator is a useful fact for a parent: the subject list a school offers is not purely a school decision, so a mid-year subject change is rarely quick.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools here. For an IGCSE family that means inspection reporting is less locally granular than Dubai's, so the published evidence to lean on is the school's own results profile and the externally marked Checkpoint results rather than an emirate inspection band.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. Families here often sit exams at a centre some distance from home, which makes the zone-correct timetable and the exam-day logistics worth confirming in writing well before February.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education, with a small number of British-curriculum cohorts. The practical consequence for tuition is availability of specialist subjects rather than of tutors generally: Further Pure Mathematics or Computer Science may have no local specialist at all, which is precisely the case online delivery answers.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The smallest IGCSE cohort of the seven emirates, and the clearest example of why a family should not be limited to tutors within driving distance: a single Extended-tier physics specialist may not exist inside the emirate in a given term.

schoolClusters.note: Students we support sit IGCSE at schools across this group, which run Cambridge and Pearson entries side by side. Several enter different boards for different subjects, so one household can be working to two timetables at once. Confirming board and tier per subject is the first thing a plan needs.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain cluster
schoolClusters.note: A smaller British-curriculum group under ADEK, where sixth-form entry conditions published by the schools themselves are the clearest statement of what IGCSE grades a student needs. Those published conditions make a better revision target than a general ambition to improve.

Sharjah, Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah schools where cohorts are smaller and specialist subject teaching is thinner on the ground. This is the cluster where a family most often finds that the subject they need help with has no local specialist available in exam term.

igcse-home-tuition.modesIntro: Four shapes of support, chosen by where you are in the countdown rather than by budget alone. A Year 10 family and a Year 11 family eleven weeks from paper one should not buy the same thing. All four are delivered one-to-one over live video, with a free trial lesson before any block is committed.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across Years 10 and 11
modes.description: One or two sessions a week, running with the school's scheme of work rather than ahead of it, so that each topic is consolidated while it is still being taught. This is the cheapest way to arrive at the February of Year 11 without a backlog, and the format where a tutor can actually build the exam technique a paper rewards rather than patching content.
bullets: Session keyed to the topic the school taught that week
A past-paper question set after each topic, marked against the official mark scheme
A running list of recurring errors, reviewed monthly
Checkpoint or mock results used to re-order the plan, not just to report it

modes.title: The twelve-week series block
modes.description: A fixed block running from roughly twelve weeks before paper one to the final study leave, built around papers rather than topics. Sessions move to two or three a week, each one anchored on a timed question set under exam conditions, with the marking done together so the student sees where the mark scheme actually awards credit.
bullets: Zone-correct timetable used to order the subjects by paper date
Timed sections rather than whole papers in the first six weeks
Mark-scheme reading as a taught skill, not an afterthought
A written stop rule for topics that are not worth more hours

modes.title: Coursework and practical-skills clinics
modes.description: Short, specific sessions on the components that are marked inside the school or that test practical reasoning on paper: the alternative-to-practical papers, graph and error analysis, and the planning and evaluation skills a science paper assesses. The student's own work stays the student's own work throughout; the session teaches the technique and reviews what the student has written.
bullets: Graph plotting, anomalous results and precision of description
Planning an investigation to the criteria a paper actually rewards
Feedback on a draft the student wrote, never text written for them
Your school's internal deadline treated as the hard date

modes.title: The between-series resit sprint
modes.description: For a student moving from a June result to a November entry, or from November to the following March or June. The window is short and the content is already taught, so the work is diagnostic: read the statement of results, identify which papers cost the grade, and spend the available weeks on those papers rather than on a full re-teach of the syllabus.
bullets: Component-level reading of the statement of results
Entry confirmed with the exams officer before any hours are bought
Plan written in weeks remaining, not in topics remaining
Explicit decision on which subjects are not worth re-entering

sections.heading: What a UAE family is actually buying when they search for IGCSE home tuition
paragraphs: A search for IGCSE home tuition in the UAE is a search for a private, one-to-one hour with somebody who knows the papers. The word home describes where the parent expects the lesson to happen, not what the lesson is. Once the format question is separated from the teaching question, the two can be answered honestly and in order, and the answers turn out to point in different directions for most families in the Emirates.

The market answer for a visiting tutor is a real one. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts a household visit at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, with independent visiting tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500, and monthly in-home packages advertised around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. The price absorbs travel. So does the timetable: a tutor crossing Dubai at 5pm is not available for three other households that evening, which is why the pool a family can book from shrinks to whoever lives within reach of their address.

IB Gram does not run a visiting-tutor service in the UAE. Tuition here is delivered as one-to-one online tuition over live video, one student and one tutor, with household visits offered only in India. The trade that buys is the whole point: a family in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain chooses an Extended-tier 0625 physics specialist on the strength of what they have taught, not on the strength of their postcode, and the hour that would have gone on a drive goes on the paper instead.

The table below sets the options side by side. Group classes at a centre are included because they are genuinely cheaper and genuinely right for some students; school-run support is included because it is free and is the first thing a family should exhaust. The AED figures are what the market publishes, not an IB Gram price list, and each is attributed in the cost section further down.
bullets: Separate the format question from the teaching question before spending anything
Price a household visit including travel, not at the headline hourly figure
Ask what happens to the booking when a tutor's own timetable changes
Exhaust the school's own after-hours support before buying private hours

sections.heading: Three series a year, and finding the one your child is entered for
paragraphs: IGCSE is not an annual event. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, plus a March series used by centres in some regions, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. That means a UAE family may be working to any one of several different clocks, and most parents are surprised to learn which one their child is actually on.

The second thing to establish is the zone. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for that zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong timetable was used. A zone is not a detail for the exams officer alone. It changes the date of paper one, which changes the order a revision block should run in, which changes what a tutor should be teaching in March.

The third is the board, per subject. Plenty of UAE schools enter Cambridge for sciences and Pearson for mathematics, or the reverse, and a few enter different boards for different students in the same class. Since the syllabus code determines the paper structure and the mark scheme, a tutoring plan built on the wrong code is wasted work at full price. The front page of a past paper carries the code; so does the entry confirmation the school can print.

The table below gathers the dates Cambridge and Pearson have actually published, using the Cambridge March 2027 series as the worked example of how far ahead the administrative deadlines sit. Note what the dates show: the entry closes about ten weeks before the first paper, and the forecast-grade deadline lands after the exam period has opened. Confirm every date against the board's own live timetable before planning around it, since provisional timetables are revised.
