sections.heading: The tutor permit, the ethics rule, and the four questions to ask first
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, not informal. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, u.ae states that it 'is granted free of charge for two years', and MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Eligibility is broader than parents expect. u.ae lists teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE 'will be subject to fines and penalties' outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here and you should distrust any page that quotes one. A separate restriction matters in the capital: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct points the same way. Asking for your child's own teacher privately is asking them to breach that.

So four questions, before any money moves. Which board and syllabus code have you taught, and for how many series? Do you hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may we see it? Who marks the work between lessons, and what do we receive in writing? And what exactly happens if the match does not work after two sessions? A provider claiming any regulator's approval has already answered a different question badly: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE or board accreditation, operates no UAE premises, and says so on every page rather than in a footnote.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the school deadline is tonight
paragraphs: There is a line in IGCSE coursework, portfolio and practical work that a tutor does not cross, and the week before a school deadline is when families are most tempted to ask. The rule is simple to state: the student's work has to be the student's own, and a tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback on it. A tutor never writes a sentence of it.

In practice the honest version is more useful than the dishonest one anyway. A tutor can teach the skill the task assesses, read a draft and say which paragraph does not answer the question, mark a practical write-up against the published criteria, model the method on a different dataset, and run the timed conditions the real paper will impose. A tutor cannot supply text, restructure a piece into its final shape, provide completed work to copy from, or sit beside a student editing until the thing is finished. Boards and schools treat that as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever took the money.

This matters commercially as well as ethically, because the alternative is openly on sale in this market. One site ranking for these queries advertises finished Internal Assessments at a fixed price; that is an academic-integrity breach, and buying it puts a child's entry at risk for the sake of one deadline. Reproducing board material is the other common trap: we reference and link official syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com rather than hosting copies, because distributing them is a copyright problem regardless of how convenient it would be. Ask any provider where the line sits. The answer tells you what you are buying.

process.title: Send three facts, not a shortlist
process.description: Board, syllabus code, series. One email to your school's exams officer produces all three, and they determine everything that follows: which specification is taught, which papers are practised and how many weeks remain. Families who start here get matched faster than families who start with a subject name and a budget.

process.title: A diagnostic against a real paper
process.description: The first session is a timed section of an actual past paper for the right board and tier, marked live on a shared screen. It usually disagrees with the school report, and that disagreement is the useful part. It produces a topic order based on where marks went missing rather than on where the textbook happens to begin.

process.title: Match to a specification, not a subject
process.description: We match on the code your child sits and on the evening hours your family can actually keep on Gulf Standard Time. If nobody in the pool has taught that specification, you are told so before you pay, along with what is available instead. A disclosed gap is cheaper for everyone than a hopeful match.

process.title: A written plan counted backwards
process.description: Sessions are sequenced from the entry deadline and the paper date, not from today. The plan names which paper each block targets, where the school's internal deadlines and mock weeks fall, and how the schedule shifts for Ramadan and Eid. It is written down so it can be argued with.

process.title: Review against marks every half-term
process.description: Progress is read off school assessment marks and timed-paper scores, not off how the sessions felt. Half-termly the plan either continues, changes topic order, or stops. Where a subject cannot realistically be recovered before this series, we say so and discuss the November route instead of selling more hours.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code goes in writing
whyPoints.description: Before the first paid session you receive the board, the code and the tier your tutor is teaching to. It sounds administrative and it is the single biggest predictor of whether the hours convert. A tutor teaching 'physics' rather than 0625 or 4PH1 is teaching a subject your child is not being examined in.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted with the source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a market rate published by the provider named beside it and read in October 2026. We would rather show you the whole range, including the cheaper end, than publish a number with no provenance. Three of the six ranking competitors we studied publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: The regulator named, never claimed
whyPoints.description: We explain what KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE and the Ministry of Education each do, because a parent needs to know. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from any of them and runs no UAE premises. Anyone selling you regulator-approved tutors is selling something that does not exist for private online lessons.

whyPoints.title: Coursework reviewed, never written
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the skill the task assesses, reads a draft and says what does not answer the question, and marks against published criteria. No text is supplied and no piece is taken to completion. In a market where finished Internal Assessments are openly advertised, this boundary is worth stating rather than assuming.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before you pay
whyPoints.description: For some specifications, Computer Science 0478 and first-language Arabic among them, the pool is genuinely thin. You are told that before any money moves, with the realistic alternative named. A gap you know about is a scheduling problem; a gap you discover in week three is a refund argument nobody wanted.

faqs.question: Does IGCSE online tuition in the UAE work the same way in Fujairah as it does in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The lesson does, because it runs over live video and the same specialist pool is reachable from every emirate. What differs is everything around it. A Fujairah school is supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than KHDA, its term dates can differ from Dubai's, and the local pool of IGCSE subject specialists willing to drive to the east coast is effectively empty. That last point is why online delivery is not a compromise there: it is the only version of weekly one-to-one specialist support available at a sensible rate. We confirm your school's board, series and assessment calendar first, whichever emirate it sits in.

faqs.question: Which of the five UAE education authorities has any say over a private online lesson?
faqs.answer: None of them, directly. KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge and the federal Ministry of Education regulate private schools and, in Dubai's case, training institutes with premises. A one-to-one lesson over video between a tutor and a family is not a school. The authority that does reach the tutor is MoHRE, through the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. That distinction is why nobody can honestly advertise regulator-approved private tutors, and why you should treat the phrase as a warning sign rather than a credential.

faqs.question: My son's school will not tell me his syllabus code. Who do I ask, and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer rather than the subject teacher or the front desk; the exams officer holds the centre entry record and the answer is three lines long. It matters because Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 assess different papers in a different order, and the practical arrangement differs too. A tutor given the code teaches the specification your child is examined in. A tutor given only the subject name teaches physics in general, which is interesting and does not reliably move a grade. If the school is slow, the code usually appears on a mock paper's front cover.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor see my child's school report or inspection file?
faqs.answer: Only what you choose to share. The school report, the marked mock script, the assessment calendar and the entry record are all held by the school and released to you, not to us. We ask for them because they shorten the guessing period: a marked script tells a tutor where marks actually went in Paper 2, which a grade cannot. The inspection report is different, because it is public. KHDA and the other emirate authorities publish theirs free, and the phase-level findings for your child's year group are more useful to you than the overall band.

faqs.question: If the lesson happens over video, whose rules govern the tutor?
faqs.answer: The permit rules, not the school ones. u.ae states that the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, and that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit will be subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of any page quoting an amount. Separately, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of pupils at their own school. That restriction follows the teacher onto a video call, so asking for your child's own teacher privately is asking them to breach it.

faqs.question: What is recorded during an online lesson, and who can see it afterwards?
faqs.answer: Ask before you book, and expect a written answer. A reasonable provider tells you which platform is used, whether sessions are recorded, where any recording is stored, how long it is kept and who besides the tutor can open the shared folder. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection is the reason this is a real question rather than a nicety, particularly when the data concerns a minor. A name, year group, board and syllabus code are what a match actually needs. A photograph, a school name and a full set of grades usually are not, and you can decline them.

faqs.question: Can we get online tuition for Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies as well?
faqs.answer: Yes, with two conditions that come from the rules themselves. First, the stream decides the tutor: KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with different language of instruction for each group, so a first-language tutor is wrong for an additional-language pupil. Second, the content is set. KHDA states that using different or additional content without prior MoE permission is strictly prohibited, so support stays on the prescribed material. In an exam term we will usually tell you this is not where the marginal hour belongs.

faqs.question: Why is my daughter taught Arabic in a different class from her Arab classmates?
faqs.answer: Because the two courses are genuinely different and KHDA requires them to be taught apart. Its mandatory-subject guidelines state that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for the first-language group; non-Arab pupils are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language for Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies. It is a curriculum rule, not a judgement about your daughter's ability.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE grades does the UAE Ministry of Education count towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five, on the British track. Gulf Today, reporting the Ministry's clarification in July 2026, states that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor publishes six, which is wrong and expensive to plan around. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae, because no tutoring platform performs or guarantees equivalency.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor replace what my child's school is supposed to be doing?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling you the wrong thing. The school holds the entry, sets the tier, teaches the specification and runs the internal assessment calendar. Tuition works on a narrower territory: what is practised, in what order, with what feedback, between now and the paper. The most useful tutoring sits alongside the school's own scheme of work rather than running a parallel course. If the school is the problem, the inspection report for that subject phase and a conversation with the head of department will do more than buying extra hours.

faqs.question: We move from Ajman to Dubai in Year 10. What does the new school get to decide?
faqs.answer: More than parents expect. The new school holds its own centre number and makes its own entries, so it decides the board, the specification, the tier and the series your child sits, and it may use a different board from the old one in the same subject. It also places your child in the Arabic and Islamic Education stream and moves the school file from Ministry of Education supervision to KHDA. Ask for the entry record in writing within the first fortnight, then compare specifications. The gap between two boards in the same subject is usually a handful of topics, not a year.

faqs.question: What does an hour of online IGCSE support cost in the UAE, and who publishes those figures?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run from about AED 45 an hour at the budget online end, where EdFlik lists from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, where Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150, to AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists, with Bestimate's Dubai table and TutorChase's AED 270 in that band. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Those are the market's numbers, attributed, not an IB Gram price list. Ask what the hour includes and excludes in writing.

faqs.question: Is a screen a problem for the IGCSE science practical component?
faqs.answer: Less than you would think, because of how the component is actually assessed. Many UAE centres enter candidates for the written alternative-to-practical paper, which tests experimental method, apparatus, variables, tables, graphs and sources of error on paper rather than at a bench. That is well suited to a shared screen: the method is planned, the graph is drawn and annotated live, and the mark scheme's expectations are applied to the student's own answer. Where a centre enters the laboratory paper instead, the school runs the practical work and tuition supports the recording and analysis around it. Confirm which paper your child sits first.

faqs.question: My child has nine subjects and two are failing. Where should the money go first?
faqs.answer: Into whichever two subjects the equivalency file and the post-16 plan actually need, which is not always the two with the worst marks. Five IGCSE passes at grade 3 or E carry the Ministry of Education file, Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, so a borderline fifth subject matters more than a sixth strong one. After that, look at which subject the next stage requires: A Level Mathematics and the sciences expect Extended-tier grades behind them. One marked mock script per subject usually settles the argument in an hour, and it is free to obtain.

faqs.question: Nobody in the pool has taught my child's syllabus. What happens then?
faqs.answer: You are told before you pay, which is the part most of this market avoids. Some specifications are genuinely thin on the ground, Computer Science 0478, Further Pure 4PM1 and first-language Arabic among them. In that case we say what is available instead, whether that is a closely related specification taught by a specialist who will read your board's papers first, a shorter diagnostic block rather than a weekly commitment, or nothing at all this series. A disclosed gap is a scheduling problem you can plan around. An undisclosed one becomes a refund argument in week three.

faqs.question: The page is about online tuition, so does anyone visit the house?
faqs.answer: No. Tuition for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and nobody attends a UAE address. Home visiting is a service IB Gram runs only in India. We target the home-tutor phrasing because it is what parents type into Google, and we would rather explain the format honestly than let you discover it after booking. What you gain is the pick of specialists for one narrow paper rather than whoever lives within a twenty-minute drive, plus rescheduling that costs minutes instead of a forfeited session.

igcse-online-tuition.closingHeading: Start with three facts, not with a shortlist
igcse-online-tuition.closingBody: Email your school's exams officer and ask for the board, the syllabus code and the series your child is entered for. Ask the subject teacher for the marked mock script rather than the grade. Then look up your school's inspection report on the regulator's own site and read the phase your child is in, not the headline band. With those in hand, a conversation about online IGCSE tuition takes fifteen minutes instead of three weeks, because the only remaining question is which specialist has the right evening free. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, and the first one is a timed past paper rather than a sales call.

Each profile names the subject, the tier and the boards that tutor has taught. Ask for the syllabus code your child's school entered before you book a paid hour.

intro.heading: The system an IGCSE family in the UAE is already working inside
paragraphs: Searching for an IGCSE online tutor in the UAE usually starts with a mark on a report. It should start one step earlier, with the paperwork. Your child's school is the exam centre. It chooses the board, enters the candidate, sets the tier, submits coursework and practical marks, and issues forecast grades. A tutor hired from outside that building changes none of those things. What an outside tutor can change is how well your child answers the papers the school has already committed them to, and that is a narrower and far more honest promise than most of this market makes.

The second thing worth knowing is that there is no single UAE schools authority. Five separate bodies sit above private schools here. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah's private education authority regulates private education in that emirate, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Which of those names appears on your child's school file changes what you can look up, who approves the fees, and who publishes the inspection report you should read before buying a single hour. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the emirate reaches further into the classroom than a parent in Dubai might assume. None of the five, however, inspects private tuition. That is a separate permit, issued to a person rather than to a provider, and it is the part of the picture most tutoring pages skip.

Then there is the Ministry layer that sits on top of every licensed curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of which international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and the federal rule behind that is simple: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Those subjects occupy real hours in a Year 10 and Year 11 week, they are taught from content the Ministry sets, and they are excluded from the five subjects the equivalency route counts.

This page is written around that context rather than around a sales pitch. It covers who owns which decision in an IGCSE year, what the private tuition permit actually says, where the syllabus code lives, how practical science is assessed when the teaching happens on a screen, what the Ministry of Education equivalency file asks of an IGCSE student, what IGCSE tuition rates in AED look like across this market, and where an hour realistically fits in a UAE school week. Lessons from IB Gram are delivered online, one to one, over live video. No tutor is sent to a UAE address.

igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: An IGCSE online tutor is rarely hired for IGCSE alone. Families arrive from Lower Secondary wanting a head start, or leave for A Level and the Diploma needing a specific grade in a specific subject. These are the four stages the same tutoring plan has to serve, and what each one asks for in the UAE.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The two-year course most British-curriculum schools in the UAE teach, graded by syllabus rather than by school. Each subject carries its own four-digit code, its own paper structure and its own tiering rules. Cambridge runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, with a further series in some regions in February and March. The centre, not the family, decides which series a candidate is entered for, and the entry locks both the subject and the tier months before the paper is sat.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone. It also warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after reading the wrong zone timetable. For a UAE family that single line matters more than any revision tip: the timetable to plan around is the one your child's centre is working from, not the first PDF a search returns.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board widely taught in the Emirates, with its own codes, its own tier names and its own calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and again in November each year. Subject codes look different from Cambridge ones, so a tutor who has taught Mathematics A under code 4MA1 has prepared students for a different paper pattern from one who has only taught the Cambridge equivalent. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, which is why a date should always be checked against the live official timetable.
programmes.countryNote: The November entry matters in the UAE because it gives a resit route that does not cost a full academic year. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A family weighing a retake can therefore see, from published dates, how long the gap between sitting and result actually is.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course begins, ending at Checkpoint tests that Cambridge runs in March, May and October. Nothing here appears on a university file, which is exactly why it is the cheapest place to fix a problem. A Year 9 student who cannot rearrange a formula, write a controlled paragraph or read a results table will meet all three again inside an IGCSE paper, under time pressure, for marks that do count. One hour a week at this stage replaces several in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools this is also the stage where the mandatory Ministry subjects, the chosen second language and the option-block choices all land in the same term. Parents are asked to pick IGCSE options in Year 9 without having seen a single IGCSE paper. A tutor's most useful contribution here is not teaching ahead; it is showing a family what the Extended tier in a given subject actually demands before the option form is signed.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma entry
programmes.description: IGCSE grades are entry currency. UAE sixth forms set subject-specific conditions, and the gap between a grade that clears a threshold and one that clears it comfortably is usually two or three topics deep rather than general ability. Maths and the separate sciences are where the step up bites hardest, because an A Level or Higher Level course assumes fluency with algebraic manipulation that an IGCSE paper will accept in a slower form.
programmes.countryNote: This is where tiering shows its teeth. A Core or Foundation entry can still satisfy the Ministry of Education equivalency minimum while closing off the A Level route in that subject, because the tier caps the reportable grade. Families often discover this in Year 12 admissions rather than in Year 10, when the entry was made. Checking the tier against the intended post-16 route is a ten-minute conversation that saves an expensive year.

igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects UAE families most often ask about, with the Cambridge code and the Pearson equivalent where one exists. Confirm the code on your child's school entry first: two subjects with the same name and different codes are two different papers, and the revision that suits one wastes time on the other.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most requested IGCSE subject in this market. The 2025 Cambridge specification separates a non-calculator paper from a calculator paper at both tiers, which changed what arithmetic fluency is worth. Marks go on unshown method, misread demand words and algebra that collapses under time pressure rather than on unseen topics. Check the current paper numbers for your child's series on the official syllabus.

subjects.name: Additional and International Mathematics (Cambridge 0606 · 0607)
subjects.description: Taken alongside or instead of 0580 by schools preparing students for Higher Level or A Level maths. Content reaches into calculus, trigonometric identities and functions that 0580 never asks for. Students who coast through 0580 Extended often meet their first genuine difficulty here, and it is the single best predictor of how a post-16 maths course will go.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Two theory papers plus a practical component. Electricity and electromagnetism cost UAE students more marks than any other topic, usually because circuit reasoning is being learnt as pattern recognition rather than as cause and effect. Numerical answers lose marks on units and significant figures long after the physics is understood.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic reaction pathways are the three places marks disappear. The practical component rewards a student who can read an unfamiliar method and spot the controlled variable, which is a skill taught on paper as much as at a bench. Equation balancing and state symbols are small, repeatable marks that students keep leaving behind.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: A subject students assume rewards memory and that actually rewards precision. Osmosis, enzyme graphs, transport in plants and genetics crosses carry the marks, and the examiner wants the named structure, the correct direction of movement and the comparative word. Extended-tier questions ask students to apply a known mechanism to an unfamiliar organism.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654 · 0653)
subjects.description: One block of lessons covering all three sciences, common in UAE schools where the timetable cannot carry three separate subjects. Content is narrower than the single sciences, so tutoring here is mostly about not over-reaching: a student revising separate-science material for a co-ordinated paper is spending hours on topics that will not be examined.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 · 0990 · Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading responses carry most of the grade. Students who read widely still lose marks by summarising when the question asks them to analyse effect, or by writing a composition that ignores the specified form and audience. Timing is the quiet killer: the second long answer is where grades are lost.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 · 0511)
subjects.description: A different paper from First Language English, and families regularly buy the wrong tuition for it. Marks sit in note-making, summary writing to a word limit and a speaking component. Accuracy matters less than fitness for purpose: a correct sentence that answers a different question scores nothing.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 · 0455)
subjects.description: Data-response and case-study papers where the application mark depends on using the stimulus rather than reciting a definition. UAE students write confident theory and then score two marks out of six because nothing in the answer refers to the business in front of them. Evaluation marks need a judgement, a reason and a condition.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 · 0417)
subjects.description: The theory paper is where grades are made, not the practical one. Pseudocode tracing, binary and hexadecimal conversion, and the difference between validation and verification come up every series. ICT carries practical tasks assessed in school; Computer Science rewards a student who can trace an algorithm line by line without guessing the output.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460 · 0470)
subjects.description: Both reward structure over volume. Geography needs case-study detail with real place names and figures; History needs source-handling that explains provenance rather than content. Students lose marks writing everything they know about a topic instead of answering the command word in the question stem.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.levels: First language and foreign language routes
subjects.description: Taught in two separate streams in UAE schools, with different expectations and different languages of instruction. Support here has to work from the school's own material, because the content for the mandatory subjects is set centrally. A tutor's job is comprehension, script fluency and written accuracy inside that material, not a parallel syllabus.

igcse-online-tutor.regionsTitle: The seven emirates, and who holds the school file in each
igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: An online lesson does not care which emirate you live in. The paperwork does. The authority above your child's school decides which inspection report you can read, who approved the fee, and which office answers a question about enrolment or records. Here is the position in each emirate, and what it changes for a family buying tuition.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority oversees the quality of private education here. Dubai held 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with UK curriculum pupils the largest group. Depth of provision means a parent can compare several schools' published reports before deciding what tuition is actually for.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. It is the authority almost no tutoring site names. Its professional-ethics rules for school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which changes who a family should accept an offer from.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under the Department of Education and Knowledge, with a smaller British-curriculum cluster than the capital. A narrower local pool is exactly where live online one-to-one lessons stop being a compromise: an Extended-tier Chemistry specialist is reachable on a screen whether or not one lives within driving distance of the house.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The emirate's private education authority regulates private education here and, like Ras Al Khaimah's authority, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That makes it worth asking the school directly which specification it is licensed to deliver before assuming a subject follows the pattern used over the Dubai border.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Families here commonly travel a long way to a British-curriculum school, so the late-afternoon window that a visiting tutor would spend in a car is the window an online session uses for teaching.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, so questions about licensing and records route to the Ministry rather than to an emirate-level regulator. The practical effect for tuition is a thinner local specialist market and more families booking a subject specialist by video from the start.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, and the emirate that returned zero mentions across the competitor pages researched for this market. A family here has the same IGCSE entry deadlines and the same equivalency requirements as one in Dubai, with the smallest pool of local subject tutors in the country.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Private schools here fall under the federal Ministry of Education. The east-coast drive makes an in-home arrangement expensive in time rather than only in dirhams, and a cancelled visit is harder to replace. One-to-one online lessons remove the travel variable from the schedule entirely.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's British-curriculum sector is the deepest in the country, and the schools below are among those UAE families name most often when they ask for IGCSE support. Each publishes an inspection report through the emirate's authority, which is the document to read before deciding which subject actually needs paid hours.

The capital's British-curriculum cluster is smaller than Dubai's and its regulator is a different body with its own inspection framework and its own staff ethics rules. Students we support in this cluster attend schools of this kind; a family should still check the current published report for the specific campus.

Across Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the British and mixed-curriculum provision thins out quickly, and so does the local tutor pool for Extended-tier sciences and Additional Mathematics. This is the cluster where online delivery changes the answer rather than simply offering a second option.

igcse-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways families buy online IGCSE lessons from us, all delivered one to one over live video and scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The right one depends on how far away the series is and whether the problem is a topic, a tier or a habit.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, term-long
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same slot each week through the term. This is the arrangement that fixes a topic gap properly, because the tutor sees the school's homework, the class test and the mock in sequence and can tell the difference between a misconception and a time-management problem. Most families start here with one subject rather than three, and add a second only once the first slot is settled.
bullets: 60 or 90 minutes, same weekday, booked in GST
Written notes after each session naming the next task
Worked around the school's own deadline calendar
One subject at a time until the slot is proven

modes.title: Pre-series intensive block
modes.description: A fixed block of sessions counted backwards from the first paper, used when the entry is already in and the time left is short. The work is paper-shaped rather than topic-shaped: timed questions, mark-scheme language, and the two or three topics where this particular student is losing recoverable marks. Families usually book this for Extended-tier maths and the separate sciences, where the marks are most diagnosable.
bullets: Planned from the centre's own timetable, not a generic calendar
Timed past-paper questions attempted first, discussed second
Focused on recoverable marks, not full syllabus coverage

modes.title: Paired sessions for two students
modes.description: Two students at the same tier in the same subject, taught together over video, splitting the hour between them. It works when both are genuinely at the same point, which is less often than parents hope, and it does not work as a way to cover two different syllabuses at once. Siblings a year apart usually do better in separate shorter slots than in one shared hour.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE online tutor changes, and what your child's school keeps hold of
paragraphs: An IGCSE online tutor teaches; the school decides. The school is the examination centre. It selects the board, enters the candidate, chooses the tier, submits coursework and practical marks, issues forecast grades where a series requires them, and holds the mark book that the next school will ask for. Nothing bought from outside that building moves any of those decisions. Saying so plainly is the first useful thing a tutoring page can do, because a family who understands the division of labour buys the right hours at the right time.

What an outside tutor does change is how well a student answers the paper the school has already entered them for. That is a narrower claim and a more testable one. It covers the misconception the class has moved past, the demand words a student keeps misreading, the method marks being thrown away in working, and the revision plan that currently consists of rereading notes. It also covers the conversations a parent cannot have from the outside: which of nine subjects is actually costing grades, and which is simply uncomfortable.

The table below is the map we send families who ask what tuition will and will not fix. Read the second column first. Where the school owns a decision, the tutor's job is to work to it rather than argue with it, and the family's job is to get the facts out of the school in writing: the board, the subject code, the tier, the series and the internal deadline dates. Half the wasted money in this market is spent preparing for a paper the candidate was never entered for.

sections.heading: Five authorities above UAE private schools, and the one thing none of them inspects
paragraphs: There is no single schools regulator in the Emirates, which is why a page that says KHDA and stops is describing one emirate and implying a country. Dubai's authority oversees the quality of private education there. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah's authority regulates private education there, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The practical difference is reach. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so a question about which specification a subject follows has an official answer rather than a school-level one. In Dubai the authority publishes inspection judgements and, in May 2026, confirmed there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under an economic incentives package. Those are both things a family can verify independently, which is more than can be said for most claims made in this market.

Now the part no competitor page states: none of these five bodies inspects your private tuition. An authority licenses the school. A separate federal permit licenses the individual who teaches privately. Nobody rates the quality of a tutoring hour, and no provider can borrow authority from a regulator that has not assessed it. Any page describing its tutors as approved by a UAE regulator is describing something that does not exist for private tuition. What a parent can do instead is read the school's published report, ask the tutor for their permit position, and judge the teaching themselves from a trial lesson.

sections.heading: Permission to charge: the private tuition permit when the lesson happens on a screen
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the Emirates is a permitted activity, not an informal favour. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The Ministry's own service is listed as the issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with no fees stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow for a parent. The first is that the free permit removes the usual excuse: a tutor who says the paperwork is expensive or slow is describing something other than this permit. The second is that individuals providing private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting a figure is quoting a rumour, and we will not repeat one. Ask instead, politely and early, what the tutor's permit position is.

A separate rule governs who the tutor may teach. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct has been reported as barring service to students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy, but treat the underlying principle as settled: the offer of your child's own subject teacher, privately and for money, is the one to decline. A tuition business with premises and staff is a third category again, requiring an educational services permit for a training institute from the Dubai authority, which is not a credential any online tutor holds.

sections.heading: Find the syllabus code before you buy an hour
paragraphs: Two subjects called IGCSE Physics can be two different papers. Cambridge codes run as four digits, so Physics is 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, Mathematics 0580, Additional Mathematics 0606, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, First Language English 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes look different: Mathematics A is 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1 and English Language A 4EA1. A tutor who has taught one of those has not automatically taught the other, and the revision that suits one wastes hours on the other.

The code also tells you where the marks sit. Paper counts, calculator rules and the route for practical assessment differ between boards and between tiers, and specifications change: the 2025 Cambridge Mathematics specification separated a non-calculator paper from a calculator paper, which altered what arithmetic fluency is worth in a Year 11 revision plan. Read the current specification for your child's series rather than a summary of an older one, and check the paper numbers against the entry rather than against a sibling's experience two years earlier.

Then there is the timetable. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that using the correct version of the timetable for the zone is essential, and warns it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them. So the sequence before any paid hour is: ask the school for the board, the code, the tier and the series; ask which zone the centre sits in; then read the official timetable from the board's own site. Those four answers shape every plan built after them.

sections.heading: Practicals, the alternative to practical, and the part of IGCSE science that stays in the school lab
paragraphs: This is the honest limit of online science tuition, and it deserves a straight answer. Cambridge science syllabuses assess practical skills either through a practical test or through a written alternative to practical paper, and the centre decides which route its candidates take. A tutor on a screen cannot run a titration for your child, cannot supervise a practical test and cannot stand in for the school's laboratory. Any page implying otherwise is selling something it cannot deliver.

What live online lessons can do is almost everything the paper actually rewards. Both the practical test and the alternative to practical paper are marked on written reasoning: reading an unfamiliar method, identifying the independent and controlled variables, spotting the source of error, completing a results table with consistent significant figures, plotting and interpreting a graph, and describing an improvement that would genuinely reduce uncertainty. Those are taught with a shared screen, a past-paper method and a mark scheme in front of both people, and they are where students lose most of the available marks.

The division of labour is therefore clear. The school provides the bench, the apparatus and the supervision. The tutor provides the reasoning, the vocabulary the mark scheme rewards and the practice at interpreting results the student did not generate. Confirm which practical route your child's centre uses before booking, because preparing for the written alternative when the centre enters candidates for the practical test, or the reverse, wastes a term of effort.

sections.heading: Dropping a subject to free up revision time, and what the Ministry actually counts
paragraphs: Every Year 11 reaches a week where somebody suggests dropping a subject to make room. Before that conversation, a family should know what the Ministry of Education equivalency route counts. For the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

Read that twice before dropping anything, because two traps sit inside it. The first is the count: one ranking UAE tutoring page states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is more than the sourced requirement, and a family planning around the wrong number drops the wrong subject. The second is the exclusion: if Arabic and Islamic Education do not count towards the five, then a student holding exactly five other subjects has no margin at all, and losing one of them to a timetable clash or a withdrawn entry is a problem that surfaces years later at a UAE university admissions desk.

The reassuring part is that the minimum grade is low. A grade no lower than E or 3 means a Core or Foundation tier entry can still satisfy the equivalency count, even though the same tier caps the grade a student can report and will close off an A Level route in that subject. So the tier decision and the equivalency decision pull in different directions, and they need to be made together rather than in separate meetings. For the American track, the published requirements are a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with at least 450 in SAT Math. For the IB Diploma no points threshold appears in that source, so we publish none: verify on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority before relying on any figure. Equivalency is a process the family and the authority complete, not something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies: the content rule that binds any outside tutor
paragraphs: These subjects run beside the IGCSE timetable rather than inside it, and they are not optional. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and the KHDA mandatory subjects guidance required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The federal position behind it is that private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies and adhere to the Ministry's general regulations, whichever curriculum they are licensed for.

The organisation of those lessons is prescribed in detail, which is why outside support here works differently from maths tuition. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for social studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length if the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

The rule that constrains tutoring most is the content one: for these subjects, using any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited. An outside tutor therefore cannot bring a parallel syllabus, a preferred textbook or imported worksheets into Arabic, Islamic Education or social studies. What is legitimately available is comprehension, script fluency, vocabulary, written accuracy and exam technique worked through the school's own material. Schools are also required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, which is a school-level requirement a parent can ask about directly, and which no private tutor can claim as a personal credential.

sections.heading: What an online IGCSE hour costs across the UAE market
paragraphs: Most pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote a currency UAE families do not transact in. Here are the bands as published by providers and rate trackers in this market, read in October 2026. These are market figures, not IB Gram's price list: IGCSE tuition rates in AED run from roughly 45 an hour at the budget online end, through 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, 200 to 450 and above for an exam-year specialist, 180 to 500 for an in-home visit once travel is priced in, and 500 to 650 and above at the premium end. Monthly packages seen in this market include an online plan around AED 799 for eight sessions and in-home plans between AED 1,599 and AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits.

What moves a number inside those bands is not mystique. It is scarcity of the exact match, the month you start, and whether travel is being paid for. An Extended-tier Additional Mathematics tutor who has taught 0606 to the current specification is scarcer than a general maths tutor, and scarcity prices itself. Six weeks before a series, every specialist's evening slots are already committed, so the same hour costs more and there is less of it. Travel is the other big variable, and it buys nothing academic: an in-home rate includes a journey across a congested city, priced into an hourly figure.

Put tuition next to the fee it sits beside. Dubai's authority confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, so the school bill is a known quantity for the year and the tuition decision can be made against it rather than guessed at. A rate tracker's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session in this market run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. We publish a trial lesson and a consultation rather than a price list, and we do not quote a figure we cannot attribute.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against live one-to-one online, under UAE conditions
paragraphs: The in-home option is real and plenty of UAE families buy it. It is not what IB Gram sells here. Our lessons are delivered one to one over live video, and home visits are part of our service in India only. That is the same position stated on every country page on this site, and stating it before a parent asks is better than discovering it after a booking. The argument for online delivery in this market, though, does not rest on policy. It rests on who your child can actually be taught by.

A visiting tutor is drawn from the pool living within a reasonable drive. In Dubai, where UK curriculum pupils are 37 per cent of a 387,441-student private sector, that pool is deep for Year 9 maths and thin for Extended-tier Chemistry at 7pm on a Tuesday. In Al Ain, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Umm Al Quwain or Fujairah it is thin for almost everything above Core tier. Online delivery replaces a geographic pool with a subject pool: the question stops being who is nearby and becomes who has taught 0620 Extended to the current specification.

The operational differences are just as concrete. A visiting session is one cancellation away from a lost week, because a replacement has to live nearby too. An online slot can move to another evening or another tutor in the same subject. Materials behave differently as well: a past-paper question and its mark scheme sit on a shared screen where both people annotate the same lines, and the session notes arrive in writing afterwards. A family that travels in the summer, or between emirates mid-year, keeps the same tutor and the same slot rather than starting a search again.

sections.heading: Where an online hour actually fits in a UAE school week
paragraphs: The UAE school week runs Monday to Friday with a Saturday and Sunday weekend, and most private schools finish in the middle of the afternoon. That shape decides when tuition is possible far more than any preference does. A Year 11 student with nine subjects, mandatory Ministry subjects on the timetable and homework from both is not short of willingness in the evening; they are short of a usable hour. Choosing the slot badly is the most common reason a sensible tuition plan quietly stops working by week four.

Schools build their own timetables in short units, and the KHDA mandatory subjects guidance calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit while advising that a mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. That is a useful reference point for tuition too: a 60-minute online session is roughly one and a half school lessons of concentration from a tired fourteen-year-old, and 90 minutes is only worth booking when the student is being set timed questions rather than listening. Two shorter sessions in a week usually beat one long one in Year 10, and the reverse becomes true during a pre-series block.

Then there are the fixed points in a UAE calendar: prayer times, the school-run window, the shortened Ramadan school day, and the Eid break landing inside a revision term. A sensible plan moves sessions to post-Iftar slots through Ramadan rather than pretending the month is normal, pauses during study leave if the school's own plan needs the time, and avoids booking anything in the sixty minutes after a long commute home. sections.heading: Coursework, past papers and the line a paid tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Some pages in this market sell finished assessed work. One advertises completed internal assessments at a published price. It is worth being blunt about what that is: a breach of academic honesty rules that puts the student's entry at risk, not a shortcut. A paid tutor teaches, questions, models technique and gives feedback on what the student has produced themselves. A tutor who hands over sentences for a piece the school will submit has made the student's result unsafe and the school's declaration false.

In practice the line is easy to hold and easy to recognise. Legitimate support looks like this: explaining what a command word is asking for, teaching the structure a mark scheme rewards, reading a student's own draft and asking the questions a marker would ask, and practising the skill on a different task so the student can apply it alone. Illegitimate support looks like a return of edited text the student could not have produced, a supplied investigation plan, or a correction pass that leaves no trace of the student's own reasoning. The school submits coursework and practical marks and the board moderates them, so a mark that does not match the candidate's own papers invites scrutiny.

Materials carry a second rule. Board syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are copyright documents, and we do not reproduce them or supply them as downloads. We reference them, cite the official page and link out to cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, and we work from them on a shared screen during a lesson, which is what teaching from them actually requires. If a provider offers a drive full of papers for a fee, that tells a parent something about how it treats other rules too.

process.title: Send us the code, the tier and the series
process.description: Four facts start everything: the board, the four-digit or alphanumeric syllabus code, the tier your child is entered at, and which series the centre is entering. A recent school report and the most recent assessment paper help more than a description of the problem. If you do not have the code, ask the school in writing; it is the single most useful sentence you will get from them this term.

process.title: A trial lesson, with the conditions stated
process.description: One trial lesson per student, booked by a parent, with no card details taken to arrange it. It is a diagnostic rather than a sample lecture: the tutor sets work, watches how the student reasons through it, and tells you afterwards what the actual gap is. You get that assessment in writing whether or not you book another hour.

process.title: Match by subject, tier and board, then fix the slot
process.description: We match on who has taught that specification, not on who lives closest to you. Once a tutor is agreed, the weekly slot is set in Gulf Standard Time around the school day, the commute and the Ministry subjects already on the timetable. The slot matters as much as the tutor; a brilliant hour nobody can attend is worth nothing.

process.title: Teach, then report in writing
process.description: After each session you receive notes naming what was covered, what the student did unaided, what was set before next week, and where the marks are currently going. Those notes are deliberately plain, so you can compare them with the school's own report rather than take our word for progress.

process.title: If no specialist is free, we say so
process.description: Some subject and tier combinations are genuinely scarce, particularly Additional Mathematics, Extended-tier sciences and first-language Arabic in an exam term. Where no suitable tutor has availability we tell you that and give an honest wait, rather than placing a general tutor in a specialist slot and hoping. A family can plan around a no; they cannot plan around a wrong match.

whyPoints.title: The subject pool, not the driving radius
whyPoints.description: Live online delivery means the question is who has taught your child's specification at that tier, not who happens to live nearby. For a family in Al Ain, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah, Umm Al Quwain or Fujairah looking for Extended-tier sciences, that difference decides whether a specialist is available at all.

whyPoints.title: The regulatory picture, named properly
whyPoints.description: Five authorities regulate UAE private schools and a separate federal permit covers private tutors. We name which is which, explain what each one does, and point to the official source. We claim no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any of them, because none exists for private tuition.

whyPoints.title: Numbers with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a market band published by a provider or a rate tracker and read in October 2026, attributed as such. We publish no satisfaction percentage, no score average and no self-awarded rating, because we cannot show you the data behind one.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor here teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced. We do not supply text for coursework, we do not hand over finished assessed pieces, and we do not distribute copyright papers or mark schemes as downloads. That line protects your child's entry, which is the point of it.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what tuition cannot move
whyPoints.description: The school owns the board, the entry, the tier, the coursework submission and the laboratory. We say so on the page rather than in a conversation after you have paid. A tuition plan built on that division of labour targets the marks that are actually recoverable.

whyPoints.description: One-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with written notes after each session. No tutor is sent to a UAE address, and nobody will discover that at the booking stage. Home visits are part of what we do in India, and nowhere else.

faqs.question: Who actually enters my child for the IGCSE papers, the school or the tutor?
faqs.answer: The school. Your child's school is the examination centre: it makes the entry, chooses the subject code, sets the tier and submits coursework and practical marks. A tutor hired from outside has no role in any of that and cannot change an entry once the final deadline has passed. This is why the first thing we ask a UAE family for is the board, the code, the tier and the series. If a provider offers to handle entries for a candidate who is enrolled at a school, ask exactly what they mean, because the centre holds that responsibility.

faqs.question: Does the authority that licenses our school change anything about online tuition?
faqs.answer: Not for the lesson itself, but it changes what you can verify. Dubai's authority oversees private education quality there, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah have their own authorities that also approve curricula and assessment methods, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Which one holds your school's file decides which inspection report you can read and who answers an official question. None of them inspects private tuition, so no tutoring provider can borrow their authority.

faqs.question: Does anyone inspect a tutoring company the way a school is inspected?
faqs.answer: No. School inspection and private tuition are separate things in the Emirates. An emirate authority licenses and inspects the school. A federal permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, licenses the individual who teaches privately. Nobody awards a quality rating to a tutoring hour, which is why any claim to be an approved or accredited tutor should be read sceptically and why we make no such claim. A tuition business with premises and staff in Dubai needs an educational services permit for a training institute, which is a different thing again and not a credential an online tutor holds.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor teaching my child from outside the UAE still need the private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: The permit is a UAE work permit, issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and granted free of charge for two years, and it applies to individuals providing private tutoring in the country. Where a tutor is based changes which rules reach them, so the useful question for a parent is simply: where is this tutor, who employs them, and what is their permit position? Ask it before the first paid hour. Anyone who cannot answer plainly is telling you something. We say where a tutor is based rather than hiding it behind an international phone number.

faqs.question: Can my child be tutored privately by a teacher who works at another UAE school?
faqs.answer: Teachers registered in government or private schools are among the categories eligible to apply for the MoHRE private tuition work permit, so a schoolteacher tutoring privately is a recognised arrangement rather than an irregular one. The restriction concerns their own students. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules have been reported as prohibiting school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct has been reported as barring service to students affiliated with that school. Treat the detail as press-reported, check the current policy, and decline the offer of your own child's subject teacher.

faqs.question: What should I ask a provider before paying for a first online IGCSE hour?
faqs.answer: Six questions. Which board and syllabus code has this tutor actually taught, and at which tier? Where is the tutor based and what is their permit position? What happens in the trial lesson and what conditions attach to it? What do I receive in writing after each session? What is the policy if a session is missed or the connection drops? And what will you not do, specifically around coursework? The answers take five minutes to collect and they sort this market faster than any review page will.

faqs.question: Is dropping an IGCSE subject in Year 11 a problem for the Ministry's equivalency count?
faqs.answer: It can be. The British track requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A student carrying exactly five other subjects therefore has no margin, and dropping one leaves the file short. One ranking UAE page states six subjects are required, which is more than the sourced requirement, so check the number before planning around it. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority before any subject is withdrawn.

faqs.question: Does a Core or Foundation tier entry still count towards UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the published requirement, yes: the British track asks for a grade no lower than E or grade 3, which sits below the ceiling a Core or Foundation entry imposes. The complication is elsewhere. A lower tier caps the grade that can be reported, and that cap is what closes off an A Level or Higher Level route in the same subject. So a tier can satisfy the Ministry's minimum and still end a post-16 plan. Those two decisions should be made in the same conversation, before the final entry deadline, not in separate meetings a year apart.

faqs.question: Which of the Cambridge science papers can an online tutor genuinely prepare my child for?
faqs.answer: All of the written reasoning, and none of the bench work. Cambridge sciences assess practical skills through either a practical test or a written alternative to practical paper, and the centre chooses which route its candidates take. Both routes award marks for reading an unfamiliar method, identifying variables, completing results tables consistently, plotting and interpreting graphs and explaining sources of error. Those are taught well on a shared screen with a past-paper method in front of both people. The apparatus, the laboratory and the supervision stay with the school. Confirm which route your centre uses before booking anything.

faqs.question: Where do the three Ministry subjects fit when my daughter already has nine IGCSEs?
faqs.answer: They sit on the timetable beside the IGCSE courses, not instead of them. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. So the honest answer is that a Year 11 week is already full before tuition is added. That is an argument for one subject at a time, a slot chosen around the real timetable, and for not buying hours in a subject where the marks are not actually being lost.

faqs.question: May an outside tutor bring their own worksheets into Arabic or Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: No, and this one is explicit. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, so a parallel syllabus or an imported textbook is not available to any outside tutor. Schools must also run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in these subjects, with prescribed languages of instruction, and must ensure their Arabic and Islamic Education teachers hold appropriate KHDA approval. Legitimate outside support works through the school's own material on comprehension, script fluency, vocabulary and written accuracy.

faqs.question: What is the honest price range for an online IGCSE hour in this market?
faqs.answer: Market bands published by UAE providers and rate trackers in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for an exam-year specialist, with a premium end reaching AED 500 to 650 and above. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 500 because travel is priced into the hour. Those are other people's published figures, attributed as such, not our price list. What moves a number is scarcity of the exact subject and tier, and how close the series is.

faqs.question: My son writes all his maths working by hand. How does that work over video?
faqs.answer: It works the way the paper does, as long as the setup is right. Most students write on paper and hold it to the camera, or work on a tablet with a stylus so the tutor sees each line appear in real time. The second is better for maths and sciences, because method marks are lost in the steps rather than in the answer, and a tutor needs to see the step where the reasoning turned. A shared screen carries the question and the mark scheme. What matters is that the student writes during the lesson rather than watching someone else write.

faqs.question: My school's exam timetable differs from the one I found online. Which should we plan around?
faqs.answer: Your centre's version. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that using the correct timetable version for the zone is essential, and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of a series and revises them before the final version. So ask the school which zone the centre sits in, then read the official timetable from the board's own site. A revision block counted backwards from the wrong date is a wasted term.

faqs.question: We are moving from Dubai to Ras Al Khaimah in January. Does the tuition plan change?
faqs.answer: The tutor and the slot do not need to change at all, which is one practical advantage of online delivery during a move. What does change is the paperwork around the child: the new school is regulated by a different authority, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, which also approves curricula and assessment methods, and the new school becomes the examination centre with its own series and possibly its own zone timetable. Ask the receiving school in writing which board and codes it enters, and whether tier entries already made can be carried across.

faqs.question: My daughter is in Year 9 and starts IGCSE next year. Is it too early for a tutor?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest point to buy an hour, not the earliest. Nothing in Year 9 appears on a university file, so a weakness can be fixed without a grade attached to it. Cambridge runs Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which gives a useful external reference point. The other reason to look now is the option form: families choose IGCSE subjects and sometimes tiers in Year 9 without having seen a single IGCSE paper, and one honest session about what Extended tier demands in a subject is worth more than a term of catching up later.

faqs.question: How late in the evening can an online session start without damaging the next school day?
faqs.answer: For most UAE families the last useful start is around 20:00, and only in an exam term. The school week here runs Monday to Friday with an early-to-mid-afternoon finish, so the realistic windows are straight after school, early evening and one late slot for timed paper practice. A 90-minute session after a long commute produces attendance rather than learning. During Ramadan, moving the slot after Iftar works better than squeezing it into a shortened school day, and pausing through study leave is usually a better decision than adding hours to it.

igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the code, not the sales call
igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the four facts: the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series your child's school has entered. With those in hand, any tutoring conversation in the UAE becomes checkable, and most of this market's vagueness stops working. Send them to us with a recent assessment paper and we will tell you honestly whether an online IGCSE tutor is the right purchase, which subject should come first, and what we think the marks are actually going on. Lessons are one to one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with written notes after each session and a trial lesson before you commit.
