Each one works from a named syllabus code rather than a general sense of the subject, and each plans the term around the series date your child's exams officer has confirmed, not around a generic school year.

intro.heading: The IGCSE year is a sequence of lock dates, and most families arrive after the first one
paragraphs: Search for an IGCSE private tutor in the UAE and you will be shown hourly rates, subject lists and photographs of smiling teenagers. Almost none of those pages mention a date. That is the part that matters. An IGCSE grade is produced inside a fixed structure of deadlines set by Cambridge International and Pearson, administered by your child's school, and largely invisible to parents until something has already closed. Final entries go in months before the first paper. The decision about whether your child sits the Core or the Extended tier goes in on the same form. A forecast grade is submitted weeks before the exam window opens. None of that is negotiable in April.

This page is organised around that calendar rather than around our service. It counts backwards from the first paper to the decisions that have to be made before it, and it says which of them a tutor can genuinely influence and which are already settled. The honest answer is that tuition bought eighteen months out does different work from tuition bought at nine weeks, and the second kind costs more per unit of grade. A family who understands the sequence buys fewer hours and gets more from them.

Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the Emirates; home visits are a service offered only in India, and that is stated the same way on every country page on this site. For an IGCSE subject that turns out to be the right constraint rather than a compromise. A Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 teacher or a Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 specialist does not live within a thirty-minute drive of every community in the UAE, and a fixed exam date is a bad moment to discover that.

What follows is specific. There are the published key dates for a Cambridge series alongside Pearson's November series, so you can see how far ahead an entry deadline sits. There is the Core and Extended tier comparison with the grade ceilings attached. There is the five-subject Ministry of Education equivalency count, which reaches back into subject choices made in Year 9. There are market rates in AED with their sources, because a page that tells you what things cost is more useful than one that asks you to enquire. Every figure carries where it came from, and anything we could not verify from a primary source is marked as unverified rather than smoothed over.

One more thing before the detail. The question parents ask on the phone is almost never the question that decides the grade. Families ask what the hourly rate is; the answer that changes the outcome is which series the child is entered for and how many teaching weeks remain inside it. Two students at the same school, in the same subject, with the same tutor and the same rate, finish a long way apart because one started in October of Year 10 and the other in March of Year 11. The rate was identical. The calendar was not.
bullets: Final entries, and with them the tier, close months before the first paper is sat
Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with different timetables

igcse-private-tutor.programmesIntro: Four stages matter to a UAE family looking at IGCSE. The two boards are not interchangeable, the years before Year 10 decide how much content has to be rebuilt later, and the post-16 route determines which tier and which subjects were the right ones to enter two years earlier.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The larger of the two boards in UAE schools. Subjects carry four-digit codes: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, First Language English 0500. Most subjects are tiered, with a Core route and an Extended route sitting on different papers. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable.
programmes.countryNote: A UAE centre sits the June and November series. Cambridge publishes a full set of key dates for each series, and its exams officers guide is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Ask your school's exams officer which zone your centre is in and keep that timetable.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The second board in UAE British-curriculum schools, with codes in a different format: Mathematics A 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1, Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1. Tiering is narrower than Cambridge: Mathematics A is offered at Foundation and Higher, while most other subjects are untiered. Practical skill is assessed inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical test.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE exams in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live timetable on qualifications.pearson.com rather than a date copied onto a tutoring page.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The years before IGCSE, where the gap that later looks like a Year 11 problem is usually created. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October and are diagnostic rather than certificated. A weak algebra foundation in Year 8 is cheap to repair; the same weakness surfacing in a Year 11 mock costs several times as many hours because it has to be fixed while new content is still arriving.
programmes.countryNote: This is also when the subject list that the Ministry of Education will later count is effectively shaped. A child who drops a science or a second language in Year 9 to lighten the load can find the equivalency file short of five countable subjects two years later. UAE families moving between curricula mid-key-stage should check the option-block structure at the receiving school before the transfer, not after.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: A Level and IB Diploma entry
programmes.description: Post-16 entry criteria are where a tier decision made two years earlier becomes visible. A Level and IB Diploma courses in UAE schools typically ask for grades above the ceiling available on the Cambridge Core tier in the relevant subject, and Higher Level sciences and Mathematics usually ask for more than a bare pass. The exact threshold is the school's to set and varies between schools in the same emirate.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE university applications, grades also feed the Ministry of Education equivalency file. The published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, together with one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae before relying on it; the rules are restated periodically.

igcse-private-tutor.subjectsIntro: Subjects are listed with both boards' codes, because the code is what determines which past papers are useful. A tutor who teaches generic physics to a 4PH1 candidate is teaching the wrong paper structure, and the student finds that out in the exam hall rather than in the lesson.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject where the tier decision bites hardest. Extended and Higher carry the algebra, trigonometry and functions content that post-16 courses assume. Marks are lost most often on multi-step problems where method marks exist but no working is shown, and on bearings, similar shapes and compound interest questions that look routine and are not.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics (Cambridge 0606 · Pearson 4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main maths qualification by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. Calculus arrives early, and the step up in algebraic fluency is steep. This is one of the subjects where a UAE family searching locally for a specialist most often finds nobody within driving distance.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism are where marks disappear, usually because circuit reasoning is memorised rather than understood. The practical component differs by board: Cambridge centres offer either a practical test or the written alternative to practical paper, while Pearson assesses practical skill inside the written papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry account for a disproportionate share of lost marks, followed by organic chemistry naming and the precise wording expected for observations. Examiner-style phrasing matters here: a correct idea expressed loosely scores nothing, and that is a fixable, teachable gap.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Students who revise by rereading retain little, and the extended-response questions reward structured recall with named examples. Experimental design questions on variables and controls are regularly answered in general terms and marked down for it.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654 · Cambridge 0653)
subjects.description: The double and single award routes taken where a school's option blocks will not hold three separate sciences. Content is drawn from all three disciplines, which means a tutor has to be comfortable across them rather than a single-subject specialist, and the syllabus boundaries differ from the separate-science versions.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 and 0990 · Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.levels: Single tier, with coursework or exam routes
subjects.description: Reading questions are marked on inference and selection, not on quantity. Directed writing fails on register and audience more often than on grammar. Where a centre uses a coursework portfolio route, the drafting process is the student's own work and a tutor's role is questions and feedback on it.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Taken by a large share of UAE students whose schooling has changed language partway through. The speaking component is separately assessed and is the part most often left unpractised until the final weeks. Timed summary-writing technique is the fastest available improvement in this subject.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 and 0450 · Pearson 4EC1 and 4BS1)
subjects.description: Both subjects reward applied analysis using the data in front of the student and penalise rehearsed definitions. Diagram accuracy in Economics, including correctly labelled axes and shifted curves, is a routine source of lost marks. Case-study questions need the case, not a textbook answer.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 and 0417)
subjects.description: Algorithm and pseudocode questions separate grades, and trace tables are the single most useful technique to drill. The theory papers reward precise terminology about data representation and networks, where approximate wording scores nothing. Practical ICT components are centre-assessed and run to the school's own internal deadlines.

subjects.name: Arabic (Cambridge 0508 First Language · Cambridge 0544 Foreign Language)
subjects.description: Studied both as an IGCSE subject and as a mandatory school subject under emirate regulation, which are not the same requirement. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in first-language Arabic, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction, so tutoring has to match the stream the child is actually in.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460 and 0470)
subjects.levels: Single tier, with coursework or alternative paper routes
subjects.description: Both carry a route choice at centre level: a coursework component or a written alternative to coursework paper. Source-based questions in History are marked on use of the source rather than on background knowledge, and Geography case studies need named places, figures and dates to reach the top band.

igcse-private-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in the UAE changes which boards are available nearby, how many IGCSE centres there are to choose between, and in a few cases whether a private-candidate entry is the realistic route. Delivery is identical everywhere: live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest concentration of IGCSE centres in the country, regulated by KHDA, which publishes its inspection reports. With 227 private schools in 2024-25 and a UK curriculum covering 37 per cent of private-school enrolment, most Dubai families have both boards available within a few communities and a real choice of centre.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Both IGCSE boards are represented across the island, Khalifa City and the Raha corridor. ADEK's professional-ethics rules restrict school staff from taking paid private work with their own pupils, which narrows the local pool more than parents expect.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller set of British-curriculum centres than the capital. Families in Al Ain more often find that a specific subject at Extended tier is not taught by anyone locally available, which is the situation online one-to-one tuition was built for rather than a second-best alternative.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That approval power means a Sharjah school's IGCSE option blocks can legitimately differ from a Dubai school's, so check the option list before assuming a subject is available.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here sit under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority. There are fewer IGCSE centres, and families commuting into Sharjah or Dubai for school add travel time to every weekday evening, which is exactly the hour an in-home tutor would need.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which also approves curricula and fees. The British-curriculum provision is concentrated in a handful of schools, so a tier change or a subject swap can mean a conversation about a private-candidate entry at a centre further south.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The east-coast location makes any in-home arrangement a scheduling problem before it is a teaching one, and a late-afternoon slot that holds every week is worth more to a Year 11 revision plan than a nominally cheaper local rate.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the federal Ministry of Education, and the smallest market for British-curriculum provision in the country. Families here are the clearest case for subject specialists reached by video: the alternative is not a cheaper tutor, it is no tutor in that subject at that tier.

schoolClusters.note: British-curriculum schools across Dubai run IGCSE through Years 10 and 11, with option blocks and board choices set school by school. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four of them UK curriculum, creating 16,846 new places. Students we support attend schools across this group; none of them is a partner or client of IB Gram.

ADEK-regulated British-curriculum schools in the capital and Al Ain run both IGCSE boards. Entry deadlines, forecast-grade submission and mock timetables are set centre by centre here as everywhere, so two children in neighbouring communities can be working to different internal dates in the same series.

Provision thins out north of Dubai, and option blocks are narrower. Where a subject at Extended tier is not offered locally, the practical question becomes whether another centre will accept a private candidate and by which deadline, which is a question for the exams officer rather than for a tutor.

igcse-private-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways families use an IGCSE private tutor, and they suit different points in the calendar. A weekly subject slot does a different job from a block bought at nine weeks, and the second is more expensive per grade point for reasons that have nothing to do with the hourly rate.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the course
modes.description: One subject, one fixed slot, running from the start of Year 10 or early Year 11. Content is covered as the school covers it, so gaps get caught in the week they appear rather than in a January mock. This is the cheapest route to the same grade because nothing has to be rebuilt, and the tier decision can be made on evidence instead of on nerves.
bullets: A slot that holds every week, on Gulf Standard Time
Pace matched to the school's scheme of work and internal deadlines
Tier evidence accumulating before the final entry form
Past papers introduced tier-matched, not generically

modes.title: A revision block counted backwards from the series
modes.description: A defined number of hours between a mock result and the exam window, planned paper by paper rather than topic by topic. The block starts from the actual timetable for your child's zone or series, works out how many sessions fit, and allocates them to components by marks available rather than by what feels weakest.
bullets: Built from the live official timetable for the series, not an assumed date
Allocated by paper weighting and mark availability
Timed-condition practice with marking against published criteria
Written session notes after each lesson so the plan stays visible

modes.title: Coursework and portfolio support
modes.description: For the IGCSE subjects with a centre-assessed component, a tutor's role is teaching, questioning and feedback on work the student has produced. That means reading a draft and asking what the evidence supports, not supplying sentences. The student's own work is the only thing that can be submitted, and a tutor who offers otherwise is creating a malpractice risk for your child.
bullets: Feedback on the student's own drafts, against the published criteria
Research and structure method taught, not content supplied
The school's internal deadlines treated as the real deadlines
Nothing written, completed or edited to submission on the student's behalf

sections.heading: What a UAE parent is actually asking for when they search this
paragraphs: An IGCSE private tutor in the UAE is a subject teacher working one-to-one with a Year 10 or Year 11 student against a board-set exam series. The useful version of that job starts with three facts: which board your child's centre has entered them with, which series they sit, and which tier they are entered at. Without those three the hourly rate is meaningless, because the same hour spent on the wrong tier's past papers or the wrong board's paper structure produces nothing.

Most families arrive at the search after a report, a mock result or a parents' evening. The question underneath is usually not about teaching method. It is whether there is still time, what it will cost, and whether the thing that went wrong is fixable before the papers. Those are answerable questions and this page answers them in order, starting with the calendar, because the calendar determines what the honest answer is. At twenty months out almost everything is recoverable. At nine weeks the recoverable set is smaller, more specific and worth knowing precisely.

The delivery answer comes first so nothing later reads as a surprise. Online IGCSE tuition with IB Gram means live one-to-one video lessons, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen and written notes after each session. IB Gram does not operate home visits in the Emirates. That is not a limitation disguised as a feature: it is what makes a Pearson Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 teacher reachable from Fujairah and a Cambridge 0654 specialist reachable from Al Ain, which no local pool in those emirates can promise.

sections.heading: Two series a year, and the entry deadline that sits months before the paper
paragraphs: Both IGCSE boards run two main series a year. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. UAE centres sit the June and November series. The table below uses a Cambridge series whose full key dates have been published alongside Pearson's November 2026 series, because the point is the shape of the gap between the deadline and the paper, and that shape repeats every year.

Look at the distance between the first row and the second. Final entries for that Cambridge series closed on 27 November 2026 for an exam period beginning 3 February 2027: a gap of more than two months, and your school's internal cut-off will have been weeks earlier again. Pearson's November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with entries closing well ahead of it. Everything a family can decide, including the tier, the subject list and whether to add a subject as a private candidate, has to happen before that first row, not after it.

The zone question is the one that catches families who print a timetable from the internet. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and its exams officers guide states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam when the wrong version was used. Ask your exams officer which zone your centre sits in, get the IGCSE exam zone timetable for that zone, and build the IGCSE revision plan from it rather than from a date on a tutoring site.

sections.heading: The Core and Extended tier decision, and the date it stops being reversible
paragraphs: Most Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered. A Core entry and an Extended entry cover different content and sit different papers, and they do not reach the same grades. Pearson tiers far fewer subjects, chiefly Mathematics A 4MA1 at Foundation and Higher. Parents are rarely told that the tier sits on the same entry form as the subject, which means it locks on the final entry date and not at the point someone finally raises it in a Year 11 progress meeting.

The grade ranges in the table are the ones published in the Cambridge syllabus documents; confirm your child's specific subject and reporting scale on cambridgeinternational.org, since syllabuses report on either the A*-G scale or the 9-1 scale depending on the version a centre offers. The consequence is blunt. A Core entry has a ceiling. If a post-16 course your child wants asks for a grade above that ceiling, the tier decision made on an entry form in Year 11 has already answered the sixth-form question, and no amount of tuition after the deadline changes it.

A tutor's useful contribution to this decision is evidence rather than opinion. Four or five pieces of timed, tier-matched work marked against published criteria tell you more than a mock grade does, because they show whether the student is failing to reach the supplement content or simply losing marks to technique across both tiers. That evidence has to exist before the entry form, which means the work has to start in the autumn term. Collected in February, it is a description of a decision that has already been made for you.

sections.heading: Year 10 is where Year 11's workload is quietly decided
paragraphs: Year 10 has no external exams, and that is the problem. Two years of content sit across Years 10 and 11, and a student who finishes Year 10 with soft foundations in algebra, moles or source analysis spends Year 11 learning new material while simultaneously repairing old material. Every hour spent on repair is an hour not spent on exam technique, and exam technique is where the final grades are made. The arithmetic is unforgiving: a gap that takes four hours to close in October of Year 10 regularly takes fifteen in February of Year 11, because by then it has to be closed around mocks, coursework deadlines and the mandatory school subjects.

The second thing Year 10 settles is the subject count. Ministry of Education equivalency counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among them. A student who trims their option blocks for workload reasons in Year 9 or Year 10 can reach Year 12 with four countable subjects and a problem nobody noticed. That is a conversation to have with the school's head of key stage four, in Year 10, with the equivalency rule in front of you.

For tuition, Year 10 is the cheap year. One weekly session in the single subject that is drifting, running from October, costs less in total than a block bought in the spring of Year 11 and does more, because it changes what the student knows rather than how they revise. It also produces the tier evidence described above, as a by-product, in time for the entry form. Families who book in Year 10 generally buy fewer hours overall than families who book at nine weeks, which is the opposite of what the search volume on panic queries would suggest.

sections.heading: Five subjects, not six: the ministry count that reaches back into Year 9
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency is the process that makes a foreign school certificate usable for UAE university admission, and it is the deadline nobody counts backwards from. The published clarification of the requirements for British-curriculum students is specific: a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details in that rule matter more than the rest. The first is that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which surprises families who assumed the mandatory school subjects would count. The second is the number itself. At least one page currently ranking for UAE IGCSE queries states that candidates must take six subjects. The published clarification says five. A page that gets the number right is more useful than a page with a longer subject list, and the only safe move for your own file is to read the current wording on moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation authority before acting on any version of it, including this one.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation. It is a regulatory process run by the ministry, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. What a tutor can do is make sure the five countable subjects are actually in a state to clear the threshold, which is a Year 10 question rather than a Year 13 one. The American-track requirements in the same clarification are included below for families moving between systems inside the UAE, since that crossover is common here.

sections.heading: Fourteen weeks out: a plan counted in papers, not in good intentions
paragraphs: A revision plan built from the syllabus contents page is a plan to run out of time. A plan built from the timetable works differently. Start with the actual dates for your child's series and zone, count the weeks, subtract the ones lost to Ramadan timing changes, Eid, half term and the school's own mock fortnight, and you are left with the real number of sessions available. That number is usually smaller than the family assumed and it is the only honest basis for deciding what to attempt.

Then allocate by marks rather than by anxiety. If a component carries a large share of the subject's total and the student is weakest there, it gets the sessions. If a topic is worth few marks and is genuinely broken, it gets left alone and the student is told so, which is more useful than a plan that pretends everything is coverable. Each session ends with a specific, markable piece of work: a question set, a past-paper section under timed conditions, a graph to plot. Work that is produced and marked moves a grade. Work that is read does not.

Ramadan shifts the whole shape of the plan in the UAE, and it is predictable enough to plan around rather than react to. Sessions move later, post-Iftar slots fill first, and energy in a 16:00 lesson is not what it was in January. Families who reschedule in advance keep their slot; families who wait find the specialist's evenings have gone. The same is true of the final fortnight, when every Year 11 family in the country wants the same two hours on a Saturday.

sections.heading: The practical paper, and what a video lesson can honestly do about it
paragraphs: This is the fair question to ask about online science tuition, so here is the specific answer. Cambridge science syllabuses assess practical skill either through a practical test paper or through a written alternative to practical paper, and which route a candidate sits is the centre's decision. Pearson International GCSE sciences assess practical skill inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical test. Confirm the route on the specification for your child's syllabus code, because the two routes reward noticeably different preparation.

Neither route awards marks for being in a laboratory on exam day. Both award marks for reading an instrument correctly, tabulating results with consistent significant figures, plotting a graph with sensible axes and a line of best fit, identifying the anomalous point, describing a variable as controlled rather than just naming it, and writing an observation in the precise language the mark scheme expects. Every one of those is a paper-based skill, and every one of them is improved by a teacher watching a student do it and correcting the actual error.

Over live video that looks like this: the student's own graph on a shared screen, marked line by line against the published criteria; a results table rebuilt in front of them to show where the significant figures went wrong; observation wording rehearsed until it is precise instead of approximately right. What online tuition cannot do is supervise the hands-on practical test if the centre has entered the student for that route. Where that applies, the school's laboratory sessions do that job, and the tutoring hour is better spent on the data, graph and evaluation questions that carry marks in every route.

sections.heading: Coursework, portfolios and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Several IGCSE subjects carry a centre-assessed component: an English coursework portfolio where the centre offers that route, a Geography or History coursework option with a written alternative paper as the other choice, practical ICT work assessed in the school. Those components run to internal deadlines set by your child's school, not by the board, and those internal deadlines are the ones that actually govern a family's spring term. Ask for them in writing at the start of the year.

What a tutor may do with that work is narrow and worth stating plainly, because this is the part of the market with the worst behaviour in it. A tutor teaches the method, explains the published criteria, asks what the evidence supports, points out where a claim is unsupported, and gives feedback on a draft the student produced. A tutor does not supply sentences, restructure a piece into submission condition, or hand over a model answer to be adapted. One page currently ranking in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright. That is a malpractice trigger that falls on the student, not the seller, and IGCSE coursework feedback from IB Gram works the other way round by design.

The practical test of whether support stayed on the right side of the line is simple: could the student explain every choice in the work to a teacher who asked, without preparation? If yes, the work is theirs. If no, something was done for them. Our tutors are briefed to work to that standard, and the same rule applies to revision help on a draft two days before a school deadline, which is when the pressure to cross the line is highest.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects sharing the same Year 11 week
paragraphs: A UAE IGCSE student is not only an IGCSE student. Private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, and in Dubai KHDA sets out exactly how. Those subjects occupy real timetable space in the same Year 10 and Year 11 weeks as the IGCSE course, and they do not disappear in exam season. Families planning a revision block without accounting for them consistently overestimate how many hours a week are available.

KHDA's requirements are detailed enough to plan around. Instructional time for the mandatory subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit; schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in first-language Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. The requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

One consequence matters for tutoring. For these subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support for Arabic or Islamic Education therefore means working with the material the school is required to use, and it has to match the stream the child is in: a non-Arab student in Arabic as an additional language is sitting a different course from an Arab student in first-language Arabic, and so is their tutoring.

paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for these queries publish no price at all, and two of the others quote US dollars. Here are the market bands in AED, with where each figure comes from. These are market rates read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. Our own model starts with a single trial lesson at no charge, booked through the enquiry form with no card details taken, and a quote for the subject and tier after it, because an hourly number without the subject, the tier and the number of weeks left is not a quote.

The pattern across the bands is consistent. Rates rise with subject scarcity and tier, not with marketing. A Core-tier maths hour and an Extended Further Pure Mathematics hour are different products, and the premium at the top of the table is largely scarcity. The other variable nobody prices openly is timing: the specialist end of every band sells out first in the eight weeks before a series, so the family booking in March for a June series is choosing from a smaller pool at a firmer price than the family who booked in October.

Two honesty notes. Monthly packages are priced per month, which means a late start buys fewer teaching weeks for the same fee, and that is worth checking before signing one. And we do not describe our tutors as current IB, Cambridge or Pearson examiners, because examiner status for an individual is not something we can evidence for you, and in this market it is claimed more often than it is held. Ask any provider, including us, how they would prove it.

sections.heading: In-home against live online once the entry is already in
paragraphs: Home tutoring is a real market in the UAE and a reasonable thing to want. It is worth describing accurately. A locally hired in-home tutor arrives at the family's address, teaches for an hour or two, and leaves; the published market band for that, travel included, runs roughly AED 180-500 an hour, and the individual tutor needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit to do it legally. The hour costs more than an online hour largely because someone spent forty minutes in traffic to deliver it.

IB Gram does not offer that in the Emirates. Home visits are a service offered only in India, and UAE families are taught one-to-one over live video instead. The comparison below is the case for why that is the better fit when an exam date is fixed, and the strongest column is the tutor pool. An in-home arrangement selects from whoever is within a thirty-minute drive of your community. Video selects by syllabus code. For a Core-tier maths student in a well-served part of Dubai the difference may be small. For an Extended Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 candidate in Umm Al Quwain it is the difference between a specialist and nobody.

The second real difference is continuity. UAE families relocate, travel in the summer and spend parts of the year outside the country, and an in-home arrangement ends at the emirate border. A video slot follows the student to Muscat, to Doha, to a grandparent's house in the UK in July, and back again in time for a November series. Over a two-year IGCSE course, the sessions that would have been lost to travel and traffic add up to more teaching time than most families expect.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and who licenses the tutor
paragraphs: Two separate regulatory questions get confused in this market. The first is who oversees the school: in Dubai it is KHDA, in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is ADEK, in Sharjah the Sharjah Private Education Authority, in Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, and in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education. Those five bodies are the complete map for UAE private schools. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not just inspection sits at emirate level.

The second question is whether the tutor is permitted to teach. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure you see quoted should be treated with scepticism.

Two things follow for parents. Ask any individual tutor whether they hold the permit, since the application runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time and no fee, which leaves little excuse. And be careful with the word approved. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific licence issued to a specific physical centre. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE centre, and claims no regulator or exam-board accreditation. Anyone describing their tutors as regulator-blessed should be asked for the permit number.

process.title: Tell us the three facts that matter
process.description: Board, series and tier, plus the subject and the syllabus code if you have it. If you do not know them, your child's exams officer does, and the question takes one email. Those three facts determine which past papers are useful and which tutor is the right one, and nothing sensible can be planned without them.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with the condition stated
process.description: One trial lesson at no charge, booked through the enquiry form, with no card details taken and no obligation afterwards. It is a teaching session rather than a sales call: the tutor sets diagnostic work, marks it live, and tells you what the gap actually is. That diagnosis is yours whether or not you continue.

process.title: A plan counted backwards from your series
process.description: We start from the live official timetable for your child's board, series and zone, subtract the weeks lost to mocks, Ramadan timing and holidays, and show you how many sessions genuinely remain. Hours are then allocated by paper weighting rather than by topic order, and you see the allocation before you commit to it.

process.title: Weekly lessons on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Live one-to-one video, a fixed weekly slot, a shared screen, and written notes after each session recording what was covered and what was set. Work is produced and marked every week against published criteria, because marked work is what moves a grade. Session notes make the plan visible to you without having to ask.

process.title: Review at the mock, not after the papers
process.description: The mock result is the decision point. We review the plan against it, reallocate the remaining sessions, and tell you plainly if the target needs changing. If a tier or subject question is still open at that point we say what the evidence supports and what the entry deadline permits, which is usually less than families hope.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is treated as the plan
whyPoints.description: Most tutoring is sold by the hour and planned by the topic. We plan from the entry deadline, the forecast-grade date, the zone timetable and the mock window, because those are the dates that decide what is achievable. A plan that ignores them is a wish list with an hourly rate attached.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject names
whyPoints.description: A 0580 candidate and a 4MA1 candidate sit different papers with different structures, and a Core entry and an Extended entry are different courses. Tutors are matched to the code and the tier, and past-paper work is tier-matched from the first session rather than after a mock reveals the mismatch.

whyPoints.title: Specialists reachable from every emirate
whyPoints.description: Live video removes the thirty-minute-drive constraint that limits who a family in Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain can actually hire. The scarce subjects at Extended tier are where that matters most, and it is the reason we deliver online here rather than sending anyone to a UAE address.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support that keeps the student safe
whyPoints.description: Feedback on the student's own drafts, against the published criteria, and nothing written or completed for them. The test we work to is whether the student could explain every choice in the work to a teacher who asked. In a market where finished coursework is openly sold, that boundary protects your child's entry.

whyPoints.title: Figures with a source, or no figure
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page carries where it was read and when, every regulatory statement names the authority, and the IB session dates that could not be verified from a primary source are not published at all. We claim no regulator or exam-board accreditation, hold no UAE centre, and publish no statistic we cannot show the working for.

whyPoints.title: An honest answer about availability
whyPoints.description: If no tutor covering your child's subject at the tier and time you need is free, we say so rather than booking a generalist into the slot. Where the specialist is outside the UAE, you are told that before the first lesson, along with what it means for timing on Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: Our school has not told us which IGCSE series my son sits. How do we find out?
faqs.answer: Email the exams officer, not the class teacher. Ask three things: which board the centre enters candidates with, which series your son is entered for, and which administrative zone the centre sits in. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones with different timetable versions, and its own guidance says it is essential to use the correct version for your zone. The reply gives you the dates that everything else is planned from. Without it you are working from a generic calendar, and a generic calendar is how families discover a deadline after it has closed.

faqs.question: Can the Core or Extended tier still be changed after the final entry has gone in?
faqs.answer: Usually not without a withdrawal and a fresh entry, if the board permits one at that point, and the centre makes that call rather than the family. The tier sits on the same entry form as the subject, so it locks on the final entry deadline. For one published Cambridge series, final entries closed on 27 November for an exam window opening on 3 February, and your school's internal cut-off will have been earlier again. If a tier conversation is still open in the spring term, treat it as a decision that has already been made and plan around the ceiling that applies.

faqs.question: My daughter's first paper is in nine weeks. What can an IGCSE private tutor realistically change?
faqs.answer: A meaningful amount, but not everything, and the honest version is more useful than a reassuring one. In nine weeks you can fix exam technique, rehearse the components that carry the most marks, repair two or three specific topics, and remove the errors that cost marks on questions she already understands. You cannot rebuild two years of a subject from the foundations, and anyone promising that is selling something else. The first session should be a diagnosis that tells you which of those categories her lost marks fall into, so the remaining hours go where the marks actually are.

faqs.question: Does the Arabic grade count towards the five subjects the ministry asks for?
faqs.answer: No. The published clarification of the equivalency requirements states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. Those five must be accredited subjects passed at no less than E or grade 3, alongside one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Families who assumed the mandatory school subjects would count sometimes reach Year 12 a subject short. Check the current wording on moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation authority before you rely on any version of this rule, including ours.

faqs.question: How does a live video lesson prepare a child for the written alternative to practical paper?
faqs.answer: Directly, because that paper is a paper rather than a laboratory. It awards marks for reading instruments, tabulating results with consistent significant figures, plotting graphs with sensible axes, identifying the anomalous point, and describing variables as controlled rather than merely naming them. All of that improves when a teacher watches the student do it and corrects the real error. Over video that means the student's own graph on a shared screen, marked line by line against the published criteria. If the centre has entered your child for the hands-on practical test instead, the school's laboratory time does that part.

faqs.question: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: does the choice change how many hours we need?
faqs.answer: It changes what the hours are spent on more than how many there are. Cambridge tiers most subjects into Core and Extended with different papers, so past-paper work has to be tier-matched. Pearson tiers far fewer, chiefly Mathematics A 4MA1 at Foundation and Higher, and assesses practical skill inside the written science papers rather than in a separate practical test. Paper structures, command-word habits and mark-scheme phrasing differ between the boards. A tutor working from the wrong specification can teach the content correctly and still leave a student unprepared for the paper in front of them.

faqs.question: What happens to the revision plan during Ramadan, and who reorganises it?
faqs.answer: We do, in advance, and that is the whole point of raising it early. Lessons move later in the day, post-Iftar slots fill before anything else, and concentration in a late-afternoon session is not what it was in January. Families who reschedule before Ramadan keep a slot that suits them; families who wait find the specialist's evenings have gone. The plan also subtracts the weeks lost to Eid and the school's mock fortnight before allocating sessions, so the number of hours you are shown at the start is the number that actually exists.

faqs.question: How much per hour do UAE families pay for IGCSE support, and does the rate rise before a series?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run roughly AED 33-150 an hour for budget online tuition, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180-500 for an in-home visit with travel priced in, and AED 200-450 and above for a subject specialist, with one premium provider publishing AED 650. Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list. The published rate does not usually rise in the eight weeks before a series, but the specialist end of every band sells out, so a late booking chooses from a smaller pool at a firmer price.

faqs.question: If we book in September rather than March, do the same number of hours cost less?
faqs.answer: The hourly rate is the same. The total is usually lower, because an earlier start needs fewer hours to reach the same grade. Starting in the autumn means content gaps are closed in the week they appear rather than rebuilt during a term that already contains mocks and coursework deadlines. A gap worth four hours in October regularly costs three or four times that in February. The earlier start also produces timed, marked, tier-matched work in time to inform the entry form, which the spring start cannot do at any price.

faqs.question: Can my son sit an IGCSE as a private candidate if his school will not enter him?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is a question for exams officers rather than tutors. Some centres accept external candidates for some subjects and some series, and each sets its own earlier deadline for them. Subjects with a practical test or a centre-assessed coursework component are the hardest to arrange this way, because somebody has to administer and mark that part. Start with your own school, then approach other centres in the emirate, and start months before the board's final entry deadline. In the northern emirates, where there are fewer centres, start earlier still.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with an IGCSE coursework portfolio, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the method, explain the published criteria, ask what the evidence supports, flag an unsupported claim, and give feedback on a draft the student produced. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite a piece into submission condition, or hand over a model to be adapted. The working test is whether the student could explain every choice in the work to a teacher who asked, unprepared. One page ranking in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright; the consequences of that fall on the student, not the seller, which is why the boundary is not negotiable.

faqs.question: Do we need to check a tutor's MoHRE permit, and how would we do it?
faqs.answer: Ask for it. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications run through the MoHRE app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so treat quoted amounts with caution.

faqs.question: When does a November-series result actually reach a UAE student?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume, which matters if a post-16 place depends on it. For Pearson International GCSE, November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For the June series, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Cambridge publishes its own release dates per series, with results issued to centres on Cambridge Direct before certificates follow some weeks later. Check the live date for your child's board and series on the board's own site, because provisional timetables and release dates are revised.

faqs.question: My son's school moved him to the Core tier in Year 11. Can he still take A Levels afterwards?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and on the sixth form's entry criteria, which the school sets rather than the board. On the A*-G scale a Cambridge Core entry reaches grades C to G, and on the 9-1 scale it reaches 5 to 1, so grades above those ceilings are not available from that entry however well he performs. Most A Level and IB Diploma courses ask above the Core ceiling in the subject itself. Ask the sixth form in writing what it accepts, then ask the exams officer what the entry deadline still allows.

faqs.question: We relocate to the UAE in February, mid-Year-11. What breaks, and what can be saved?
faqs.answer: The entry is the thing to check first. Whether the new school can enter your child for the series at that point, at the tier they were following, and for the same subjects, depends on the board's deadline and the centre's willingness, so ask the receiving exams officer before anything else. Board, syllabus code and tier may all change, which changes which past papers are useful. Tuition that started before the move can continue through it over video without losing the slot, which is usually the only part of the plan that survives a February relocation intact.

faqs.question: Is one weekly session enough, or should we book two subjects at once?
faqs.answer: One subject, one weekly slot, is the right starting point for most families, and it is enough when it starts early. Two subjects at once is appropriate when two are genuinely at risk and the family can protect two fixed slots a week around the mandatory school subjects and coursework deadlines. Booking three rarely works: the student runs out of time to do the work set, and unmarked work does not move a grade. Start with the subject where the gap is widest, review at the mock, and add a second only if the evidence says so.

igcse-private-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the date, not from the hourly rate
igcse-private-tutor.closingBody: The useful first step is not choosing a tutor. It is emailing your child's exams officer for the board, the series and the zone, then counting the weeks that are genuinely left. Send us those three facts and the subject, and we will tell you what the remaining time can realistically do, which components deserve the hours, and whether a specialist in that subject at that tier is actually free in the slot you need. The trial lesson that follows is a teaching session with marked diagnostic work, at no charge, with no card details taken. If the answer is that nobody covering your subject is available when you need them, we will say that too.

intro.heading: A resit is a purchase with a number attached, so start with the number
paragraphs: Results day has already happened in your house. There is a grade on the screen that is below what the school forecast, or below what a sixth form, a university offer or a Ministry of Education equivalency file needs, and the conversation has moved from teaching to money. Two numbers decide everything from here. The first is what a second attempt costs across all of its parts. The second is what that attempt has to change to be worth buying. Most families only ever see the second number as a hope rather than a target, which is why resit money so often goes on general revision in a subject where only one component failed.

The cost of an IGCSE resit arrives as four separate bills, and you control exactly one of them. The entry fee is set and published by the school or by the examination centre that accepts private candidates. The late-entry scale is set by the board, and it bites from a date months before the papers: Cambridge published 27 November 2026 as the final entry deadline for a series whose first paper sits on 3 February 2027. A results enquiry, if you go that route first, is priced by the centre and filed by its exams officer, not by a parent. Only the tutoring hours are yours to size, and sizing them is the whole job of this page.

A second attempt is cheaper to teach well than a first attempt, because you are no longer guessing. A first-time Year 11 candidate has school reports and a mock. A resit candidate has a statement of results carrying marks for each component the board set, plus the syllabus code and the variant digits of the papers actually sat. That is a diagnosis rather than an impression. A child who held up on the multiple-choice component and fell apart on the structured paper has a problem with written answers under timing, not a problem with physics. Spending on a full syllabus rewrite would be spending on the part that already worked.

A second attempt is also harder to staff than a first attempt, which is the part nobody prices honestly. You need one board, one syllabus, one tier and frequently one component, inside a window that may be eight weeks long, for a student who has already lost confidence in the subject. The pool of people who can do that within a twenty-minute drive of a villa in Khalifa City or an apartment in Jumeirah Lakes Towers is small, and it gets smaller the more specific the need. The pool of people who can do it over live video is the whole country and beyond, which is why IGCSE retake tuition is the clearest case for online delivery in the entire tutoring market.

So this page is built as a cost sheet with teaching attached. It reads the evidence you already hold, lists the four bills and who sets each, publishes the market AED bands with the provider that charges them named, puts the hours against the grade change they have to produce, compares a resit with repeating the year at frozen Dubai fees, counts the calendar backwards from the day the result landed, and sets out the private candidate route for families whose school will not re-enter their child. One thing to say plainly at the top: IB Gram does not make home visits in the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video.

igcse-resit-tutor.programmesIntro: A resit sits on one of a small number of routes, and the route changes the price, the deadline and who files the paperwork. Identify yours before you compare quotes, because a Core-tier candidate aiming at a grade the tier cannot award is being sold something that cannot be delivered. The codes and tiers below are the ones printed on your child's statement of entry.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.ageRange: Ages 14-16 · Years 10-11 · resat at any age
programmes.description: The Core tier covers the shared content of a Cambridge IGCSE syllabus and is examined on its own component set, with a grade range narrower at the top than the Extended tier's. A resit on Core is therefore two decisions, not one: whether the marks can be recovered, and whether the tier itself is the ceiling that produced the disappointing grade. Confirm the current grade range for your syllabus on cambridgeinternational.org before planning any hours.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools the tier is usually decided by the department during Year 10 and locked at entry, which means a family often discovers the ceiling only when the result arrives. A Dubai or Sharjah school will have its own policy on moving a former pupil up a tier for a second attempt, and SPEA approves assessment methods for Sharjah schools, so the conversation runs through the school rather than around it. Ask in writing which tier the re-entry would use.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.ageRange: Ages 14-16 · Years 10-11 · resat at any age
programmes.description: Extended adds the supplement content and is examined on the harder component set, with the full grade range available. Most UAE resits happen here, and most of them are component-specific rather than syllabus-wide: a strong multiple-choice mark alongside a weak structured paper, or solid theory undone by the alternative-to-practical component. The statement of results will show which, and that is where the first hour of a Cambridge IGCSE resit should go.
programmes.countryNote: Extended entries dominate the British-curriculum schools that make up the largest share of Dubai's private sector, which KHDA oversees as the authority responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Practically, that means most UAE resit candidates are Extended candidates competing for the same narrow pool of Extended-level subject specialists in the same eight-week window, and that scarcity is what the rate bands further down this page actually reflect.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.ageRange: Ages 14-16 · Years 10-11 · resat at any age
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE syllabuses carry 4-prefixed codes such as 4MA1 for Mathematics A and 4PH1 for Physics, and are examined in a May/June series and a November series each year. A Pearson Edexcel International GCSE resit is often the faster of the two board routes in practice, because the November series exists specifically as a second bite and its results reach students in January.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools teach Cambridge for some subjects and Pearson for others in the same year group, so a family resitting two subjects can find itself managing two boards, two timetables and two sets of deadlines. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the only safe practice on a UAE resit plan is to link the live timetable on qualifications.pearson.com rather than copy a date into a planner.

programmes.name: The private candidate IGCSE resit route
programmes.ageRange: No upper age limit · post-Year 11 and adult candidates
programmes.description: A private candidate IGCSE resit is an entry made through an examination centre that accepts candidates it does not teach, rather than through a school. The centre sets and publishes its own private candidate fee, handles the entry, hosts the papers and issues the statement of results. It is the route for a student whose school has left, whose school will not re-enter former pupils, or who is adding a subject the school does not offer.
programmes.countryNote: Centre coverage in the UAE is uneven. Dubai carries most of the centres that take private candidates, Abu Dhabi has fewer, and the northern and eastern emirates have fewer still, so a family in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain may be planning a drive on each paper day. Ask any centre for its published fee list, the components it can host, and whether it accepts candidates for the specific syllabus code on the statement of entry.

igcse-resit-tutor.subjectsIntro: Resits cluster in a predictable set of subjects, and the reason is almost always component-shaped rather than subject-shaped. The codes below are the common Cambridge and Pearson pairings, but check the code printed on your child's own statement of entry before anything is booked, because the same subject name sits on different codes at different schools.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended tiers, Foundation and Higher papers
subjects.description: The most resat IGCSE subject in the UAE and the one where tier choice does most of the damage. Marks go missing on multi-step problems where method marks are available but no working is shown, and on the topics taught last in Year 11 when revision time had already run out. A resit plan here is a topic audit against the component marks, then timed paper work.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical component account for most physics resits. Students who can state a law lose marks explaining a circuit in words, and the alternative-to-practical component rewards a way of writing about apparatus, variables and sources of error that is rarely taught explicitly. Both are trainable inside a short block, which is why physics responds well to a focused second attempt.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic and organic reaction pathways are the two cliffs. A resit candidate usually arrives able to recite definitions and unable to carry a calculation through unit changes without losing a factor of ten. Work on the calculation habits transfers across the whole paper, so chemistry resits often improve faster than the family expects from the first mark.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Biology grades slip on command words rather than content. Describe, explain and suggest ask for different shapes of answer and carry different marks, and a student who answers all three the same way loses steadily across a whole paper. A resit block here is largely answer-structure work against the published assessment objectives, with content revision as the smaller half.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.levels: Double award, Core and Extended tiers
subjects.description: A single qualification covering biology, chemistry and physics content, which makes a resit awkward: one weak discipline drags a grade that the other two supported. The component marks will usually show which third of the syllabus failed, and the resit hours should be weighted accordingly rather than split evenly across three sciences.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500, Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing are where marks move. Candidates who read widely still lose marks for not answering the question asked of the passage, and for writing in a register the task did not request. A resit is spent on close-reading drills and on timed writing against the published mark descriptors, not on reading more books.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, with and without the oral endorsement
subjects.description: The listening and reading components reward a scanning technique that can be taught quickly, and the writing components reward a small number of reliable sentence structures. For UAE students who need an English grade for a Ministry of Education equivalency file, this is frequently the subject where a single grade change completes the whole application.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455, Pearson 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the evaluation half of extended answers decide economics grades. Students lose marks drawing a correctly labelled diagram and then not referring to it, and lose more by describing a policy without weighing it. Both faults are visible in a single marked script, which makes economics a strong candidate for a short, evidence-led resit block.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450, Pearson 4BS1)
subjects.description: Application to the case material is the marked difference between a mid and a high grade. A resit candidate typically knows the theory and writes it in the abstract, scoring knowledge marks and missing application and analysis marks. Rebuilding answers around the case stem is the core of the work and shows up in marks within a few sessions.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables cost marks in volume, and the theory paper punishes vague definitions of hardware and data representation. Specialist supply in this subject is thinner across the UAE than in maths or the sciences, which shows up both in availability and in what the market charges for an hour. Book earlier than you would for a science resit.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Case-study recall and the skills paper carry the grade. Candidates lose marks offering a general answer where a named example was required, and lose more misreading graphs and maps under time pressure. A resit here builds a small bank of properly specific examples rather than revising the whole syllabus again.

igcse-resit-tutor.regionsTitle: Where a UAE resit candidate actually sits the papers
igcse-resit-tutor.regionsIntro: A resit is an administrative act as much as an academic one, and the administration is emirate-specific. Which authority oversees the school, how many centres accept private candidates nearby, and how far you drive on a paper morning all change by emirate. Lessons themselves are delivered online everywhere below.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and Dubai carries most of the examination centres that accept private candidates. Both the June and November series are commonly available here. Ask your school in writing whether it re-enters former pupils before assuming the private candidate route.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, so the person who taught the first attempt will not be the person coaching the resit.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with far fewer centres than the capital. Families here often find that a private candidate entry means travelling to Abu Dhabi on each paper day, which has to go into the plan before an entry is made rather than after. Confirm the centre's hosted components early.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A post-results change of qualification or tier is therefore a school-and-authority conversation, not something a parent can arrange independently with a tutor.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, alongside Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Centre choice is thin, so the practical question on a resit is which nearby centre hosts the specific components your child needs, including any alternative-to-practical paper.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. Appearing in none of the competitor pages we studied, RAK families are usually planning both a tutor and a paper-day drive at the same time.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory, and the thinnest centre coverage in the country. An east-coast family resitting in November should settle the centre question before the entry deadline, because a cross-country drive on three separate paper mornings is a different commitment from an eight-week block of online hours.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. UAQ appears nowhere in the competitor corpus we measured, which means families here get the least published help and the most guesswork. Start with the centre's published private candidate fee list, then plan the hours around the paper dates it can host.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's British-curriculum schools produce the largest share of UAE resit candidates simply by volume, and they are also where tier decisions are most often the hidden cause of a disappointing grade. Students we support attend schools across the emirate; the names below are the ecosystem a Dubai resit sits inside.

In the capital the resit conversation is shaped by ADEK's ethics rules, which keep a child's own subject teacher out of paid private tuition. That pushes families towards an external specialist from the start, and online delivery removes the Corniche-to-Khalifa-City drive from the equation entirely.
schools: Repton Al Barsha families relocating to Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: Here the binding constraint is rarely the tutor and almost always the centre. With SPEA, the RAK Department of Knowledge and the Ministry of Education each overseeing part of this group, families resitting outside Dubai need the centre's hosted-component list before they need a timetable of lessons.

igcse-resit-tutor.modesIntro: A resit has a hard deadline and a known weak component, so the shape of the hours matters more than the number of them. These four shapes cover almost every second attempt we are asked about, and each is priced by the hour rather than sold as a package you cannot leave.

modes.title: Diagnostic first, block second
modes.description: One free trial lesson in the subject being resat, with the statement of results open on screen, before anybody quotes you hours. The student works a short section of a past paper under timing while the tutor watches the process rather than the answers, and the session ends with a written note of which component the hours should target. No card is required and nothing is payable before or after the trial.

modes.title: A fixed resit block to the entry deadline
modes.description: Weekly or twice-weekly one-to-one hours running from the diagnosis to the paper, sized to the component rather than the syllabus. The block is reviewed at its midpoint against the plan written in session one, and hours can be moved between subjects if a second resit is running alongside. Most families resitting one subject book in the range of eight to sixteen hours, which is a planning assumption rather than a measured outcome.

modes.title: Final-six-weeks intensive
modes.description: For families who come to this after the entry has already been made and the window is short. Two or three sessions a week, built entirely around timed component practice and the marking criteria, with content work only where the component breakdown proves it is the cause. An intensive block cannot rebuild a syllabus from nothing, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling hours rather than a plan.

modes.description: Where the school will not re-enter your child, the academic work is the easier half. These sessions include time spent on the administration: identifying centres that accept private candidates for your syllabus code, reading their published fee lists, checking which components they can host, and working the entry deadline backwards into a revision timetable you can actually keep.

sections.heading: What the statement of results already told you, for free
paragraphs: A first attempt leaves behind evidence that a first-time candidate never has, and most families pay for tutoring without ever reading it. The statement of results carries the overall grade, and behind that grade the marks for each component the board set, together with the syllabus code and the variant digits of the papers actually sat. Those statement of results component marks are the cheapest diagnostic in the entire process, because they tell you which paper failed rather than which subject failed. The difference is the difference between a focused block and a wasted term.

Ask the school's exams officer for the component breakdown in writing, and ask for it before you speak to anybody about rates. Put it next to two other things you already hold: the forecast grade the school submitted, and the mock result it was based on. Where the forecast and the outcome agree, the problem is genuine and content-shaped. Where the forecast sat two grades above the outcome, something happened in the room rather than in the syllabus, and the hours should be spent on timing, reading the question and answer structure instead of on re-teaching topics the student already knows.

What the statement will never tell you is why. It cannot show that the paper ran out of time with two structured questions untouched, that a topic was taught during a week of absence, or that the tier was the ceiling all along. That is the only honest purpose of a first diagnostic session: the student works a section of a real past paper under timing while the tutor watches the process, and the two sources of evidence are put side by side. A resit plan written before that comparison is a guess with a price on it.
bullets: Request the component breakdown in writing from the exams officer
Compare forecast grade, mock result and final outcome side by side
Note the syllabus code and variant digits before shortlisting any tutor
Treat the first session as a diagnosis, not a lesson

sections.heading: The four bills behind a second attempt, and who sets each one
paragraphs: Families quote the tutoring rate at each other because it is the number they are shown. It is rarely the largest number and it is the only one you control. The first bill is the entry itself, made either as a re-entry through the school or as a private candidate IGCSE resit at a centre that accepts candidates it does not teach. Either way the amount is set and published by the school or the centre, not by a tutor and not by us. Ask for the published fee list in writing, and ask whether it is per subject or per component.

The second bill is the late-entry scale, which the board sets and which starts running from a date a long way before the papers. Cambridge's published key dates for its March 2027 series put final entries on 27 November 2026 for an exam period beginning 3 February 2027, which is the clearest illustration available of how early the money has to be committed. The third bill only applies if you go to the board about the original mark first: a results enquiry is filed by the centre's exams officer, priced by the centre, and some centres return the fee when a grade changes. A parent cannot file one directly.

The fourth bill is the hours, and here the IGCSE resit cost in AED is genuinely yours to size. The published market bands in the next section run from roughly AED 45 at the budget end to AED 650 for a premium named tutor, which is a fourteen-fold spread for something described on every website as the same service. The spread is not noise. It tracks who is permitted to teach, what they know about one syllabus, and whether the hour is spent on diagnosis or on filling time until the exam.
