ras-al-khaimah/al-dhait.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Diploma and both main IGCSE boards. Each match starts from a marked paper rather than a subject label, because the useful question is not which subject is weak but which questions in it are losing marks.

intro.heading: Understanding it in class and losing marks in the exam are different problems
paragraphs: Al Dhait is one of the largest residential districts in Ras Al Khaimah, spread north and south of the main road towards Dubai, mostly villas with some newer apartment blocks. Children here are scattered across more schools than in any other part of the emirate, because the district sits roughly equidistant from the city-centre campuses, the Khuzam campus and the coastal schools at Al Hamra. One household's two children can easily be at two schools on two different boards.

What unites the families who ask for help here is the shape of the complaint rather than the subject. A student is fine in lessons, completes homework, can explain a concept at the kitchen table, and then comes back from a mock three or four grades below expectation. Parents reasonably conclude that something is wrong with how the child performs under pressure, and the school often agrees, which is where the diagnosis stops.

It should not stop there, because the marks are recorded. Every mock paper is a list of exactly which questions were answered well, which were answered partially and which were abandoned. Read against the mark scheme, that list tells you whether the loss is pacing, command-term misreading, method not shown, a specific insecure topic, or an inability to start unstructured questions. Those five have different fixes and very different timescales.

The commonest finding in this district, across both boards, is that the content is largely in place and the marks are being lost in how answers are written. A student who writes a correct answer with no working loses method marks. A student who answers 'evaluate' as though it were 'describe' loses the top band without writing anything untrue. A student who spends eleven minutes on a four-mark opener forfeits the end of the paper. None of these is a knowledge problem, and all of them look like one on a report.

The sections below set out the diagnosis properly: how to read a marked paper, the mathematics topics that cost the most marks at IGCSE, how practical and data questions are actually credited in the sciences, what each command term demands, how the IB mathematics exploration is structured by criterion, what a mock does and does not tell you, and what the market charges. Tuition for Al Dhait families is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are offered only in India.

One local note. Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Questions about how a school assesses, reports or sets its mocks belong with the school and with that authority, not with an authority in another emirate.

ras-al-khaimah/al-dhait.programmesIntro: The three programmes below produce different diagnostic evidence. IGCSE gives you a marked paper against a published scheme; the Diploma gives you that plus criterion-marked internal work; MYP gives you criterion judgements and no paper at all.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight to ten subjects examined terminally, with published mark schemes for every past paper. That makes IGCSE the easiest stage at which to diagnose a problem precisely, because the student's answer can be laid next to the exact wording the examiner was told to credit.
programmes.countryNote: Al Dhait households frequently have children on both boards at once, and the mark schemes are not interchangeable. Cambridge Physics 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 credit practical understanding through different components, so a diagnosis built from the wrong board's scheme will misread a student's weakness. Get the syllabus code from the entry statement before any diagnostic work begins.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Terminal papers sit alongside internally assessed work marked against published criteria, so a Diploma student has two separate sets of evidence about where marks are going.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in this district often have a clear split: strong on paper marks and weak on internally assessed criteria, or the reverse. The two need completely different support. Criterion marks that lag behind paper marks usually point at reflection and communication rather than at subject understanding, and that is a writing problem with a short timescale.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of eight and reported as a 1-7 grade. Because there is no external paper before the optional eAssessment, the only diagnostic evidence available is the criterion breakdown behind the reported number.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where Al Dhait parents have the least information and the school has the most. The question worth asking at every reporting point is which of the four criteria the grade is built from. A student strong on knowledge and weak on communicating is heading for exactly the mark-loss pattern this page describes, two or three years before it shows up in a mock.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and unexamined. The measurable things at this stage are reading fluency, number-fact recall and written stamina, each of which can be tested in a few minutes and improved with short, frequent practice.
programmes.countryNote: The writing stamina deficit that produces mid-band extended responses at IGCSE is usually visible in Year 4. A child who can explain an idea aloud and cannot sustain a written paragraph is not weak at the subject; they are untrained at writing at length. Twenty minutes of timed writing twice a week changes it faster than any amount of extra content.

ras-al-khaimah/al-dhait.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are listed with the specific components where marks go missing, because that is the level at which a diagnosis is useful. A general statement that a student is weak at chemistry is not actionable.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Algebraic fractions, graph transformations, compound percentage change, bounds and the long unstructured multi-mark problems account for most of the recoverable marks. Students lose further marks writing a correct answer with no working, which forfeits method credit in both boards' schemes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus technique and proof. The characteristic loss is in the unstructured later questions where a topic is recognised but no method is prompted. In the exploration, marks go missing in personal engagement and reflection rather than in the mathematics itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and calculator work. Hypothesis testing, chi-squared and regression are the usual gaps. A real share of lost marks are calculator operation errors rather than mathematical ones, which is why calculator-specific practice is part of the diagnosis.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry gate everything after them. Multi-step calculations lose marks to rounding carried through several stages. In the practical component, marks go to precise language about variables and reliability rather than to describing the procedure.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Circuits and electromagnetism at IGCSE; fields and thermodynamics at Higher Level. Uncertainty and graph-analysis questions carry real marks and are rarely taught explicitly, so they often represent the fastest available recovery in the subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Extended-response marks are awarded for named mechanisms and exact terminology, so a student who revises by rereading plateaus in the middle bands. Data-handling questions are the second reliable loss, usually through imprecise comparative language.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: The summary task and reading-at-speed components separate the grades. In writing, register control earns more credit than vocabulary range. Speaking endorsement arrangements differ between the 0510 and 0511 variants, so the code matters to any diagnosis.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis rewards a repeatable paragraph structure applied under time pressure. Most students in this district have the ideas and lose marks on organisation, which is a quicker repair than reading more texts.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the internal assessment commentaries carry the grade. Evaluation written without reference to the diagram just drawn stops earning credit at the top band, and Higher Level quantitative questions reward legible working.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Command terms do most of the work in the case-study papers. Answering 'evaluate' at the depth of 'outline' loses the top band with nothing factually wrong, which is the clearest example of a writing loss rather than a knowledge loss.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Trace tables and pseudocode discipline account for a large share of IGCSE marks and are highly trainable. The Higher Level internal assessment loses criterion marks when students begin coding before the problem is properly scoped.

regions.note: Extensive villa streets closer to the city side, with children split between the city-centre campuses and the Khuzam campus. Two schools in one household is common here, which means two boards and two mark schemes.

regions.name: Khuzam

regions.name: Al Nakheel
regions.note: The commercial centre, holding the Indian-curriculum schools and most of the emirate's tuition centres. Families here can compare group provision against one-to-one more easily than elsewhere in the emirate.

regions.name: Al Uraibi and Al Mairid
regions.note: Older districts by the creek with earlier school finishes. Useful when an Al Dhait household is coordinating siblings across two different campuses with different end times.

regions.name: Al Hamra Village and Mina Al Arab
regions.note: The southern coastal communities and the IB-heavy side of the emirate. Al Dhait children attending these campuses travel the furthest and are rarely home before three.

regions.note: On the southern edge towards Umm Al Quwain. Some families here send children to schools across the emirate border, which changes both the board and the term calendar.

modes.description: A first session spent on the marked paper itself, identifying which of the five loss patterns is actually operating, followed by weekly sessions aimed only at those. Most students in this district turn out to need two or three specific repairs rather than a general course rerun.

sections.heading: Reading a marked paper: the five loss patterns
paragraphs: A diagnosis takes about an hour and needs three documents: the student's marked paper, the mark scheme for that paper, and the student in the room willing to explain what they were thinking. Everything else is guesswork. Reports describe outcomes; the paper records causes, question by question, in a form that can be counted.

There are five patterns worth separating, because conflating them wastes a term. Pacing shows up as the last question blank or rushed while the opening questions are over-answered. Command-term misreading shows up as correct content at the wrong depth. Method not shown shows up as right answers with partial credit. Insecure topics show up as whole questions abandoned rather than attempted badly. And the inability to start unstructured questions shows up as blanks on exactly the questions that carry the most marks.

Counting matters more than impressions. Add up the marks lost under each heading. In this district the usual result surprises families: pacing and command-term losses together often account for more marks than every content gap combined, and they are the two cheapest to fix. A student who has been told for a year that they need to work harder has frequently needed to work differently for about three weeks.

The table below maps the symptom families actually report onto the underlying pattern, how to confirm it, and what it takes to repair. The confirmation column matters: each pattern has a specific test, and running the test prevents a term of expensive effort aimed at the wrong thing.

sections.heading: The mathematics topics that cost the most marks
paragraphs: Across both IGCSE boards the same handful of topics account for a disproportionate share of lost marks, and they are not the topics students worry about. Trigonometry and geometry get the anxiety; algebraic manipulation and proportional reasoning take the marks. The reason is that the latter appear inside questions about something else, so a weakness there leaks across the whole paper rather than costing one question.

Algebraic fractions are the clearest case. A student who cannot combine them reliably will lose marks in questions ostensibly about rearranging formulae, about simultaneous equations, about rates of change and about graph work. Fixing the fraction technique repairs marks in four topic areas at once, which is why a diagnosis that works at topic level rather than question level is worth the hour it takes.

The same holds at Diploma level in a different register. In Analysis and Approaches the recurring leak is algebraic fluency inside calculus questions: the differentiation is understood and the simplification afterwards goes wrong. In Applications and Interpretation it is calculator operation, particularly in statistical tests where the right test is chosen and the wrong menu is used.

The table lists the topics worth checking first, with where they actually appear and why they go wrong. It is written for Extended and Higher tier candidates; for Core tier students the first three rows still apply and the last two generally do not. Work down it in order and stop at the first row that produces an error, because a leak high in that list makes everything below it harder to read accurately.

sections.heading: How practical and data questions are actually credited in the sciences
paragraphs: Practical and data-handling questions are the most reliably recoverable marks in IGCSE and Diploma science, and the most consistently neglected. They are not testing whether a student can perform an experiment. They are testing whether a student can write about one in the specific language a mark scheme credits: independent and dependent variables, control variables, repeatability, anomalous results, and the distinction between accuracy and precision.

That language is rarely taught explicitly, because in a busy practical lesson the activity itself consumes the time. The result is a predictable pattern in marked papers: students describe what they did, which earns little, rather than justifying why it was done that way and what would make the data more reliable, which earns the marks. The repair takes two or three sessions and is largely vocabulary and sentence structure.

The boards route this differently, which is another reason the syllabus code matters. Cambridge offers a practical test and an alternative-to-practical written paper depending on the centre's arrangements; Pearson handles practical understanding within its own paper structure. A student preparing for one and sitting the other has practised the wrong component, and this is a common discovery in a district where neighbouring children are on different boards.

For students taught online, the question of practicals comes up immediately and deserves a straight answer: practical work is done at school, and tuition supports the written understanding of it. A tutor can teach experimental design, error analysis and graph interpretation to a high standard over video. A tutor cannot and should not substitute for a school laboratory.

sections.heading: Command terms and the depth each one is asking for
paragraphs: Command terms are the single largest source of avoidable loss in written subjects, and they are the easiest thing on this page to fix. Every board publishes a glossary of them, every mark scheme is built around them, and almost no student has read either. The result is students answering every question at the same depth, which loses marks in both directions: too much written for recall questions and too little for analytical ones.

The mechanism is worth stating plainly. A one-mark 'state' question wants one piece of information, and a paragraph earns no more than the one mark while consuming time that the end of the paper needs. A six-mark 'evaluate' question wants a judgement supported in both directions with a conclusion, and a well-written description of the topic earns perhaps two of the six. Both errors are produced by the same habit.

Teaching this is quick because it is a classification task rather than a content one. A student sorts twenty past-paper questions by command term, writes the expected shape of each answer in note form rather than in full, and compares against the mark scheme. Two or three sessions of that typically produces a visible shift in the next timed paper, which is why it is usually the first repair attempted.

sections.heading: The IB mathematics exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Internal assessment is where Diploma students in this district most often lose marks they did not know were available, because the work is marked against published criteria that most students never read. The mathematics exploration is the clearest example and a useful template for the others: the criteria are lettered, each carries its own mark allocation, and they reward different things.

The pattern in marked explorations is consistent. The mathematics is usually competent. What is thin is the personal engagement, which asks for genuine individual initiative rather than a topic chosen from a list, and the reflection, which asks the student to consider the significance and limitations of what they have found rather than summarising it. Those two criteria are frequently where several marks sit unclaimed.

Presentation and mathematical communication are the other recoverable band. Presentation rewards a coherent, organised, concise piece with a clear aim. Mathematical communication rewards correct and consistent notation, defined terms, and appropriate use of symbols and graphs. Both are checkable against a descriptor in an afternoon, and both are routinely lost to habits rather than to ability.

Mark allocations and descriptor wording are revised between syllabus versions, so confirm the current letters and marks against your child's own subject guide or with their teacher before planning around them. What does not change is the method: read the descriptor, find the specific sentence the examiner is looking for, and check whether the student's draft contains it. A tutor may teach that process and give feedback on drafts the student has written. The exploration itself must be the student's own work throughout.

sections.heading: What a mock tells you, and what it hides
paragraphs: Mocks are the best diagnostic instrument a family has and the worst predictive one. They are frequently sat on shortened papers, sometimes with the topics flagged in advance, often in a hall with different conditions from the real series, and marked by a teacher who knows the student. Each of those is a reason to treat the grade with caution and the question-by-question breakdown with great respect.

What a mock reliably shows is where marks were lost within that paper. What it does not show is how a student will perform when the paper is full length, when no topics have been signalled, and when the stakes are real. Pacing in particular is systematically understated by a shortened mock, which is why students whose mock was comfortable sometimes run out of time in the actual exam.

There is a second distortion in the other direction. A mock sat before the syllabus has been completed will show gaps that are not gaps at all, merely content not yet taught. Families read a February mock as a verdict when half of it may be testing material scheduled for March. Asking the school which topics had been covered before the mock turns a frightening grade into a useful map.

The practical approach: ignore the overall grade, take the paper home, count the losses under the five headings from the first section, and ask the school two questions. Which topics had been taught before this paper was sat, and was this a full-length paper under exam conditions. Those two answers determine whether the mock is evidence or noise.

sections.heading: What a term of targeted repair costs around Al Dhait
paragraphs: No published rate table exists for Ras Al Khaimah, so the honest figures are Dubai ones. The bands below carry the provider who publishes them and should be read as a ceiling rather than a local quote. Families in this emirate commonly report paying at or below the Dubai mid-band for an equivalently qualified teacher.

The useful way to budget a targeted repair is by the work rather than by the hour. A pacing repair is two to four weeks, which is four to eight sessions. A command-term repair is two to three weeks. Method-shown habits take one to two weeks. An insecure topic is six to twelve weeks because the content has to be rebuilt and then tested. Adding those up for a specific student gives a number that a rate card cannot.

Marking is the cost most families do not anticipate and the one that produces the result. A full timed paper marked properly against the official scheme takes a tutor real time outside the session, and a programme of eight to twelve papers per subject is where a pacing problem actually gets fixed. A cheaper arrangement that skips the marking is not a cheaper version of the same thing.

IB Gram does not publish a fixed hourly rate on these pages. A consultation establishes which repairs are needed and how long they should take, a trial lesson tests the match, and a quote follows. For wider context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package, so confirm your own school's position locally rather than assuming it applies here.

sections.heading: Working from Al Dhait: the honest limits of live video
paragraphs: Diagnostic work suits video unusually well, because the central activity is two people looking at the same marked paper. A shared screen with annotation is in some respects better than two people leaning over one sheet of paper: both can write, the annotated version is saved, and the student can refer back to it the following week. Marking, counting and comparing against a scheme all transfer without loss.

Where video asks more of the student is in sustained talking. A diagnosis depends on a student explaining what they were thinking when they wrote a wrong answer, and a reticent child in a room where family can hear them will not do that. Headphones and a space out of earshot fix it in most cases, and the trial lesson is where it is tested rather than assumed.

There are two things video cannot do, and they should be said plainly. It cannot run a school laboratory, so practical work stays at school and tuition supports the written understanding of it. And for a young child who needs an adult physically beside them to stay on task, a local arrangement is the better choice. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India.

The reason this format is the right one in Al Dhait is supply rather than preference. The district sits between three school clusters, children here are spread across both IGCSE boards and the IB, and the local pool of teachers who have marked a specific Higher Level paper or supervised an exploration is very small. Matching on syllabus code rather than on distance is what makes a diagnosis possible at all.

process.title: Send the marked paper, not a summary
process.description: The marked mock, the mark scheme if the school released it, and the syllabus code from the entry statement. A report tells you an outcome; the paper records the cause question by question, and that is what a first session is built on.

process.title: Count the losses before teaching anything
process.description: Marks lost to pacing, to command terms, to method not shown, to insecure topics and to unstarted long questions, added up separately. The result frequently reorders a family's priorities, because the cheap repairs often account for more marks than the expensive ones.

process.title: Name the repair and the timescale
process.description: Each pattern has a realistic duration: two to four weeks for pacing, six to twelve for a rebuilt topic. Agreeing both at the start means progress can be judged against something specific rather than against a general sense of whether things feel better.

process.title: Run marked timed papers alongside
process.description: Full papers sat to time and marked against the official scheme, with the review in the next session. Without this the diagnosis cannot be retested, and pacing in particular only improves under genuine time pressure rather than in discussion.

process.title: Re-diagnose at the next real assessment
process.description: The next mock or timed paper is the checkpoint. Marks lost under each heading are recounted, and the plan either narrows to what remains or the match changes. Nobody should be guessing in March whether a term of sessions worked.

whyPoints.title: The diagnosis comes first
whyPoints.description: Sessions begin from your child's own marked paper and a count of where the marks actually went. That is a different starting point from a general course rerun, and it is usually why two or three specific repairs replace a term of broad revision.

whyPoints.title: Papers marked to the board's own scheme
whyPoints.description: Self-assessed practice teaches a student almost nothing about how credit is awarded. Papers are marked against the official scheme and reviewed line by line, which is what turns a timed paper from an exercise into evidence.

whyPoints.title: Command terms and criteria taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: The published command-term glossary and the internal assessment descriptors are read with the student rather than paraphrased. Most marks lost in written subjects in this district are lost to depth of answer, and that is a classification skill rather than a content one.

whyPoints.title: Honest timescales, including the slow ones
whyPoints.description: Pacing is a two to four week repair. An insecure topic is six to twelve weeks. An inability to start unstructured questions takes a term. Those are stated before anyone commits, so a family is not judging progress against an unrealistic expectation.

whyPoints.title: Coursework boundaries that protect the student
whyPoints.description: Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and TOK essays remain the student's own work. Sessions explain descriptors and give feedback on drafts the student has written, and never supply text, data or a finished product.

whyPoints.title: Plain about what IB Gram is
whyPoints.description: An independent tutor-matching platform with no UAE premises and no accreditation from the Department of Knowledge, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Schools named on this page are local context only.

faqs.question: How do we work out exactly where our son is losing marks?
faqs.answer: Take his marked mock, the mark scheme for that paper, and an hour with him in the room. Count the marks lost separately under five headings: pacing, command-term misreading, method not shown, insecure topics, and long questions never started. The totals usually reorder a family's assumptions, because pacing and command-term losses together often exceed every content gap combined and are the two cheapest to repair. A report gives you an outcome; the paper gives you the causes question by question.

faqs.question: Which maths topics quietly cost IGCSE students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Algebraic fractions, proportional and percentage reasoning, graph transformations, and bounds or rounding. None of them is the topic students worry about, and all of them appear inside questions ostensibly about something else, so a weakness leaks across the whole paper rather than costing one question. Fixing fraction technique alone repairs marks in rearranging formulae, simultaneous equations, rates of change and graph work. That is why a topic-level diagnosis is worth the hour it takes rather than a question-level one.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: Cambridge offers centres a choice between a practical test and a written alternative-to-practical paper in the sciences, and Pearson handles practical understanding within its own paper structure. Either way the marks go to writing about experimental work in specific language: identifying independent, dependent and control variables, justifying why a step improves the data, handling repeats and anomalies, and suggesting a specific improvement rather than 'be more careful'. It is one of the most recoverable areas on any science paper and takes two or three sessions.

faqs.question: What does the command term 'explain' actually want?
faqs.answer: A reason or a mechanism, with cause linked to effect, usually for three or four marks. 'Describe' wants what happens in sequence without reasons. The characteristic loss is answering 'explain' with a description, which is factually correct and earns perhaps one of four marks. Board and subject glossaries differ slightly, so read the one in your child's own syllabus document. The fastest repair is sorting twenty past-paper questions by command term and writing the expected answer shape in note form before checking against the scheme.

faqs.question: How is the IB mathematics exploration marked?
faqs.answer: Against lettered criteria, each with its own mark allocation: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. The consistent pattern in marked explorations is competent mathematics with thin personal engagement and thin reflection, because those two criteria reward genuine individual initiative and critical consideration of limitations rather than a summary of findings. Mark allocations and wording are revised between syllabus versions, so confirm the current figures with your child's teacher or subject guide before planning around them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my daughter's past papers properly?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the marking is the part that produces the result rather than an administrative extra. A paper marked against the board's official scheme shows exactly which marks were available and which wording earned them, which is information a student cannot generate alone. Self-assessment fails in both directions: a generous student learns nothing, a harsh one only becomes discouraged. Proper marking takes a tutor real time outside the session, so an arrangement that skips it is not a cheaper version of the same programme.

faqs.question: Is a mock grade a reliable prediction of the real result?
faqs.answer: It is the best diagnostic you have and a poor predictor. Mocks are often shortened, sometimes have topics signalled in advance, and are usually marked by someone who knows the student. Shortened papers in particular understate pacing problems, which is why a comfortable mock can be followed by running out of time in the real series. Ask the school two questions: which topics had been taught before the paper was sat, and was it a full-length paper under exam conditions. The answers decide whether the grade is evidence or noise.

faqs.question: My child insists she understands it in class but freezes in the exam. What is that?
faqs.answer: Almost always two of the five loss patterns operating together, most commonly an inability to start unstructured long questions combined with pacing. Classroom work is scaffolded: a teacher sets context, breaks a problem into steps and prompts the next move. An exam question worth six marks provides none of that. The repair is practice specifically on the highest-mark questions with the scaffolding removed, which is uncomfortable at first and is the only thing that works. It takes about a term.

faqs.question: How many marks is it realistic to recover in a single term?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on which pattern is operating, which is why the diagnosis comes first. Pacing, command-term and method-shown repairs are quick, two to four weeks each, and together they often account for a substantial block of marks in a marked paper. Rebuilding a genuinely insecure topic takes six to twelve weeks and repairs the marks attached to that topic alone. Nobody should promise a specific grade from a specific starting point, and anyone who does is selling something other than teaching.

faqs.question: What does targeted tutoring cost for a family in Al Dhait?
faqs.answer: No rate table has been published for Ras Al Khaimah, so the figures available are Dubai ones and should be read as a ceiling. Named providers publish AED 45-150 an hour for budget online tuition, AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180-500 for in-home visits with travel priced in, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist, with one premium provider at AED 650. Budget by the repair rather than the hour: four to eight sessions for pacing, eight to sixteen for a rebuilt topic. IB Gram quotes after a consultation.

faqs.question: Are there local tutors in Al Dhait for Higher Level subjects?
faqs.answer: Generalist support is findable locally and is often the right answer for a lower-secondary student. Higher Level specialists are a different matter: this emirate has a small private-school set, which means few Higher Level sets, which means few teachers with Higher Level experience, which means a very small pool anywhere in the northern emirates. Matching over live video changes the filter from who lives nearby to who teaches that course and has marked that paper. Where no specialist is available you are told rather than matched to an approximation.

faqs.question: Would a good revision guide do the same job as paid sessions?
faqs.answer: For content gaps, often yes, and it should be tried first. A well-chosen guide plus the official syllabus document covers what was missed, and it costs a fraction of a term of sessions. What a guide cannot do is count where your child's marks are actually going, mark a timed paper against the official scheme, or notice that their working drifts only under time pressure. Buy the guide for content and pay for attention where attention is the missing ingredient.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks when his final answer is right?
faqs.answer: Because method carries marks. On questions worth three or more marks, both boards' schemes award credit for the steps as well as the answer, and a bare answer forfeits them. It is also the cheapest repair on this page: one to two weeks of rewriting answers in the scheme's own structure usually fixes it permanently. Check it by looking only at the questions worth three or more marks on his last paper and comparing what he wrote with what the scheme was prepared to credit.

faqs.question: How often should a student sit a full timed paper?
faqs.answer: Weekly in the exam term, and once a fortnight before that, with eight to twelve full papers per subject across an exam year. Schools typically manage two or three in class, enough to show the format and nowhere near enough to build pace. The paper has to be full length and uninterrupted, which is why a weekend morning works better than a school night. The review in the following session is where the learning happens; a paper sat and never discussed is an hour spent for very little.

faqs.question: Is it worth asking for a remark after results?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the decision should be made on evidence rather than disappointment. Both boards operate review and enquiry-about-results processes with their own deadlines, which are short, so the decision has to be made quickly after results are released. The school's examinations officer manages the request rather than the family, and there is usually a fee and a risk that a mark can move in either direction. Ask the school to look at the component marks first: a single unexpectedly low component is a stronger case than a disappointing total.

intro.heading: Who actually lives in Al Hamra Village, and why it changes the tutoring question
paragraphs: Al Hamra Village is not a suburb of a city. It is a self-contained waterfront community roughly twenty-five kilometres south of Ras Al Khaimah city centre, built around a golf course, a marina and a small mall, with the E11 running past it towards Umm Al Quwain in one direction and Al Jazirah Al Hamra in the other. That geography is the first thing that shapes an academic plan here, and it is the thing most tutoring pages written for the UAE quietly ignore.

Three household types dominate. There are long-lease villa families on the golf and marina plots, usually with two or three school-age children and one or two parents commuting south towards Dubai or working inside the emirate's hospitality and manufacturing sector. There are apartment households in Bab Al Bahr and Al Hamra Views, often smaller, often on shorter contracts, and often arriving mid-year from another country entirely. And there are part-year owners who treat the village as a second home, with children enrolled remotely or in schools abroad, who want continuity rather than a term's worth of lessons.

Each of those three groups hits a different wall. The villa families run into the school run: a child at a campus in Al Nakheel or Khuzam leaves the village before seven and is not back, fed and settled, until close to five. The apartment families run into mid-year entry, which in practice means arriving into the second half of a Cambridge IGCSE course with a syllabus they have never seen and an entry deadline that has already passed. The part-year households run into continuity, because a tutor who only teaches from a desk inside Ras Al Khaimah cannot follow a family to Europe for six weeks of summer.

The academic pressure point they share is thinner specialist cover. Ras Al Khaimah's private-school set is small and concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, so a student taking a less common Higher Level option is often one of very few in the whole emirate doing so. When that happens, the local pool of people who have taught that exact syllabus is not small, it is close to empty. That is the practical reason IB and IGCSE tutors in Al Hamra Village work online rather than by car.

IB Gram matches students to tutors by syllabus code, level and assessment component, then delivers the lessons one to one over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. What a family here gains from that is access rather than convenience, which is a different argument from the one a Dubai page would make. A student in Al Hamra Village sitting Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics should be taught by somebody who knows the 4PH1 paper structure, and in this emirate that person is reached over a screen.

The rest of this page is written for those three households specifically: when a weekday lesson can realistically start from this village, which campuses the children actually attend, what the Ras Al Khaimah market charges, what the Department of Knowledge controls, how Cambridge and Pearson deadlines fall months before the exams, and where the line sits between teaching a student and producing work for them.

ras-al-khaimah/al-hamra-village.programmesIntro: Families in the village sit across four distinct programme routes, and they are not interchangeable. A child who moves between them mid-stream loses time, so it is worth knowing what each one assesses before booking anything.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units rather than separate subjects, with learning organised around six conceptual themes and assessed continuously by the class teacher. There is no external examination and no published grade, which is why parents often do not realise a gap has opened until the first year of lower secondary. Reading fluency, number sense and the habit of writing an extended explanation are the three things that carry forward.
programmes.countryNote: Primary provision inside Ras Al Khaimah is the easiest part of the emirate's school map to fill, and most Al Hamra Village children at this stage are at a campus within a twenty-minute drive. Support at this level is usually short and diagnostic: a handful of sessions to establish whether a maths or literacy gap is genuine before it reaches a graded programme.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each marked against four criteria lettered A to D on a one-to-eight scale, with the four criterion totals converted to a single grade from one to seven. Criterion A is usually knowledge and understanding; the later criteria reward investigation, communication and reflection. Students who are strong on content but weak on structured written response lose marks on C and D without understanding why.
programmes.countryNote: The IB Middle Years Programme tutor requests we see from Ras Al Khaimah cluster around criterion-based feedback, because a report card of letters and eights reads nothing like a percentage. Lessons here are usually spent teaching a student to write to a command term and a criterion descriptor rather than re-teaching content they already know.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internally assessed component alongside external papers, and the internal assessment is marked against published criteria by the school and then moderated. Higher Level courses add both content and a further examination paper in most subject groups.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the Al Hamra Village distance problem bites hardest. A student taking a Higher Level option that only a handful of candidates in the emirate sit will not find a local teacher who has marked that component before. An online IB tutor in Ras Al Khaimah solves a supply problem, not a travel problem, and that is the honest framing.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses assessed almost entirely by terminal written papers, with syllabus codes that matter: Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610; Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1, Physics 4PH1. Cambridge separates Core and Extended tiers in several subjects, capping the attainable grade on the Core route, and the tier decision is made by the school at entry.
programmes.countryNote: Most Al Hamra Village families on the British route reach IGCSE through a campus in Al Hamra or Al Nakheel, and the first thing a Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Al Hamra Village needs to establish is which board and which tier the school has actually entered the child for. Cambridge and Pearson set different papers for the same subject name, and preparing for the wrong one wastes a term.

ras-al-khaimah/al-hamra-village.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Ras Al Khaimah families ask for most often, with what each one actually assesses and the point at which marks tend to go missing. Requests from this village skew towards the sciences and Economics, which is a direct consequence of how few local candidates sit them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with a Higher Level paper that rewards technique under time pressure. Marks go missing in two places: unjustified steps in a proof question, and the exploration, where students choose a topic too large to treat properly in the page allowance.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work, with graphical display calculator use embedded in the papers rather than optional. Students arriving from a content-heavy system often under-use the calculator and lose method marks they could have had for free.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, waves and, at Higher Level, extended topics that assume confident algebra. The recurring failure is not conceptual: it is unit handling, significant figures and the inability to write the three-mark explanation the mark scheme wants.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Bonding, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. Organic chemistry is where Ras Al Khaimah students most often stall, because it rewards pattern recognition across dozens of reactions rather than memorising a list of facts.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cell processes, genetics, physiology and ecology, assessed with a heavy emphasis on data interpretation. Students who revise by rereading notes score well on recall questions and badly on the graph, table and experimental-design items that carry the bulk of the marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and, at Higher Level, additional quantitative work. Diagram accuracy is the single largest source of lost marks: an unlabelled axis or a missing shift arrow turns a correct argument into a partial one.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, marketing, operations and finance, with a case-study paper that punishes generic answers. Students need to apply a tool to the specific firm in front of them, which is a skill that has to be practised on unseen material rather than read about.

subjects.name: English: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Close analysis of literary and non-literary texts, an individual oral and a comparative essay at Higher Level. The common gap for students in this emirate is unseen commentary: plenty of practice on studied texts, almost none on a passage they have never met.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking at the level the school's licensed curriculum sets, running alongside the international programme rather than instead of it. For non-Arab students this is frequently the weakest line on a report and the easiest to move with weekly structured practice.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language
subjects.description: Standard Arabic grammar, literary analysis and extended writing, assessed to a markedly higher standard than the additional-language route. Specialist cover for this stream is one of the harder matches to make anywhere in the northern emirates.

regions.note: The commercial centre of Ras Al Khaimah and where several of the emirate's larger private campuses sit. Twenty to thirty minutes from the village in normal traffic, longer on a school morning.

regions.name: Khuzam

sections.heading: What a search for IB and IGCSE tutors in Al Hamra Village is really asking
paragraphs: The literal answer: IB and IGCSE tutors in Al Hamra Village are available through IB Gram as one-to-one lessons over live video, matched to the exact syllabus and level the student sits, with a free first lesson before anything is booked. We do not send a tutor to an address in this village or anywhere else in the UAE, and we say so before you ask.

Behind that search there are usually one of three real questions. The first is availability: can a family twenty-five kilometres south of Ras Al Khaimah city actually get a specialist, or will they be offered a generalist who covers everything from Year 4 maths to Diploma Chemistry. The second is timing: will a lesson fit after a school run that eats the late afternoon. The third is competence: does the person teaching know this board's papers, or just the subject in general.

Those three questions have different answers here than they would in Dubai Marina, which is why this page is not a Dubai page with the place name swapped. In Dubai a family has a genuine choice between a car-borne tutor and a remote one, and the comparison is about cost and convenience. In Al Hamra Village the comparison is between a remote specialist and nobody at all for several of the subjects parents ask about most.

So the structure below works outwards from the household rather than inwards from the product. Who lives here, where their children go to school, what the afternoon actually looks like, what the market charges, what the regulator controls, when the deadlines fall, and what a tutor is and is not allowed to touch.

sections.heading: The Al Hamra afternoon: what the school run does to a lesson slot
paragraphs: A secondary student living in Al Hamra Village and schooled in Al Nakheel or Khuzam is typically in a car or bus for forty to sixty minutes a day. School finishes in the early afternoon, the run home takes twenty-five to thirty-five minutes depending on the Sheikh Mohammed Bin Salem Road, and then there is food, a sibling pickup and in many households an activity at the golf club or the marina. A 16:00 lesson sounds reasonable on paper and is a negotiation every single week in practice.

The slots that hold are later than families first expect. For students at the campus inside the community, 16:30 works. For Al Nakheel and Khuzam students, 17:00 is the earliest reliable start and 17:30 is the one that survives a bad traffic day. For households out towards Seih Al Uraibi or with a parent commuting from Dubai, 18:30 or 19:00 is the honest answer. A slot that is slightly too late and always happens beats a slot that is ideal and is cancelled twice a month.

Friday and the weekend behave differently. Ras Al Khaimah schools run a Monday to Friday week with Friday finishing early, which makes Friday afternoon the single best window in the week for a ninety-minute session, particularly for coursework and extended writing that does not fit into sixty minutes. Saturday mornings work for exam-year students and almost never for anyone younger.

Ramadan rearranges all of it. School days shorten, the afternoon becomes unworkable for most households, and the useful window moves to after Iftar. We re-base the whole Ras Al Khaimah timetable for that month rather than asking families to keep a slot that no longer fits, and the tutor stays the same throughout.

sections.heading: The school map Al Hamra families actually work with
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah's private-school provision is small by UAE standards and concentrated in three places: the Al Hamra and Al Jazirah Al Hamra area, the Al Nakheel commercial centre, and Khuzam inland. For a family in the village that means a short list rather than a choice, and it means siblings are often at the same campus by necessity rather than preference.

Curriculum coverage follows the same pattern. The British route through International GCSE is well represented, Indian curricula have long-established campuses serving a large resident community, and the IB continuum exists but at far fewer sites than a family arriving from Dubai or Abu Dhabi would expect. A child who wants a specific Diploma subject combination may find that no campus within reach offers it.

This is where the regulator matters in a practical way. The Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, according to the UAE government's own guidance, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader remit than inspection alone: what a school is permitted to offer is a regulatory decision, not purely a commercial one.

For tutoring, the consequence is simple. We ask which campus, which board and which tier before matching anybody, because the same subject name means different papers at different schools, and a student entered for Cambridge Core cannot be prepared with Extended material. The school's entry decision sets the ceiling, and a tutor who does not check it wastes the family's money.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Ras Al Khaimah, in AED
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring sites in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. The figures below are market rates gathered from published competitor pages and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table for 2026. They are what the market charges, not an IB Gram price list, and they are included because a family planning a two-year Diploma needs a number to plan against.

Rates in the northern emirates sit at the lower end of the published UAE bands for generalist work and at the same level as Dubai for genuine specialists. The reason is supply, not generosity: a Year 8 maths tutor is easy to find anywhere, while someone who has marked Higher Level Chemistry internal assessments is scarce everywhere, and scarcity prices the same in Al Hamra Village as in Jumeirah.

The in-home column is included for honesty rather than as an offer. It is what the market charges when somebody drives to a villa, and in this emirate that premium buys a shorter list of available subjects rather than a longer one. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE, so for us that column is a comparison, not a product.

Two cost notes specific to this market. First, a part-year household paying for a block of lessons and then stopping for eight weeks usually spends more over a two-year course than one paying a steady weekly rate, because re-diagnosis costs lesson time. Second, exam-year support is the expensive part of the plan, so a family that starts in the first Diploma year typically spends less per grade moved than one that starts eight weeks before the papers.

sections.heading: Specialist cover this far north: what we can and cannot fill
paragraphs: This is the section competitors leave out, and it is the one a family in Al Hamra Village should read first. There are subjects where a Ras Al Khaimah student has a genuine local choice, subjects where the local pool is one or two people, and subjects where there is nobody in the emirate who has taught the syllabus. Pretending otherwise wastes a parent's time.

Our rule is disclosure before booking. If the subject and level you need has a tutor available who teaches from inside the UAE, you are matched to them. If it does not, we say so and offer the alternative, which is a specialist based elsewhere teaching on Gulf Standard Time. The lesson is the same format either way, because every UAE lesson is online, but the family should know which situation they are in before paying for anything.

The scarcest requests from this emirate are consistent: Higher Level Chemistry and Physics, Economics, Business Management, Arabic as a first language, and internal assessment supervision in any science. The easiest to fill quickly are International GCSE Mathematics, English, the separate sciences at Core and Extended tier, and Middle Years support across all eight subject groups.

Where a match genuinely cannot be made on the timeline you need, we say that too. A parent told honestly in October that a particular Higher Level option will take three weeks to staff can plan around it. A parent told in October that everything is fine, and discovering in November that it is not, has lost a month.

sections.heading: The Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge and what it controls
paragraphs: Private schooling in the UAE is not governed by one body. Dubai answers to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its own Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall under the federal Ministry of Education. A family moving within the country changes regulator as well as address.

For Al Hamra Village the relevant authority is the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, which the UAE government describes as regulating private education in the emirate. Alongside Sharjah's authority, it also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That last phrase is the one parents underestimate: the range of courses a campus may offer is a regulated matter.

Underneath all of it sits a federal baseline. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule that puts Arabic on a British-curriculum timetable in Al Hamra Village just as firmly as on a timetable in Dubai.

IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by any of these bodies, and no tutoring platform should imply otherwise. What we do is name the authority that applies to your child's school, explain what it governs, and point you at its own published material rather than paraphrasing it. Where a tutor is teaching privately from inside the UAE, the relevant permit is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the paper: Cambridge and Pearson deadlines
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names an exam session, a registration deadline or a results date. That absence is strange, because the deadline a family most often misses is not the exam itself but the entry, which falls months earlier and is made by the school rather than the parent.

Cambridge International runs International GCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a Ras Al Khaimah centre that is a real administrative risk, not a footnote.

The March 2027 series is the clearest worked example of how far ahead the paperwork runs. Cambridge publishes the exam period as 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results released on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates issued in late June. The entry closes more than two months before the first paper.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May or June and November series each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is always the document to work from rather than a date copied onto a tutoring page. IB session and results dates are set by the IB and should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator, which is why none are printed here.
