sections.heading: Cambridge series, entry deadlines and the zone rule that binds your dates
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Which series your child sits is a school decision, made as a Cambridge centre, and it is made early. Entries are the hinge of the whole plan: a revision schedule aimed at the wrong series is wasted work, and a family that assumes June when the school has entered November loses a term of urgency it will not recover.

The administrative detail families most often miss is zoning. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a Ras Al Khaimah parent that means a timetable downloaded from a search result is not evidence of anything. Ask the exams officer which zone the centre sits in and work from that version.

A worked example of how far ahead entries fall: for the Cambridge March 2027 series, the examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due by 27 November 2026, forecast grades by 27 February 2027, results are released on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. The March series is not the series most UAE centres use, but the shape is the point - the deadline that decides what your child sits lands roughly ten weeks before the first paper.

Pearson candidates work to a parallel but separate calendar. International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year, the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the right habit is to link the live official timetable rather than trusting a date copied onto a tutoring page, including this one.

sections.heading: Does Business Studies count towards UAE equivalency?
paragraphs: For a British-track student, the Ministry of Education equivalency rule is specific and worth knowing before Year 10 option blocks are chosen. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

Business Studies is an accredited IGCSE subject and can sit inside that count of five. What the rule does not do is rank subjects, so a family worrying about whether Business Studies is respected has the wrong question; the questions that matter are whether the certificate is from an accredited board and whether the grade clears the floor. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a requirement of six IGCSE subjects for UAE candidates. Five is the figure in the sourced reporting, and a family planning around six is budgeting for an exam it may not need.

Equivalency is a Ministry process, not a tutoring product. IB Gram does not perform, submit or expedite it, and no tutoring purchase makes it faster. Verify current requirements on the Ministry of Education's own channels or with the emirate attestation authority before relying on any figure, including the ones quoted here, and keep in mind that the American-track requirements are different again - English through a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and at least 450 in SAT Mathematics.

There is no published IB points threshold in the sourced material, so this page does not state one. If a tutoring site quotes you an IB equivalency score without pointing at a Ministry page, treat the number as decoration.

sections.heading: Finding a 0450 specialist when the local pool is small
paragraphs: Private education in Ras Al Khaimah is regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader remit than inspection alone, and it is why RAK Department of Knowledge private schools can differ from Dubai schools in fee structure and in approved programme mix even when both sit Cambridge papers.

What the regulator cannot do is manufacture subject specialists. Across the northern emirates the realistic supply of adults who have taught 0450 to examination for several years is thin, and thinner again in a specific subject-and-year combination. Postcode matching therefore fails here in a way it does not fail in Dubai: insisting on someone who lives nearby narrows an already narrow pool to whoever is available, which is how a family ends up paying specialist rates for a generalist with a textbook.

IB Gram's answer is to drop the distance constraint rather than the specialism. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard for cash-flow tables and screen sharing for marked scripts. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India - so the comparison a parent should make is not online against our own in-home option, but a subject specialist on video against a nearby generalist in the room.

On permits, the position is worth stating plainly because it is a live compliance question in the UAE. Individuals providing private lessons need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and MoHRE publishes the application route as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' through its smart app, website and e-services system. Ask any tutor you are considering for theirs, whether the lessons run in person or, as ours do, over live video.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, past papers and what a tutor may hand over
paragraphs: Business Studies 0450 has no coursework, which removes the most common academic-honesty trap in the IGCSE suite. It does not remove the question entirely, because families often tutor Global Perspectives 0457 or an IB Middle Years project alongside it, and because the habits a student learns in a Business Studies session carry into subjects where work is submitted.

The boundary is simple to state. A tutor teaches, questions, models an answer to a different question, and gives feedback on the student's own attempt. A tutor does not supply finished answers for submission, does not edit a submitted piece into shape line by line, and does not sell assessed work. One operator in this market openly sells completed Internal Assessments; under IB and Cambridge regulations that is malpractice, and the exposure falls on the student, whose certificate is at risk, not on the seller.

The same restraint applies to material. Syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, and the right behaviour is to reference and link them rather than host or redistribute copies. A session can work through a paper your school has provided; it should not be a file-sharing service. If a tutoring site offers you a download pack of mark schemes, that is a copyright problem advertising itself.

The practical version for a Ras Al Khaimah parent: expect written feedback on your child's own scripts, expect a tutor to be able to quote the criteria a mark scheme uses, and treat any offer to produce finished written work as a reason to end the conversation. On a timeline-led plan this matters more than it sounds, because the fastest route to a wasted year is a student who reaches May having submitted work they cannot reproduce under exam conditions.

sections.heading: What Cambridge 0450 tuition costs around Ras Al Khaimah
paragraphs: Market rates are publishable, and almost nobody in this search result publishes them. The figures below are other providers' published rates, with the tier they sit in, so you can see where a quote falls rather than whether it feels expensive. They are market context and not an IB Gram price list; our own position is a free first lesson and a consultation that quotes against the plan your child actually needs.

Two structural things drive the spread. The first is travel: a visiting tutor is paid for the hour plus the journey, and in a spread-out emirate like Ras Al Khaimah the journey can be a third of the booking. The second is specialism. A graduate who can keep a Year 10 moving through Section 2 and a teacher who can mark a Paper 2 case study to the published criteria are different products at different prices, and the gap widens in the exam year because the second one is scarce.

On a timeline view, the cheapest effective purchase is almost always early and small - one weekly hour in Year 10 - and the most expensive is late and large: four sessions a week in April, which buys technique and cannot buy content. Families who start after mocks should budget for twin sessions across twelve to fourteen weeks rather than a single weekly hour, because once the weeks are short, frequency is the only variable left to pull.

Monthly package shapes seen in the market include online blocks around AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home blocks around AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

process.title: Tell us the week count, not just the subject
process.description: The first message that helps is short: year group, series the school has entered for, the last mock or report grade, and the date of the paper if you know it. That is enough to say which of the three plans applies and whether weekly or twin sessions make sense.

process.title: A free first lesson used as a diagnostic
process.description: The trial is a working session, not a sales call. The tutor sets two past questions - one data response, one six-mark evaluate - marks them live, and names which assessment objective is losing the marks. You get that assessment in writing whether or not you continue.

process.title: A written plan with dates on it
process.description: After the trial you receive a plan mapped to the weeks remaining: which syllabus sections get rebuilt, when the first timed paper lands, and what should be finished before the January mock or before study leave. It is a document you can hold the tutor to.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marking between them
process.description: Sessions run on a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, Sunday to Thursday or at the weekend. Work set in one session is marked before the next, with the marks broken down by objective so you can see whether the loss is knowledge, application, analysis or evaluation.

process.title: A re-plan at each pressure point
process.description: The plan is revisited after mocks, at the start of Ramadan if it falls in the revision run, and six weeks out. Each review can reduce frequency as well as increase it; a student who is on track in April does not need four sessions a week, and we will say so.

process.title: Change the tutor without losing the plan
process.description: If the match is wrong, say so after the second session. The diagnostic, the plan and the marked scripts move to a different tutor so the new person starts from your child's actual position rather than from a blank page.

whyPoints.title: The plan is built from a date, not a package
whyPoints.description: Most tutoring is sold in blocks of hours. A Business Studies plan starts from the week count to the paper and works backwards, which is why the first thing we ask for is the series your school has entered rather than how many hours you want to buy.

whyPoints.title: Marking against the published criteria, every week
whyPoints.description: Answers are marked the way a Cambridge examiner marks: by objective, with the missing link named. A parent gets a weekly picture of where the marks went rather than a sentence saying the session went well.

whyPoints.title: Specialism instead of proximity
whyPoints.description: Dropping the distance requirement widens the pool from whoever is free in Ras Al Khaimah to a teacher who has taught 0450 repeatedly. Lessons run over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the gain in match quality costs nothing in convenience.

whyPoints.title: Figures that carry their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed to the provider who published it, and every regulatory statement to u.ae, KHDA, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. Nothing here is a statistic we invented about ourselves.

whyPoints.title: Honest limits on what weeks can buy
whyPoints.description: We will tell you when a request is unrealistic - new content four weeks out, or eight subjects tutored at once - and what to spend the money on instead. No tutor can promise a grade, and the ones who do are describing something other than teaching.

whyPoints.title: Clear boundaries on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Teaching, questioning and feedback on your child's own attempts. Never finished answers for submission, never redistributed Cambridge papers, and no pretence that a tutoring purchase affects a Ministry equivalency decision.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the June series should 0450 tutoring start?
faqs.answer: If you want content and technique both rebuilt, start thirty weeks out, at the beginning of Year 11, with one weekly hour. If the aim is to convert a mock grade into a better final grade, twelve to sixteen weeks of twin sessions after January mocks is the realistic window. Under six weeks, the honest plan is examination technique only: command-word drill, timing and two case studies a week. Starting late is not pointless, but it changes what you are buying, and a tutor who promises the same outcome from six weeks as from thirty is not reading your calendar.

faqs.question: What is actually on Paper 1 and Paper 2 of Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 is short-answer and data-response questions drawn from all six syllabus sections, 1 hour 30 minutes, 80 marks, half the grade. Paper 2 is a case study about one named business, handed out inside the exam room, also 1 hour 30 minutes and 80 marks for the other half. Paper 1 rewards breadth of knowledge; Paper 2 rewards reading the case properly, using figures from its appendices, and finishing long answers with a supported decision. Confirm the current structure for your child's syllabus year with the school's exams officer, since Cambridge revises syllabuses on a cycle.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies split into Core and Extended tiers?
faqs.answer: No. Unlike Mathematics 0580 or the sciences, Business Studies 0450 is a single-tier syllabus: every candidate sits the same two papers and the whole grade range is available to all of them. That simplifies entry decisions and removes the tiering conversation families have about Maths. It also removes a safety net, because there is no easier paper to move down to if the year goes badly. The practical consequence is that diagnosing a problem early matters more in this subject than in a tiered one, since the only available lever later is preparation rather than entry.

faqs.question: My son sits Business Studies next June and it is already late October. Is that too late?
faqs.answer: No, but it changes the shape of the work. You have roughly thirty weeks, which is enough to revise all six sections twice, sit a mock in January, triage the weak sections in spring and still arrive at study leave with technique trained. What it is not enough for is a comfortable pace alongside two other subjects started at the same time. Pick the subject that is costing the most marks, start there with one weekly hour, and add a second subject only when the first shows a stable mark trend across three marked attempts.

faqs.question: Does 0450 have any coursework or an assessment to submit?
faqs.answer: No. Business Studies is examined entirely by the two written papers, with no coursework component and nothing to submit through the school. Families sometimes budget tutoring time for a project that does not exist in this subject, usually after confusing it with Global Perspectives 0457, which does carry an individual report, or with an IB Middle Years project. If your child's school mentions a Business Studies assignment, it is almost certainly internal school assessment rather than a Cambridge component, and it will not count towards the certificate grade.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter write long answers and still score two marks out of six?
faqs.answer: Because length is not what the mark scheme pays for. A six-mark question in 0450 usually wants a developed chain of reasoning and then a judgement that rejects the alternative. A student who writes everything they know earns the knowledge mark, perhaps one development mark, and nothing for analysis they never completed or evaluation they never attempted. The fix is mechanical and fast: identify the verb, allocate time by mark value, and write to a template per command word. Most students show a visible change on their next marked attempt within two or three sessions.

faqs.question: Which part of the 0450 syllabus costs Ras Al Khaimah students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Section 5, financial information and decisions, in most cases. It arrives late in the course, it is the least forgiving under time pressure, and it is where a correct method still loses marks for a missing unit or an untransferred figure. Section 6, external influences, runs second, usually because students treat exchange rates and government intervention as general knowledge rather than applying them to the business in front of them. Section 2, people in business, is the one students over-revise because it feels productive and rewards a fourth pass with almost nothing.

faqs.question: Does Business Studies count among the five subjects the UAE equivalency rule requires?
faqs.answer: Yes. The sourced British-track rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. Business Studies is an accredited IGCSE subject and can sit inside that count. One ranking competitor states six subjects are required; five is the figure in the sourced reporting. Verify current requirements with the Ministry of Education or the emirate attestation authority before planning around any number.

faqs.question: Can a tutor in Ras Al Khaimah teach my child the Paper 2 case study in advance?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone offering to is describing something that does not exist. In 0450 the case study is seen for the first time inside the exam room; there is no pre-release booklet for this syllabus. What a tutor can do is practise the skill the case study tests: reading three pages quickly, mapping each question to the relevant appendix, quoting the business's own figures, and finishing with a decision. Students who have worked through twelve old case studies under time walk into an unseen one with a routine, which is the only legitimate form of advance preparation available.

faqs.question: What does Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies tutoring cost around Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Market rates published by other providers run roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget online help, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to AED 500 for a visiting in-home tutor once travel is included, and AED 200 to AED 450 or more for examination-year specialists. Those are their figures, not ours. The spread is driven by travel time and by whether the tutor can mark a Paper 2 answer against published criteria. IB Gram's first lesson is free, and we quote against the plan your child needs rather than selling a fixed block.

faqs.question: My child's school has entered the November series rather than June. Does the plan change?
faqs.answer: Yes, and mostly for the better if you plan early. Cambridge runs IGCSE examinations in both a June and a November series, so a November candidate gets the long summer inside the preparation window rather than outside it. The risk is that a new school year starts in September while the paper sits in November, so the student is revising one syllabus while a timetable pushes another. Twin sessions from late August, tapering to short clinics in the exam fortnight, handles that better than a steady weekly hour. Confirm the series on the statement of entry.

faqs.question: Do we need a Business Studies tutor who actually lives in Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Not for this subject. The pool of adults within a short drive of Al Nakheel or Al Dhait who have taught 0450 to examination repeatedly is small, and insisting on proximity narrows it to whoever happens to be free. Dropping the distance requirement widens it to teachers who have marked the case study many times. IB Gram delivers lessons one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time; we do not offer home visits in the UAE, since that is a service we run only in India. The comparison to make is specialist on video against generalist in the room.

faqs.question: How do online Business Studies lessons handle cash-flow tables and calculations?
faqs.answer: With a shared whiteboard and screen sharing, which suits this subject better than it suits a practical science. A cash-flow forecast is built cell by cell on screen with the student driving, so the tutor sees the order the numbers go in rather than only the final answer. Marked scripts are shared on screen and annotated live. Students photograph handwritten attempts and send them before the session, which is how the marking turnaround stays inside a week. The one thing to arrange is a quiet room and a device with a keyboard rather than a phone.

faqs.question: What should the first session cover if the mock is three weeks away?
faqs.answer: Command words and timing, not content. Three weeks before a mock, the highest-yield hour is sorting fifteen past questions by verb, writing the opening two sentences of each, and learning to allocate minutes by mark value. The second hour should be a full timed Paper 1 section, marked hard. Content repair starts after the mock, because the mock script tells you which sections to repair and guessing before it wastes the one diagnostic you get for free. Bring the previous report and any marked work to the first session.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan interrupt a Business Studies revision plan in the northern emirates?
faqs.answer: It changes the timetable rather than stopping it, provided you plan for it. School days shorten, family routines shift, and plans built on a 16:00 weekday slot quietly stop happening. Families who move to post-Iftar sessions keep continuity through the period; families who pause for a month lose roughly a sixth of the preparation window and return to a plan that no longer fits the weeks remaining. Decide which it will be before the month starts, and tell the tutor early enough that the slot is still available when you want it back.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Ras Al Khaimah, and does it affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: The emirate's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah's authority, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. It is a broader remit than inspection alone. For tutoring, the regulator that matters more is MoHRE: individuals giving private lessons need the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and those tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask any tutor for their permit; it is a reasonable question and a quick one to answer.

intro.heading: Starting from the mark you have, not the grade you want
paragraphs: Physics is the IGCSE where a student's grade and their understanding most often disagree. A child can explain refraction clearly at the dinner table and still lose half the marks on a question about it, because 0625 does not test whether you understand physics. It tests whether you can state a definition in the words the mark scheme accepts, rearrange a formula under time pressure, read a value off a graph with a unit attached, and describe an experiment in enough detail that someone else could repeat it. Those are separate skills, and each one can be taught.

That is why this page is organised around time rather than around topics. The useful first question is not what your child finds hard, it is how many weeks remain before the paper and what the current script actually shows. A student twenty-four weeks out with a grade D mock has a different plan from one six weeks out with a grade B who keeps losing marks on the practical paper, and a sensible tutor will not offer the same course to both.

Ras Al Khaimah adds its own constraints to that arithmetic. The emirate's private-school set is small and spread between the city side around Al Nakheel, Khuzam and Al Uraibi and the southern coastal provision near Al Hamra, so the nearest physics specialist is often not near at all. Families from Mina Al Arab or Al Marjan Island who drive to a city tuition centre twice a week spend more time in the car than in the lesson, and the group class they arrive at is usually built around the maths and chemistry demand rather than physics.

IB Gram teaches every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The gain is not convenience, it is match quality: a student in Al Dhait can be taught by a tutor who teaches 0625 all week, rather than by whoever is willing to drive to Al Dhait at five in the afternoon. Physics teaches well in this format because the work is diagrams, graphs and calculations on a shared whiteboard that both people write on, and the whole board is saved afterwards.

What follows is the plan in detail: which papers your child sits at each tier, what twelve, twenty-four and seventy-two weeks of preparation can each realistically achieve, where the marks actually go in electricity, calculation and the practical paper, what the Ras Al Khaimah school year does to a revision timetable, and what the market charges in AED. Every figure quoted is attributed, and none of it is a price list for this platform. Ras Al Khaimah parents also want to know how a physics tutor handles the practical paper when nobody is in the room, and that is answered below with the mark scheme rather than with reassurance.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-physics-0.programmesIntro: Physics at sixteen is a staging post. These are the three stages either side of 0625, and what a tutor is actually doing at each one.

programmes.name: Lower secondary science, before the 0625 course begins
programmes.description: The groundwork that decides how the first 0625 term goes: units and prefixes, rearranging a two-term formula, drawing a line of best fit, measuring with a ruler and a stopwatch and knowing which digits are meaningful. Students who arrive in Year 10 unable to make kilo, milli and mega behave predictably spend the whole course losing marks they understood the physics behind.
programmes.countryNote: Across Ras Al Khaimah campuses the switch from integrated science to separate physics usually happens at the start of Year 10, and families often notice the change only when the first assessment comes back. Support at this stage is short and cheap compared with repairs later; two months of work on calculation habits in Year 9 is worth more than a term of revision in Year 11.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics
programmes.description: Six topic areas: motion, forces and energy; thermal physics; waves; electricity and magnetism; nuclear physics; and space physics. Core candidates sit a multiple-choice paper and a theory paper, Extended candidates sit the harder versions of both, and every candidate adds either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, which carries a fifth of the grade.
programmes.countryNote: Tier is decided by the centre and printed on the statement of entry, and it is the single most consequential piece of paper in the course because it sets the available grade range. In this emirate both tiers are entered, sometimes within the same class, so a parent should read the entry rather than assume the tier from the textbook on the kitchen table.

programmes.name: A Level Physics and IB Diploma Physics
programmes.description: Cambridge A Level Physics 9702 and IB Diploma Physics both assume 0625 content as given and move immediately into deeper mechanics, fields and quantum ideas, with far heavier mathematical demand. The students who struggle in the first term are rarely the ones who found 0625 hard; they are the ones who passed it by memorising answers rather than methods.
programmes.countryNote: Post-16 physics provision in the northern emirates is thinner than in Dubai, and some families move campus or commute for it. A 0625 candidate planning an engineering or medicine route should check the specific entry requirement published by the university for their intake year, because the grade and the subject combination expected differ between institutions.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-physics-0.subjectsIntro: Tutoring 0625 means teaching six topic areas plus two skill sets that cut across all of them. These are the blocks, and what each one costs a student who has not secured it.

subjects.name: Motion, forces and energy
subjects.description: Speed, acceleration, graphs of motion, Newton's laws, moments, pressure, work, power and energy transfer. The largest topic area on the syllabus and the one most students meet first. Graph interpretation here is examined all the way through the paper, so a student who cannot read a gradient loses marks in topics that have nothing to do with motion.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Particle model, thermal expansion, specific heat capacity, latent heat, conduction, convection and radiation. The explanation questions here are marked on particle-level language, and a student who writes that heat rises rather than that warmer, less dense fluid rises will lose the mark despite understanding the convection current perfectly.

subjects.name: Waves, light and sound
subjects.description: Wave properties, reflection, refraction including ray diagrams and the refractive index, dispersion, lenses, the electromagnetic spectrum and sound. Ray diagrams are drawn marks: a construction line missing an arrow or a normal drawn by eye rather than at ninety degrees costs marks that the physics itself had already earned.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Charge, current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel circuits, electrical power and energy, and circuit symbols. More 0625 marks are lost here than anywhere else, usually because a student treats a parallel branch as though it were in series, or calculates correctly in a circuit they have misread.

subjects.name: Magnetism and electromagnetic effects
subjects.description: Magnetic fields, the motor effect, electromagnetic induction, transformers and the d.c. motor. The questions reward a student who can state a rule and then apply it to the orientation actually drawn, which is a different skill from reciting the rule, and one that responds quickly to practice with varied diagrams.

subjects.name: Nuclear physics
subjects.description: Atomic structure, isotopes, alpha, beta and gamma radiation, half-life, nuclear equations and safety. A comparatively small topic with a predictable question set, which makes it reliable territory for a student who needs secure marks quickly. Half-life calculations in particular reward a method on paper rather than mental arithmetic.

subjects.name: Space physics
subjects.description: The solar system, orbits, stellar life cycles, the Big Bang and redshift. Often taught last and therefore revised least, which is why it appears disproportionately in the list of topics students say they have never seen. Teaching it takes a few hours and usually converts straight into marks.

subjects.name: Practical skills for Paper 5 and Paper 6
subjects.description: Reading instruments, tabulating results with units in the heading, plotting, drawing a best-fit line, calculating a gradient, identifying anomalies and suggesting improvements. A fifth of the grade sits here and it is examined on method and precision rather than on knowledge, which is why it is teachable in a way the theory papers are not.

subjects.name: Calculation and command-term discipline
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, handling prefixes and standard form, significant figures, unit conversion, and answering state, describe, explain, calculate and suggest with the response each command term actually wants. This is the fastest-moving part of any 0625 course, because it adds marks across all six topic areas at once.

sections.heading: Where your child is now: reading a 0625 mock properly
paragraphs: A mock percentage is the least informative number on the report. Two students on 48 per cent can need completely different courses: one has learned four topics well and never met the other two, the other half-knows everything and cannot finish a paper. The script tells you which, and it takes about fifteen minutes to read if you know what to look for. That reading is the first thing a tutor does, and it is why we ask for the marked paper rather than the grade.

Look first at whether marks were lost on questions the student attempted or on questions left blank. Blank questions at the end mean pacing; blank questions scattered through mean missing content. Then look at the calculation questions: if the method line is right and the final number is wrong, the problem is prefixes, rearrangement or significant figures, which is a week of work. If there is no method line at all, the problem is that nobody has taught the student to write one, which is cheaper still to fix.

Next, separate the explain questions from the state questions. 0625 explanation marks are awarded for a specific chain of reasoning, and students who write a true sentence that does not contain the chain get nothing for it. A tutor can show the difference in one session using two versions of the same answer side by side, and most students never lose those marks again afterwards. It is the single highest-return hour in a physics course.

Finally, check the practical questions separately from the theory. The practical component carries a fifth of the grade and is marked on method, tabulation, plotting and precision rather than on knowledge, which means a student can be strong on physics and weak on this paper, or the reverse. Scoring those questions on their own gives you a second, more honest grade, and it is usually the one that explains the gap between what you expected and what the report said.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: which papers your child actually sits
paragraphs: Cambridge examines 0625 through three components, and which versions a candidate sits depends on the tier the centre enters them for. Core candidates take a multiple-choice paper and a theory paper built on the core syllabus; Extended candidates take the harder versions of both, covering the supplementary content as well. Every candidate then adds a practical component, either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper, worth a fifth of the grade.

The decision matters because the tiers do not share a grade range. The Core route is capped below the top grades, and the Extended route does not reach the lowest ones, so entering a struggling student for Extended and a strong one for Core both carry a cost. The tier appears on the statement of entry, and it can usually still be changed before the final entry date for the series, which is why reading that document in the autumn is worth the five minutes it takes.

In practice the tier conversation in this emirate happens too late. Classes are sometimes taught with both tiers in the room, textbooks cover both, and the first time a family sees the word Extended in writing is on the entry confirmation. If you are not sure, ask the head of science two questions: which tier is my child entered for, and what mark in the next assessment would change that answer. Both have short, factual answers.

The table sets out the components for each route, with durations and weightings as published for the current syllabus. Confirm the version for your child's exam year on cambridgeinternational.org or with the school's exams officer, because component details and timings are reviewed between syllabus cycles and the entry is the document that governs.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks, twenty-four weeks, two years: what each can do
paragraphs: The honest answer to how much tutoring will help is a function of time. Physics content takes hours to teach and weeks to consolidate, and no amount of intensity compresses that below a floor. What changes with a short runway is the plan: you stop trying to cover the syllabus and start protecting the marks that are still reachable, which usually means securing three topic areas properly and drilling exam technique rather than touching all six.

A two-year runway allows the opposite approach. Topics are consolidated as they are taught, the practical paper is prepared from the first term rather than discovered in April, and calculation habits are built before they harden into errors. Families who start in Year 10 tend to use one hour a week and finish with fewer sessions overall than families who start panicking in February, which is an argument about cost as much as about grades.

The table below is the version of this conversation we have at the consultation. It is deliberately blunt about what gets dropped, because a plan that pretends everything is coverable in six weeks is how students end up thinly prepared across the whole paper rather than solidly prepared on two thirds of it. Grade predictions are not part of it: no tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does should be treated with suspicion.

One caveat specific to the northern emirates. School mock timetables, half-terms and the Ramadan adjustment to the school day all land inside these windows, so the usable number of weeks is always lower than the calendar suggests. We build the plan around the school's own calendar, which means asking for it at the start rather than discovering a two-week mock block in the middle of the rebuild.

sections.heading: Electricity and circuits: the topic that decides most grades
paragraphs: If a 0625 cohort's marks are broken down by topic, electricity is almost always the weakest column. The physics is not conceptually harder than waves or thermal, but it is unforgiving in a specific way: a student who misreads a circuit diagram does everything else correctly and still scores zero, because the error happens before the calculation starts. Diagnosing that is simple, and the repair is a drawing habit rather than a knowledge gap.

The habit we teach is redrawing. Before any calculation, the student redraws the circuit as a clean sketch, marks which components share a branch, labels the current direction, and writes the known values onto the diagram. It takes forty seconds and it converts a misreading problem into an arithmetic problem. Students resist it because it feels slow, which is why it has to be practised under timed conditions until it is faster than the alternative.

The second cluster of lost marks is conceptual: potential difference described as something that flows, current described as being used up, resistance treated as a property of the circuit rather than of the component. These misconceptions survive because they produce correct answers to easy questions, then fail on the parallel-circuit question worth five marks. A tutor who knows the standard set can find all of them in one session with four well-chosen questions.

The third is practical. Circuit questions on Paper 5 and Paper 6 ask students to describe how to measure a resistance, what to do about a reading that drifts as a component warms, and how to improve the reliability of the result. Those answers are formulaic in the good sense: there is a right way to say them, and a student who has been shown the structure scores on questions they have never seen before.

sections.heading: Paper 5 and Paper 6: practical physics taught over video
paragraphs: A fifth of the 0625 grade comes from the practical component, and it is the part families worry about most when lessons are online. The worry is misplaced for a specific reason: both versions of the component examine recording, tabulating, plotting, analysing and evaluating rather than manual dexterity. The alternative-to-practical paper is written throughout, and even the practical test awards most of its marks for how results are handled rather than for the handling of the apparatus.

Those skills teach well on a shared whiteboard. A tutor presents a set of raw readings, the student builds the table with units in the column headings, plots the points, draws the best-fit line, calculates the gradient with a large triangle, and identifies the anomaly. The tutor marks it against the published criteria while the student watches, which is the part that actually moves the score, because the criteria are specific and nobody meets them by accident.

What online teaching cannot replace is the student's own time in a school laboratory, and we say so plainly. If your child sits Paper 5, their school's practical programme is the preparation and the tutoring complements it: we work on the write-up, the precision language and the evaluation questions, which is where the marks are lost. Ask the head of science which component the centre enters candidates for, because preparation for the two differs enough to matter.

There is one practical advantage to the online format here. Every graph, table and marked attempt from a session is saved rather than left in an exercise book, so a student revising in May has a folder of their own corrected work with the criteria written beside it. In our experience that folder is the single most used revision resource a 0625 candidate ends up with, and it costs nothing extra to produce.

sections.heading: Units, prefixes and significant figures: the quiet mark drain
paragraphs: Across a 0625 paper, a surprising share of lost marks has nothing to do with physics. It is milliamps entered as amps, centimetres used where metres were needed, a density answer given in the wrong unit, an answer written to six digits because that is what the calculator said, or a formula rearranged incorrectly under pressure. Each error is worth one or two marks, and together they routinely account for a grade boundary.

The repair is drill, and it is the least glamorous part of a physics course. Ten minutes at the start of a session on prefix conversion and rearrangement, every week, until it is automatic. Students find this tedious and parents sometimes question why a tutor is doing arithmetic rather than physics, so it is worth stating the logic: these marks are available in every topic area, they require no new understanding, and they are the cheapest marks on the paper.

Command terms belong in the same category. State, describe, explain, calculate, suggest and determine each have a required response shape, and 0625 mark schemes enforce the distinction. A student who explains when asked to state wastes time; one who states when asked to explain loses marks. Teaching the six command terms explicitly, with two examples each, takes one session and pays across both theory papers.

Significant figures deserve a specific mention because the rule is simple and widely misapplied. Give the answer to the same number of significant figures as the least precise value in the question, show more digits in the working, and never round twice. A student who writes their intermediate values in full and rounds once at the end stops losing the accuracy mark, and that is a habit rather than a skill.

sections.heading: The Ras Al Khaimah school year, and where the weeks actually go
paragraphs: Private schools in Ras Al Khaimah are regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, according to the UAE government's own guidance on private schools. One practical consequence is that term dates, assessment calendars and the school day differ between campuses more than parents expect, so a revision plan has to be built from your own school's calendar rather than a generic one.

The predictable interruptions are worth planning around. Mock examinations usually occupy a block of one to two weeks and consume revision time rather than creating it. Half-term and the winter break arrive at the point in the year when a twenty-four week plan is at its most fragile. Ramadan brings a shortened school day, which changes when a student is actually able to concentrate, and for many families an evening slot after iftar works better than an afternoon one during that period.

Cambridge adds its own fixed points. Entries close months before the papers, every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer for the zone and then work from that timetable only.

Put together, a twenty-four week plan on paper is usually eighteen or nineteen usable weeks in practice. We build that in from the start, which is why the first consultation asks for the school calendar and the mock dates alongside the mark. It is also why we would rather start a plan in September with one hour a week than in February with three.

sections.heading: What 0625 support costs around Ras Al Khaimah
paragraphs: Published tutoring rates in the UAE are set in Dubai, quoted in AED, and rarely broken down. The figures below come from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, with the source named in each row. They are market rates rather than this platform's prices: IB Gram's own rate is given at the consultation, after the trial lesson, because it depends on the subject, the level and the number of sessions.

Two things distort the comparison in the northern emirates. In-person rates look lower here than in Dubai, but the specialist pool is much thinner, so the real choice is often between a general science tutor nearby and a physics specialist online rather than between two physics specialists. And in-home rates always carry travel: a visiting tutor covering twenty-five kilometres between Al Nakheel and Al Hamra is paid for that time whether the invoice itemises it or not.

Monthly packages advertised in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, with Bestimate estimating AED 240 to 600 a month for budget weekly tutoring, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Those are useful anchors for a budget conversation, with the date and source attached.

The variable nobody prices properly is the number of sessions actually needed. A student twenty-four weeks out who starts with a diagnostic and a written plan usually needs fewer total hours than one who starts six weeks out at three hours a week, so the monthly rate is a poor guide to the total. Ask any provider what the plan is, how many sessions it assumes, and what happens when the plan changes.

process.title: Send the script and the date
process.description: Two things start the conversation: the most recent marked 0625 paper and the series your child is entered for. The script shows whether the problem is content, pacing or calculation, and the series date fixes the number of weeks available. A grade on its own cannot be planned from.

process.title: A diagnostic trial lesson
process.description: One no-charge trial lesson per subject, run as a working session. The tutor tests calculation fluency, one electricity question, one explain question and one practical-skills question, then writes you three lines on what is secure, what is shaky and what has not been taught.

process.title: A written plan with the weeks counted
process.description: You receive the topic order, the session pattern, the point at which timed papers start, and an explicit note of anything being deliberately left out. The school's own mock dates and term calendar are built in, so the plan survives contact with the term rather than collapsing in week four.

process.title: Weekly lessons and a short note after each
process.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video at a fixed time in Gulf Standard Time, with everything written on a shared whiteboard and saved. Each session ends with two or three lines on what was covered and what to practise, which is also the revision list for May.

whyPoints.title: The plan is written down
whyPoints.description: You get the topic order, the number of weeks, the date timed papers start and the list of topics being dropped, in writing, before the first paid lesson. A plan that can be checked is also a plan that can be challenged, which is the point of putting it on paper rather than describing it on a call.

whyPoints.title: Matched on tier as well as subject
whyPoints.description: Core and Extended are different courses with different grade ranges, and preparation differs accordingly. We match on the tier printed on the statement of entry, which avoids the common waste of an Extended-focused tutor drilling supplementary content at a Core candidate who will never be examined on it.

whyPoints.title: Practical marks taken seriously
whyPoints.description: A fifth of the grade sits in the practical component and it is examined on tabulation, plotting, analysis and evaluation. Those are teachable over video and are built into the plan as their own strand rather than mentioned in the last fortnight when there is no time left to fix them.

whyPoints.title: Distance removed from the equation
whyPoints.description: From Mina Al Arab, Al Marjan Island or the northern strip, two centre visits a week cost more time in the car than in the lesson. Live one-to-one video returns those hours and widens the pool from tutors who will drive to your area to tutors who teach this syllabus every week.

whyPoints.title: No grade promises, attributed figures
whyPoints.description: No tutor here will promise a grade, and every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or source that published it. IB Gram is an independent matching platform with no regulator or examination-board endorsement, which is exactly what allows it to publish the market numbers plainly.

faqs.question: Is my child entered for Core or Extended 0625, and where do I check?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry from the school is the document that settles it, and the exams officer can confirm it in a sentence. Tier is not inferred from the textbook or the class, because many centres teach both tiers in one room. It matters because the two routes sit different papers and have different grade ranges: Core is capped below the top grades and Extended does not award the lowest ones. Tier can usually still be changed before the final entry date for the series, so autumn is the time to ask, not spring.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Paper 5 and Paper 6 in 0625?
faqs.answer: Paper 5 is a practical test taken with apparatus, and Paper 6 is a written alternative-to-practical paper. Both carry a fifth of the grade and both examine the same underlying skills: recording readings, tabulating with units, plotting, drawing a best-fit line, calculating a gradient, spotting anomalies and evaluating a method. Which one a candidate sits is decided by the centre, so ask the head of science. Preparation overlaps heavily, but a Paper 5 candidate also needs time with real apparatus, which is the school's laboratory programme rather than anything a tutor can substitute.

faqs.question: My daughter understands the physics but keeps losing marks on calculations. What actually fixes that?
faqs.answer: Three habits, drilled rather than explained. Writing the formula before substituting, so method marks are available even when the arithmetic fails. Converting prefixes at the point of substitution rather than hoping, which stops milliamp and kilojoule errors. And carrying full digits through the working, rounding once at the end to the significant figures the question justifies. Ten minutes a week on these for two months usually recovers more marks than a whole topic re-taught, because the gain applies to every question on both papers rather than to one topic area.

faqs.question: How many weeks of 0625 support does a student usually need before the June series?
faqs.answer: It depends far more on the starting mark than on the target. A student within one grade of target typically needs twelve weeks at two hours, mostly technique and timed papers. A student two or more grades below usually needs twenty-four weeks, because content has to be taught before it can be practised. Under six weeks the plan changes shape entirely: exam technique, the practical paper and formula fluency, with no pretence of syllabus coverage. We set the number after the diagnostic lesson rather than selling a package before anyone has read the script.

faqs.question: Is electricity genuinely the hardest part of 0625, or does it just feel that way?
faqs.answer: It is where most cohorts lose the most marks, though not because the concepts are the hardest on the syllabus. Circuit questions punish misreading: a student who treats a parallel branch as a series one performs every subsequent step correctly and still scores nothing. Add the standard misconceptions about potential difference and current, and electricity accounts for a disproportionate share of lost marks. The repair is a redrawing habit plus four diagnostic questions that expose the misconceptions, which is a fortnight of work rather than a term.

faqs.question: Can practical skills for the 0625 practical component be taught over video?
faqs.answer: The examined skills, yes. Both versions of the component award most marks for tabulating results with correct units, plotting accurately, drawing a best-fit line, calculating a gradient, identifying anomalies and suggesting improvements, and all of that works on a shared whiteboard with the tutor marking against the published criteria while the student watches. What video cannot provide is time handling apparatus, which is the school laboratory's job. For a Paper 5 candidate the two are complementary: the school supplies the practical work and the tutoring targets the recording and evaluation marks.

faqs.question: Does the Core tier limit the grade my son can achieve in physics?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the point of the tier rather than a flaw in it. The Core route is capped below the highest grades, so a candidate who needs a top grade for a post-16 physics route must be entered for Extended. The reverse also costs: an Extended entry for a student who is not secure on core content produces a thin result rather than a stretched one. The right question for the school is what mark in the next assessment would change the entry decision, and then whether the remaining weeks make that mark realistic.

faqs.question: We are five months from the paper and the 0625 mock came back very low. What is realistic?
faqs.answer: Five months at two hours a week is enough to change the result materially, provided the plan is selective. Expect the first six weeks to go on electricity, calculation habits and the practical component, because those pay across the whole paper. Expect one or two topic areas to be dropped deliberately, with that decision written down rather than drifted into. No honest tutor will name a grade at this stage, and anyone who does is selling. What you can ask for is a written plan and a review after the next assessment.

faqs.question: Does my child need maths support as well as 0625 physics support?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the diagnostic lesson usually makes it obvious. Physics at this level needs confident rearrangement of formulae, work with powers of ten and standard form, gradient calculation and proportional reasoning. A student who is comfortable in Cambridge 0580 Extended almost always has enough. A student whose physics errors are really algebra errors is better served by a short block on those specific skills inside the physics lessons than by a second subscription, and that is cheaper as well as faster.

faqs.question: How do physics lessons work during Ramadan and the shortened school day here?
faqs.answer: Schools in the emirate run a shortened day, which moves the hours when a student can actually concentrate rather than removing them. Most families switch to a later slot, commonly after iftar, and some reduce to one session a week and extend the plan instead. Because lessons are online, the change is a scheduling message rather than a renegotiated commute, which is one of the quieter advantages of the format. We ask about this at the planning stage so the plan accounts for it rather than breaking when the term shifts.

faqs.question: What does a Cambridge 0625 physics tutor cost around Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates are Dubai rates. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts specialist IGCSE and IB tutoring at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium examiner-led work. In-home visits in that table run AED 180 to 350 once travel is counted, and travel distances in this emirate are long. IB Gram's own rate is quoted at the consultation after the trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is 0625 enough preparation for A Level Physics 9702 or IB Diploma Physics?
faqs.answer: It is the assumed starting point for both, which is not the same as being sufficient. Students who struggle in the first post-16 term are usually those who passed 0625 by memorising answers rather than methods, and the gap shows up fastest in mechanics and in the mathematical handling of data. A candidate who can derive rather than recall, who writes method lines, and who is comfortable with graphs and units will find the step manageable. If post-16 physics is the plan, say so, because it changes what a tutor emphasises in Year 11.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both 0625 Physics and 0580 Maths for the same student?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and where the physics problems are really algebra problems it is the better arrangement, because the same person sees both symptoms. The limit is depth: a tutor who teaches physics all week and maths occasionally is the right choice for a student whose maths is solid, and the wrong one for a student who needs genuine 0580 Extended teaching. Tell us both subjects at the consultation and we will say honestly whether one specialist covers it or whether two shorter weekly slots serve the student better.

faqs.question: What happens if no 0625 specialist is free at the time we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with a general science tutor. In practice there are three options: a different hour on the same days, a different day, or a wait with a date attached. Which one is on offer is stated plainly along with the trade-off, because a physics specialist at an inconvenient hour usually beats a non-specialist at a convenient one for an exam-year student. If none of the three works for your family, we say that too instead of taking a booking we cannot staff properly.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our house in Al Hamra Village for physics lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. On a practical level that is also what makes a 0625 specialist available to a family on the southern coast of this emirate at all, rather than whichever tutor is willing to drive to Al Hamra Village on a weekday afternoon. Physics suits the format: diagrams, circuits, graphs and calculations live on a shared whiteboard that both people write on, and the work is saved.

intro.heading: Check the board before you book anybody
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE tutor in Ras Al Khaimah is a narrower request than most parents realise, and the narrowness is the point. Cambridge is one of at least four examined routes a sixteen-year-old in this emirate might be on. The others are Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, Oxford AQA International GCSE and, on some campuses, the UK domestic GCSE. They are different qualifications with different papers, different grading conventions and different series. A tutor who prepares a student for the wrong one is wasting your money politely.

The reason this happens often in Ras Al Khaimah rather than rarely is that the emirate's schools are varied and small. There is no single dominant provider shaping expectations the way the larger Dubai groups do. A household may have one child on Cambridge papers and a neighbour's child on Pearson, sitting what looks like the same subject at the same age. Parents compare notes in good faith and end up with the wrong past papers and the wrong mark schemes on the kitchen table.

So the first job this page does is comparison. What makes Cambridge different from the other three, on the things that change how a student should prepare: grading scale, which series are offered, how tiering works, where coursework and practical work sit, and how to verify which one your child is on. Five minutes with a statement of entry settles it, and the school office will produce one on request. Until that document is in front of you, every other decision about tutoring is provisional, including which subjects to prioritise and how many weeks the plan actually has.

The second job is the Cambridge-specific detail nobody publishes. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and the board states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. That is a real risk with a trivial fix, and no competitor page in this market mentions it. Entry deadlines also sit months before the papers: for the Cambridge March 2027 series the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027 while final entries were due 27 November 2026.

The rest of the page covers Core and Extended and the ceiling the tier sets, where Cambridge marks actually go missing, how practical science is examined for a candidate without laboratory access, what support costs in dirhams around this emirate, and the Ministry of Education equivalency rule that counts five subjects rather than six. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are an India-only service, and saying so is more useful than implying otherwise.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses assessed by externally marked papers, with syllabuses identified by a four-digit code such as 0580 for mathematics, 0620 for chemistry, 0625 for physics and 0610 for biology. Many subjects are tiered Core or Extended, with the tier setting a ceiling on the achievable grade. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah, Cambridge entries are spread across a small set of campuses rather than concentrated in one group, so the first useful step for a parent is a statement of entry from the school office showing the syllabus codes. Several of our enquiries from this emirate begin with a family who has been revising from the wrong board's papers for a term.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other main international route, with its own syllabus codes such as 4MA1 for mathematics, and examinations available in May or June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah families moving between campuses sometimes change board mid-course, which is manageable but needs planning: the content overlaps heavily while the paper structure, the tiering language and the formula provision do not. A term of targeted technique work usually closes the difference.

programmes.name: International A Level and the IB Diploma
programmes.description: The two routes a Cambridge IGCSE student in this emirate continues into at sixteen. Cambridge runs International A Level examinations in the same June and November series as IGCSE. The IB Diploma runs on a small number of Ras Al Khaimah campuses and assesses a mixture of externally marked papers and internally assessed work moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: The Core and Extended decision in Year 10 reaches this far. A Core mathematics candidate is not well placed for either an International A Level in mathematics or Higher Level mathematics in the Diploma, so the tier decision is effectively a sixth-form decision taken two years early.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Cambridge requests from Ras Al Khaimah cluster in mathematics and the sciences, where tiering and practical assessment create the most confusion. Each subject below names the syllabus code and where the marks actually go.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, vectors, probability and statistics, tiered Core or Extended with a different grade ceiling on each. Marks disappear in multi-step questions where working is not shown, in algebraic manipulation under time pressure, and in the failure to use the formula provision the paper allows. Extended candidates lose most in the final questions, which are reachable with practice.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for a mathematics-heavy sixth form, covering calculus, further trigonometry and series. It is the single best preparation for Higher Level mathematics in the Diploma or an International A Level. Students who arrive at it without secure algebra from 0580 struggle, so the sequencing matters more than enthusiasm.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Particles, bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases, electrochemistry, energetics, rates and organic chemistry. Mole calculations with units carried correctly are the highest-value repair available. Extended-only content, including more demanding electrolysis and organic work, is where a Core-prepared student hits a wall if the tier was changed late.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Motion, forces, energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity, magnetism and atomic physics. Students lose marks writing descriptions where an explanation naming a principle was asked for, and in graph questions where a gradient is calculated but not interpreted. Equation rearrangement under time is a technique problem, not a content one.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Characteristics of living organisms, cells, enzymes, transport, respiration, coordination, reproduction, inheritance and ecology. Precision in vocabulary earns marks that approximate answers do not: diffusion, osmosis and active transport have to be distinguished exactly. Data questions on Paper 4 reward reading the axes carefully before writing anything.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing plus composition, assessed on comprehension, summary and writing for a stated audience and purpose. The summary question is the most teachable high-value component on the paper, because it rewards selection and concision rather than knowledge, and most students lose marks by copying rather than compressing.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: The basic economic problem, allocation of resources, microeconomic decision makers, government and the macroeconomy, international trade and development. Diagram accuracy, labelled fully, carries marks students routinely forgo, and evaluation questions need a judgement that follows from the analysis rather than a restated list of both sides.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Business activity, people in business, marketing, operations and finance, assessed partly through case-study material. Candidates lose marks by describing a business instead of applying a named concept to the evidence supplied and then recommending with a reason. Calculation questions on finance are reliably available marks that go unclaimed.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Computer systems and algorithms with programming, assessed by written papers rather than coursework. Pseudocode written to the board's own conventions earns marks that fluent Python does not, and trace tables are a procedural skill that can be drilled quickly. Binary, hexadecimal and data representation questions are predictable and worth securing early.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE must provide Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, with separate provision for Arabic speakers and non-Arabic speakers. These sit beside a Cambridge timetable rather than inside it, and the stream the school placed the student in determines which support is useful.

sections.heading: Cambridge against the three other boards a Ras Al Khaimah family meets
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, Oxford AQA International GCSE and the UK domestic GCSE are four qualifications that look interchangeable from outside and are not. They differ in the grading convention used, in which series are available, in how tiering works, in whether coursework or a practical examination forms part of the assessment, and in the formula and data provision given in the paper. Each of those changes how a student should revise.

Verification takes five minutes and is the single most valuable thing a parent can do before spending anything. Ask the school office for a statement of entry. It lists the board and the syllabus code for every subject the student is entered for. A code of four digits beginning with a zero, such as 0580 or 0625, is Cambridge. A code like 4MA1 is Pearson. If a statement of entry does not exist yet because the entries have not been made, ask the head of year which board the department teaches and get the answer in writing.

The reason this matters so much here is that Ras Al Khaimah has no single dominant school group setting a default. Campuses are small and varied, and families compare notes across schools in good faith. We regularly meet students who have spent a term working through the wrong board's past papers, which does some good by accident and leaves the specific paper structure they will actually face unpractised.

Where a child genuinely has changed board mid-course, the work is manageable and specific. The content overlap between Cambridge and Pearson in mathematics and the sciences is large. What differs is paper structure, the wording of command terms, the tiering arrangement and what the formula sheet gives you. A term of technique work closes that gap in most subjects, and it should be scoped as a defined block rather than treated as starting the subject again.

sections.heading: Administrative zones: the Cambridge rule that decides your child's exam times
paragraphs: Here is a Cambridge-specific fact that no competing page in this market publishes and that can cost a candidate a paper. Cambridge states that every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam as a result of using the wrong zone timetable. Zones exist so that papers are sat within a sensible window across a planet of time zones.

The practical risk is mundane and real. A parent searches for the subject timetable, finds a version, and builds the revision plan and the morning logistics around it. If the version found belongs to a different zone, the times are wrong. Families who have moved from another country are especially exposed, because they often recall the pattern from a previous centre and assume it carries over.

The fix costs nothing. Ask the examinations officer at your child's school which zone the centre is in, then use only the timetable version for that zone, downloaded from the board's own site rather than from a revision forum. Print it. Mark each paper with its date, start time and duration, and check it again a fortnight before the series begins in case anything has been revised.

Pearson candidates have an equivalent discipline for a slightly different reason. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and those can be revised before the final version, so a date taken from a provisional document early in the year may not be the date the paper is sat. The rule in both cases is the same: take dates from the board's live official timetable and verify them again close to the series, rather than trusting a figure copied onto a page like this one.

sections.heading: Core and Extended: one syllabus, two papers, two ceilings
paragraphs: Several Cambridge subjects are tiered. A tiered syllabus contains a Core curriculum and an Extended curriculum, and the papers a candidate sits depend on which route the school entered them for. The important consequence is a ceiling: a Core candidate cannot reach the top grades available on the Extended route, regardless of how well they perform. That ceiling is set by a decision usually taken in Year 10 and often not explained to parents at the time.

The decision is reasonable in both directions. A student placed on Extended who cannot cope with the additional content loses marks across the whole paper and may end up below where a confident Core performance would have left them. A student placed on Core who was capable of Extended carries a cap they did not need. Schools make this judgement from classwork, and they are usually right, but it is a judgement rather than a measurement.

What a parent should do is specific. Ask, in writing, which tier the child is entered for in each tiered subject, when that decision is reviewed, and what evidence would change it. Then ask what grade range each tier makes available. If the answer is that Core caps below the grade a sixth-form route requires, the conversation needs to happen now rather than in Year 11, because the Extended-only content takes months rather than weeks to cover.

Where a family decides to move a student up a tier, the work is definable. In 0580 mathematics it is the Extended-only algebra, functions, trigonometry and probability content. In 0620 chemistry it is the more demanding electrolysis, stoichiometry and organic material. In 0625 physics it is the extension content across the topics already met. A specialist can list exactly what is additional and plan it across a year, which is a very different purchase from general subject tutoring.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. What families consistently underestimate is how far ahead the administration sits. The board's published key dates for the March 2027 series are a clean illustration: the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due 27 November 2026, forecast grades were due 27 February 2027, results are issued on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June.

Read that sequence again as a parent rather than as an administrator. The entry deadline sits more than two months before the first paper. By the time a family notices in January that a subject is in trouble, the entry decision, including the tier, has already been made and may be difficult to change. That single fact is the strongest argument for having the tier conversation in Year 10 rather than in the spring of Year 11.

Pearson publishes its own equivalent dates and they behave the same way. The November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Provisional timetables are published ahead of each series and can be revised, so the live official timetable is the only one worth planning from.

The planning exercise that actually helps is dull and effective. Take the school calendar and the board timetable for your zone. Mark the entry deadline, the mock window, the start of exam leave, the first paper in each subject, the results date and the deadline for asking the school about a review of marking. Then count the usable weeks between now and the first paper, subtracting holidays and the Ramadan period. The number is always smaller than it felt, and it is the number any honest plan has to work with.
