sections.heading: Where Cambridge marks go missing, question type by question type
paragraphs: Marks on a Cambridge paper are allocated against a mark scheme written in particular language, and a large share of the marks students lose are available to them. The pattern repeats across subjects. A question asks for an explanation and receives a description. A question asks the candidate to calculate and the answer appears with no working, so a method mark that survived an arithmetic slip is lost too. A graph question asks what the gradient represents and gets the gradient's value.

Command words are the lever. State, describe, explain, compare, calculate, determine, suggest and evaluate each demand a different shape of answer and a different quantity of writing. Students who have never had these set out side by side write at a uniform length and are rewarded unevenly. Half an hour spent sorting past-paper questions by command word, then writing one answer of each shape, changes performance measurably. It is the cheapest intervention available in a Cambridge subject.

The second lever is the mark scheme itself. Reading one as a marker reads it is a revelation for most students: marks attach to specific words and specific statements, not to general correctness, and the scheme frequently rewards a point the student knew but did not write. Practising with the scheme beside the paper, marking their own work and arguing about whether a point earned the mark, is a more productive hour than passively reading notes.

The third is timing, which is a skill rather than a trait. A student who runs out of time on Paper 4 is not short of knowledge; they have allocated minutes badly, usually by over-writing early questions. Timed sections, then full papers, with the clock visible and a mark-per-minute target, fixes this inside a few weeks. None of these three repairs needs new content, which is why a technique block before a series frequently recovers more marks than a term of teaching.

sections.heading: Paper 5 and Paper 6: how practical science is examined
paragraphs: Cambridge science syllabuses assess practical skills, and the route differs between centres. Some candidates sit a practical test; others sit an alternative-to-practical written paper that examines the same skills through described experiments, apparatus diagrams, tables of results and sources of error. Which route your child is on is a centre decision, and it determines a meaningful share of the grade, so it belongs on the same list as the board and the tier.

The alternative-to-practical paper is widely misunderstood as the easier option. It is not: it tests exactly the reasoning a laboratory session should have produced, in writing, under time. Candidates are asked to read a described method and identify the variable that was not controlled, to complete a results table with consistent significant figures and correct units, to plot points accurately and draw a line of best fit, and to name a specific source of error and a practical improvement. Each of those is a trainable skill.

For a student working with an online tutor, this is straightforward to teach and arguably easier than in a crowded laboratory, because the written reasoning is the assessed object. A shared screen, a described experiment, a blank results table and a graph grid cover the whole skill set. What cannot be replicated remotely is the handling of apparatus, and that stays where it belongs: with the school, which runs the practical programme and, where applicable, the practical test.

The honest division of labour is worth stating. The school supplies the laboratory work, the apparatus and the supervised practical assessment. A tutor supplies the written reasoning around it: experimental design, control of variables, significant figures, units, graph work, error analysis and improvement. For candidates on the alternative-to-practical route, that written reasoning is the assessment itself, which makes it among the most efficient things to work on before a series.

sections.heading: What Cambridge IGCSE support costs around Ras Al Khaimah, and what changes it
paragraphs: Published rates in dirhams are rare in this market, so here are the market bands with the source of each. These are market figures and not an IB Gram price list. Our arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and the plan price depends on the subject, the tier and the weeks remaining before the series.

Budget online and university-student tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit roughly AED 150 to AED 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. In-home visiting tutors, travel inside the rate, run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 according to Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table and advertised home-tutor rates. IGCSE and IB specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium named tutors higher again, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Monthly figures appear as well: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four in-home two-hour sessions.

Six things move the figure for a Cambridge candidate specifically, and the tier is the one parents never anticipate. Extended work in a tiered subject draws on a smaller pool of tutors than Core work. Proximity to a series raises demand sharply from February and again in October. Session length changes the per-hour rate in both directions. A second child on a different board does not halve the cost, because the preparation is genuinely different. A scarce subject, Additional Mathematics 0606 being the usual example in the northern emirates, prices above a common one. And travel, for visiting tutors only, is inside the quoted number whether or not it is itemised.

Set this against the rest of the education bill rather than in isolation. School fees dominate, and in Dubai the Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Examination entries, revision guides and a scientific or graphical calculator are smaller lines but real. Deciding which two subjects get supported, rather than spreading thin across five, is usually the decision that makes the budget work.

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E or 3: the equivalency rule a competitor gets wrong
paragraphs: A Cambridge IGCSE student planning to apply to a UAE institution will usually need an equivalency certificate from the Ministry of Education, and the published British-track rule is clearer than most families expect. Reporting on the ministry's clarification in July 2026 set out that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and must additionally show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details in that rule matter and are regularly got wrong. First, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, so a student counting them towards the total may be a subject short without knowing. Second, the count is five, not six. At least one competitor currently ranking for UAE tutoring queries states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. Publishing the sourced figure is a small thing that happens to beat a ranking page on accuracy.

For the American track, the same reporting set out English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. No IB points threshold appears on this page because none has been read on the ministry's own site, and a number that cannot be sourced should not be published at all, let alone across many pages.

What this means in practice for a Ras Al Khaimah family is sequencing. Confirm which five subjects will count, check that the subject combination leaves the sixth-form route open, and start the attestation paperwork before results rather than after. Equivalency is a process the family completes through the official channel; IB Gram does not perform it, guarantee it, or speed it up, and nobody should imply that tutoring is required for it. Tutoring affects grades, and nothing else in that list.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is sitting Cambridge or another board?
faqs.answer: Ask the school office for a statement of entry. It lists the board and the syllabus code for every subject. A four-digit code beginning with a zero, such as 0580 for mathematics or 0625 for physics, is Cambridge; an alphanumeric code like 4MA1 is Pearson. If entries have not been made yet, ask the head of year or the department for written confirmation of which board it teaches. This takes five minutes and it is the first thing to settle, because a term of practice on the wrong board's papers rehearses the wrong paper structure.

faqs.question: What are Cambridge administrative zones, and why would they affect our exam day?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones so that papers are sat in sensible local windows. The board states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. The practical risk is a family planning around a timetable downloaded for a different zone. Ask your examinations officer which zone your centre is in, use only that version from the board's own site, and check it again a fortnight before the series.

faqs.question: Does Core instead of Extended limit the grade my child can get?
faqs.answer: Yes. A tiered Cambridge syllabus has a Core curriculum and an Extended curriculum, and the papers sat depend on the entry. A Core candidate cannot reach the top grades available on the Extended route however well they perform. The decision is normally made by the school in Year 10 from classwork, and it is a judgement rather than a measurement. Ask in writing which tier your child is entered for, when it is reviewed, what evidence would change it, and what grade range each tier makes available. The entry deadline sits months before the papers.

faqs.question: My child moved from a Pearson school to a Cambridge school mid-course. How much work is that?
faqs.answer: Less than it sounds, and it should be scoped as a defined block rather than treated as starting again. In mathematics and the sciences the content overlap between the two boards is large. What differs is paper structure, command-word wording, the tiering arrangement and what the formula or data provision gives you in the paper. A term of targeted technique work usually closes the gap: the student practises the structure they will actually face, with that board's mark schemes. Get the new syllabus codes first, then build the block around the components that differ.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper, and is it easier than a practical test?
faqs.answer: It is a written paper that assesses practical skills through described experiments: identifying an uncontrolled variable, completing a results table with consistent significant figures and units, plotting accurately, drawing a line of best fit, naming a specific source of error and suggesting a practical improvement. It is not easier, it is different, and it tests the reasoning a laboratory session should have produced. Which route a candidate sits is a centre decision, so confirm it with the school. For an online tutor it is straightforward to teach, because the written reasoning is the assessed object.

faqs.question: How far in advance does Cambridge close entries for a series?
faqs.answer: Months ahead. The board's published key dates for the March 2027 series show the exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. The gap between the entry deadline and the first paper is more than two months. That is why a tier conversation belongs in Year 10 and not in the spring of Year 11, by which point the entry including the tier has already been submitted.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge syllabus codes should I actually check on the statement of entry?
faqs.answer: The ones where tiering or sequencing changes the plan. Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core or Extended, as are chemistry 0620, physics 0625 and biology 0610. Additional Mathematics 0606 is a separate syllabus taken alongside 0580 by students heading for mathematics-heavy sixth-form study. English as a First Language 0500, Economics 0455, Business Studies 0450 and Computer Science 0478 are single-tier. Knowing the code lets a tutor work from the board's own syllabus document and specimen papers rather than a generic subject outline, which is the difference that shows in marks.

faqs.question: What do Cambridge tutors cost around Ras Al Khaimah?
faqs.answer: Market rates, not ours. Budget online and university-student tutoring runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Visiting in-home tutors run AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate, per Bestimate's 2026 table. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above. Extended-tier and scarce subjects such as 0606 price higher, and demand rises from February and October.

faqs.question: Do we need to take six IGCSE subjects for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. Reporting on the Ministry of Education's July 2026 clarification states that British-curriculum students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor states six, which is a useful reminder to verify anything of this kind on the official channel rather than on a tutoring page, including this one.

faqs.question: Will a Cambridge tutor come to our house in Al Nakheel or Al Dhait?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Ras Al Khaimah families run one-to-one over live video with a shared screen and a document both sides can write on, which suits examination work particularly well because a script, a mark scheme and a graph grid can all be on screen at once. If having an adult physically in the room is the requirement, a local visiting tutor or a tuition centre in Al Dhait is the better purchase and we would say so.

faqs.question: My child runs out of time on Paper 4. Is that a content problem?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Running out of time is almost always an allocation problem: too many minutes spent on early questions, often over-writing short-answer responses that could not earn more marks. It responds quickly to a specific drill. Practise timed sections before whole papers, work to a marks-per-minute target, and mark the student's own script against the scheme so they can see where the extra writing earned nothing. Three or four weeks of this recovers marks that another month of content teaching would not touch, and it transfers across subjects.

faqs.question: Which two subjects should we support if the budget will not stretch to five?
faqs.answer: Pick on two criteria rather than on which feels hardest. First, load-bearing: which grades does the sixth-form or Diploma place actually require, and which subject is closest to falling below that. Second, recoverable: a subject losing marks to technique, timing or command words recovers faster than one with two years of missing content. Mathematics and one science is the most common sensible pair from this emirate. Spreading one hour a fortnight across five subjects reliably produces less movement than one hour a week across two.

faqs.question: Does the school's practical programme still matter if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the division of labour should be explicit. The school supplies the laboratory work, the apparatus and any supervised practical assessment, and nothing remote replaces handling equipment. A tutor supplies the written reasoning around it: experimental design, control of variables, significant figures and units, graph work, error analysis and improvements. For candidates on the alternative-to-practical route, that written reasoning is the assessment itself, so the online work is directly on the assessed object rather than adjacent to it.

faqs.question: When in the two years is the best time to start Cambridge support?
faqs.answer: The autumn term of Year 10 if the tier decision matters, and the autumn term of Year 11 if it is technique. Both are cheaper and more effective than the spring before a series, when demand concentrates and the usable weeks are few. Count backwards honestly: take the board timetable for your centre's zone, mark the entry deadline, the mock window, exam leave and the first paper, then subtract holidays and the Ramadan weeks. What remains is the number a plan has to work with, and it is always smaller than it feels.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is available for the Cambridge subject we need?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date. The requests that most often cannot be filled immediately in the northern emirates are Additional Mathematics 0606 and Extended-tier sciences close to a series. In that case we will name when a matched tutor becomes available, offer support on an adjacent component where that is genuinely useful, or say the request cannot be served well and suggest looking locally. No competitor in the researched set publishes a coverage limit, and concealing one costs a family weeks they cannot get back before a fixed exam date.

ras-al-khaimah/cambridge-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Almost every avoidable mistake in this market starts with a parent not knowing the board, the code, the tier or the practical route. Get the statement of entry from the school office, confirm the tier in writing for each tiered subject, ask the examinations officer which Cambridge zone your centre sits in, and download the right timetable version. If after that a specific subject still needs a specialist, send a recent marked script and take the free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the course. You will get a written opinion on where the marks are going and an honest answer about how many of them are recoverable in the weeks that remain.

intro.heading: A Diploma cohort in this emirate is small, and that changes every answer
paragraphs: An IB Diploma tutor in Ras Al Khaimah is usually needed for a reason that would not arise further south. The emirate's private-school set is concentrated around Al Nakheel, Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab, and the number of campuses running the full Diploma is small. Where a Dubai school might run four Higher Level chemistry sets and timetable them against three different option blocks, a Ras Al Khaimah school runs one set or none. A student who wants Higher Level physics and Higher Level economics may find the timetable simply does not allow both.

That arithmetic produces three recurring situations. The first is a student taking a subject at Standard Level who needed Higher Level for a degree route, and who now has to cover the extra material somewhere. The second is a student in a set of eight where a single mid-year staff change removes the only specialist on campus. The third is a student whose chosen subject was never offered, who is studying it with a teacher covering outside their field or self-studying towards a May entry. None of those are failures by the school; they are what a small cohort costs.

The regulator here is not the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, and that matters more than most tutoring pages admit. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge. The federal portal states that the Ras Al Khaimah authority regulates private education in the emirate, and that the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. So when a school here adds the Diploma, changes a fee or revises how it assesses, a body inside this emirate has approved it.

The calendar is local too. Ras Al Khaimah schools sit the May session, and the weeks that matter are set by their own term dates, their internal coursework deadlines and the fortnights the UAE academic year removes. Ramadan shifts the usable study evening. Exam leave starts earlier than families expect. A plan built from a generic Dubai timeline will miss the two or three weeks where a Diploma student in this emirate actually has capacity to change something.

What this page does is set out the Diploma as a Ras Al Khaimah student meets it: the option-block reality, the internal assessment that decides a large share of each grade, the local calendar counted backwards, the Ministry of Education equivalency route and the universities inside the emirate, the academic-honesty boundary when one supervisor covers a whole year group, and what support costs in dirhams. Lessons are delivered online over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service, and we would rather state it than imply otherwise.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-diploma-tutor.programmesIntro: Three programmes matter to a Ras Al Khaimah Diploma family: the Diploma itself, the Middle Years Programme that feeds it on continuum campuses, and the IGCSE route most of the emirate's other schools run into sixteen.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subject groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus three core elements: the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and creativity, activity, service. Each subject carries internally assessed work marked by the school and moderated by the IB, alongside externally marked examinations. Subjects are graded one to seven, with additional points available from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination.
programmes.countryNote: In Ras Al Khaimah the Diploma runs on a small number of campuses, so option blocks are tight and a Higher Level set may have single figures in it. The practical consequence is that subject choice is constrained by the timetable rather than by the student's preference, and the gap that creates is the commonest reason a family here looks for outside support.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The five-year programme preceding the Diploma on continuum campuses, assessed against four published criteria per subject on a one to eight scale rather than by examination. Students arriving into Year 12 from MYP 5 have usually never sat a timed external paper, so the first term of the Diploma is a change in assessment format as much as in content difficulty.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah continuum campuses move students from MYP 5 into Year 12 with the same staff and the same buildings, which masks how different the assessment becomes. The mathematics pathway chosen in MYP 4 is the decision that most often determines whether Higher Level mathematics is available two years later on a small timetable.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: The examined route into sixteen that most Ras Al Khaimah schools run, assessed by externally marked papers in a June or November series. Cambridge syllabuses are tiered Core or Extended and Pearson offers tiering in some subjects, with the tier setting a ceiling on the achievable grade. The five-subject count at grade E or 3 is what the Ministry of Education uses for equivalency on the British track.
programmes.countryNote: Students crossing from an IGCSE stream into a Ras Al Khaimah Diploma cohort arrive with strong examination technique and no experience of internally assessed investigation work. The first Internal Assessment is where that shows, and it is the most profitable thing to work on in the first term of Year 12.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-diploma-tutor.subjectsIntro: Diploma support requests from this emirate cluster heavily in mathematics and the sciences at Higher Level, because those are the sets a small school can least afford to staff twice. Each subject below names what is actually assessed internally and where marks go.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with an internally assessed exploration carrying a published share of the grade. Higher Level adds depth in calculus and proof that Standard Level does not touch. Marks are lost in extended response questions where a correct method stops short of an interpreted answer, and in the exploration where personal engagement and mathematical communication are thin.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led methods, with the same exploration requirement. The Higher Level course expects confident use of a graphical calculator for problems that cannot be done by hand. Students who treat it as the easier route and then meet the statistics content late in Year 13 are the commonest repair job we are asked to take on.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, electricity, fields, energy and the additional Higher Level depth, with an internally assessed scientific investigation. Examination marks go missing in questions requiring a graph gradient to be interpreted physically rather than calculated, and in explanations that describe a result instead of accounting for it using a named principle.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure, reactivity, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic chemistry, plus the internally assessed investigation. Mole arithmetic with units carried correctly, and clear uncertainty treatment in practical write-ups, are the two highest-value repairs. Organic mechanisms reward pattern recognition that can be drilled in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, molecular biology, genetics, ecology, physiology and the Higher Level extensions, with an internally assessed investigation. The marks sit in data analysis and in command-term discipline: an answer that describes a trend when the question asked for an explanation earns part of the credit at best, which students repeat for two years unless it is named.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy, with internally assessed commentaries on published news articles against real economic theory. Diagrams drawn accurately and labelled fully carry marks that students routinely forgo, and the commentary word limit is enforced, so editing to length is part of the skill.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisational structure, human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with internally assessed written work based on real or supplied organisational data. Higher Level adds depth and a longer research requirement. Students lose marks by describing a business rather than applying a named tool to evidence and reaching a supported judgement.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Non-literary and literary texts studied together, assessed through examinations, an individual oral and, at Higher Level, an essay. The oral is the component students prepare least and panic about most; it rewards a global issue stated precisely and extracts chosen because they evidence it rather than because they are familiar.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems, computational thinking, programming and the internally assessed solution with its documentation. The documentation, not the program, is what is marked, so a working product with a thin design and testing record scores poorly. That single fact changes how most students allocate their time once it is explained.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay, combined with the Extended Essay for additional points. Students who treat it as opinion writing stall; the marks attach to knowledge questions handled with real examples and a counter-position taken seriously. It is coachable, and it is the core element most often left until too late.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A four-thousand-word independent research essay in a chosen subject with a school supervisor. Most lost marks are structural: a research question too broad to answer in the length, a method section missing, and a conclusion that summarises rather than answers. A tutor may coach the process and respond to the student's own drafts, never supply content.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Language B or ab initio, plus mandatory provision
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the Diploma for UAE students as a federal requirement, with separate provision for Arabic speakers and non-Arabic speakers. A Diploma student may also take Arabic as a Language B or ab initio subject, which is a different course from the mandatory provision, and support must be matched to whichever the school has placed them in.

sections.heading: Option blocks in a small cohort, and the subjects a timetable quietly removes
paragraphs: The first thing to establish about a Ras Al Khaimah Diploma is which subjects the timetable actually permits together. A Diploma student picks one subject from each of six groups, three at Higher Level. On a large campus the same subject runs in two or three blocks, so most combinations are possible. On a campus with a Diploma cohort in the tens, each subject runs once, which means two subjects sitting in the same block are mutually exclusive no matter how much a student wants both.

Families discover this at the point of choosing, usually in the spring of MYP 5 or Year 11, and the consequences land eighteen months later. A student aiming at engineering who could not fit Higher Level physics alongside Higher Level mathematics is now applying with Standard Level physics. A student who wanted economics and business management will have been told to pick one. These are not errors; they are what one teaching set per subject produces.

There are three legitimate responses and it is worth knowing them before accepting the first one offered. The school may be able to run a subject with a very small group, sometimes by timetabling it against a study period, and it is reasonable to ask. A student may sit a subject as an additional entry with school agreement, which requires real self-discipline and a teacher willing to supervise. Or the student takes the Standard Level option and covers the Higher Level gap deliberately, which is the situation most of our Ras Al Khaimah Diploma work addresses.

What none of those responses tolerates is vagueness. If a university route expects Higher Level mathematics and the timetable gives Standard Level, the gap needs naming in content terms, not in reassurance. Ask the school for the written option blocks and the subjects in each. Ask which degree routes the current combination closes. Then decide whether to argue with the timetable or to cover the gap, because doing neither is the expensive option.

sections.heading: What the Department of Knowledge approves at your child's school
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah is one of the emirates with its own education regulator rather than federal supervision, and the scope of that regulator is wider than many parents assume. The federal portal states that the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate, and that the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Each of those nouns is a real power, and together they cover most of what a parent might want to question.

That has concrete uses. If a school announces a fee change, the approving authority is identifiable and the question of whether approval was given is a fair one. If a school proposes to add or withdraw a programme, that is a regulated decision rather than a purely internal one. If the way a year group is assessed changes mid-course, the same applies. None of this makes a school's decision wrong; it means there is an accountable route beyond the head teacher's office.

It also sets the geography of your child's documents. Ras Al Khaimah schools answer to the Department of Knowledge, Dubai schools to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain schools to the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah schools to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah schools to the federal Ministry of Education. Families who have moved north from Dubai often expect a Dubai-style published inspection portal and are surprised when the route is different.

One boundary should be stated flatly. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence, registration or partnership from the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, from any other emirate regulator, from the Ministry of Education, or from the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. A permit to run a tutoring institute with premises is a specific instrument issued to training institutes in Dubai, and we do not hold one or operate a UAE centre. Any tutoring page implying regulator endorsement is making a claim worth checking.

sections.heading: Internal assessment: the marks decided before the examination room
paragraphs: A meaningful share of every Diploma subject grade is settled by work marked inside the school and moderated by the IB. The share differs by subject and level, and the school publishes it in the course outline. What matters for a student in a small Ras Al Khaimah cohort is that this is the part of the grade least affected by class size and most affected by whether anyone has explained the criteria properly.

The tasks differ sharply in character. The mathematics exploration is an individual piece of mathematics the student chose, rewarded for engagement, mathematical presentation and reflection as well as correctness. The sciences require an individual investigation with a research question, a method the student designed, and uncertainty handled honestly. Economics requires commentaries built on published articles within a strict word limit. English requires an individual oral built around a global issue. Computer science marks the documentation rather than the program.

The failure patterns are consistent and almost all of them are structural rather than intellectual. A research question too broad to answer in the word count. A method with an uncontrolled variable nobody noticed until the data was collected. A conclusion that restates the hypothesis instead of evaluating it against the evidence. A word limit exceeded, so the final section goes unread. An oral built on extracts the student liked rather than extracts that evidence the stated issue. Every one of those is visible in a first draft and fixable before submission.

That is precisely where coaching has the highest return and the tightest ethical boundary. A tutor may teach the criteria, interrogate a research question until it is answerable, point at an uncontrolled variable, ask what the data actually supports, and respond to a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not contribute content, rewrite passages, or produce any part of assessed work. The student's result depends on that boundary being kept, so we keep a written record of what was done in each session.

sections.heading: The Ras Al Khaimah academic year, counted backwards from a May session
paragraphs: Ras Al Khaimah schools sit the May session, and the useful planning exercise is to count backwards from it using this emirate's own term dates rather than a generic timeline. Every school publishes its calendar; print it and mark four things on it: internal coursework deadlines, the mock window, exam leave, and the weeks that are gone because of public holidays and Ramadan. What remains is the capacity a plan can actually use, and it is always less than a parent assumes.

The autumn term of Year 13 is where most of the internal assessment work should finish. Schools set their own internal deadlines for the Extended Essay, the explorations and the investigations, and those deadlines sit months before anything is uploaded. A student who treats the school deadline as negotiable loses the one period in the two years with genuine slack. Supervisors in a small cohort are carrying a dozen essays each, so a late draft gets less attention than an early one, which is a practical argument for finishing first rather than best.

The spring term is examination technique and content consolidation, and it is shorter than it looks. Ramadan moves the usable study evening and the school day compresses; families who plan around iftar timing keep their sessions and families who do not lose a month. Mocks usually land in January or February and are the most under-used data in the year: they produce a question-level picture of where marks are going that is worth more than the grade printed on the front.

For a comparison of how far ahead administrative deadlines sit, the Cambridge board publishes its own key dates, and they are instructive even for an IB family. For the Cambridge March 2027 series the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026 and forecast grades due 27 February 2027. That is an entry deadline more than two months before the first paper. IB session and results dates are not published on this page because they must be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator or on the IB's own site, and we will not restate a date we have not verified.

sections.heading: Equivalency, attestation and the university routes inside this emirate
paragraphs: A Diploma certificate is accepted widely, but a student applying to a UAE institution usually needs an equivalency certificate from the Ministry of Education, and the process is the family's to complete rather than a school's or a tutor's. It is worth starting the paperwork before results rather than after, because document attestation takes time and the application windows at UAE universities do not wait.

The published rules differ by curriculum and the British track is the one documented most clearly. Reporting on the ministry's clarification in July 2026 set out that British-curriculum students must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five. That five-subject rule is worth knowing because at least one ranking competitor publishes six.

For the American track the same reporting set out English proficiency at a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics at a minimum 450 in SAT Math before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold published on this page, because we have not read one on the ministry's own site and we will not repeat a figure we cannot source. Ask the ministry or the emirate's attestation channel directly, and ask your school's coordinator what previous cohorts needed.

Ras Al Khaimah students also have degree options without leaving the emirate, which changes the calculus for some families. The American University of Ras Al Khaimah, RAK Medical and Health Sciences University and University of Stirling RAK all operate here, and each publishes its own admission requirements, including which mathematics route it expects. That last point matters more than most: a student heading for an engineering or health-sciences route should check whether Analysis and Approaches is expected before accepting an Applications and Interpretation place in the timetable.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when one supervisor covers the whole year group
paragraphs: A Diploma cohort of thirty gives one teacher the supervision of several Extended Essays, and the same teacher may also be the only subject specialist marking that subject's internal assessment. That is not a criticism of anybody; it is arithmetic. The consequence is that the student carries more of the responsibility for process than they would in a larger school, and the pressure to get outside help is correspondingly higher.

The line the IB draws is about authorship. Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own, properly referenced, and produced without undisclosed assistance. A tutor may teach subject content, explain a criterion, question a research question, point at a flaw in a method, ask what the evidence supports, and respond in writing to a draft the student produced. A tutor may not contribute text or content to an assessed piece, rewrite it to a standard the student could not reach, or supply material that is then presented as the student's work.

There is a commercial market in the opposite of this, including operators that sell finished internal assessments outright. Buying one is a malpractice breach that risks the student's whole result, not a shortcut. No tutor on this platform produces assessed work, and we keep a written record of what each session covered precisely so that a school asking the question gets a straight answer.

Two practical habits reduce risk sharply. First, keep the drafts: dated versions in the student's own files demonstrate authorship better than any assurance. Second, tell the school that outside support is being used and in what form. Supervisors are not hostile to tutoring; what they object to, reasonably, is work appearing that does not match a student's classroom voice. Declaring it early removes the problem entirely.

sections.heading: What Diploma support costs in dirhams, and what moves the figure here
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for queries like this publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. Here is the market in dirhams instead, with each band attributed. These are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list: our own arrangement begins with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and what a plan costs depends on the subject, the level and the number of weeks remaining.

Diploma work sits in the upper part of the market. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutoring is advertised between roughly AED 200 and AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table giving AED 200 to 450 and above. A qualified subject tutor online sits around AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Premium named or examiner-led tutors are advertised higher, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Monthly figures appear too: packages of around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions reaching AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work.

Two factors move the number for a Ras Al Khaimah family specifically. Scarcity is the first: a Higher Level physics or Higher Level chemistry request in the northern emirates draws on a much thinner pool than general mathematics, and thin pools price accordingly in every format. Travel is the second, and it only applies to visiting tutors: a drive from the city to Al Hamra or Mina Al Arab is forty to sixty minutes each way, and that hour and a half is paid for somewhere inside the quoted rate.

Worth setting against the rest of the bill rather than looking at in isolation. School fees dominate, and in Dubai the Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Examination entries, past-paper resources and a graphical calculator are smaller but real. A Diploma plan of one weekly specialist hour in one subject across two years is a substantial commitment, and it is worth deciding deliberately which single subject gets it.

sections.heading: Getting started from Ras Al Khaimah, and what we will tell you straight
paragraphs: The useful opening move is not a phone call but three documents: the latest report, the most recent marked paper or internal assessment feedback sheet, and the written option blocks the school issued. Those tell a subject specialist what the problem is. A conversation tells them what the problem feels like, which is a different and less reliable thing. Send them and name the subject and level you are worried about.

The trial lesson is taught by the person who would teach the course and it is a lesson, not a sales call. It is free, no card is required, and afterwards you get a written note: what the tutor thinks is actually wrong, what a defined block would target, roughly how many sessions, and whether a tutor is the right purchase at all. Sometimes it is not. A Year 13 student three weeks from exam leave with four subjects in trouble needs triage and sleep more than a new weekly commitment, and we would rather say so.

Availability in the northern emirates is not unlimited and we state limits rather than hide them. A Higher Level science at short notice in a busy term is the request that most often cannot be filled immediately. Where that happens you get a date, an honest alternative, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. No competitor in the researched set discloses a coverage limit, and concealing one costs a family a term they cannot recover.

Everything then runs on Gulf Standard Time with a fixed weekly slot, a named tutor and a written note after each session. If the slot stops working because the school day changed or an activity commitment moved, it gets changed rather than missed. If the criterion levels or paper marks are not moving after a defined block, the review says so as a fact, and changing tutor or stopping are both normal outcomes rather than failures.

process.title: Name the subject, the level and the gap
process.description: Say which subject and level is in trouble and what the school has already said about it. A Standard Level entry where a university route expects Higher Level is a different job from a Higher Level student losing marks on paper technique, and the two need different tutors. Naming it precisely saves a wasted first session.

process.title: Send the three documents
process.description: Latest report, most recent marked paper or internal assessment feedback sheet, and the written option blocks. A specialist reads more from those in ten minutes than from any call. If an internal assessment draft exists, send that too, along with the supervisor's comments on it.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the subject specialist
process.description: Taught by the tutor who would take the course, with no card required and no condition attached. You receive a written opinion afterwards covering the likely cause, what a block would target, how many sessions and whether outside support is warranted at all for this student in this term.

process.title: Fix a slot the Ras Al Khaimah evening can hold
process.description: Al Hamra and Mina Al Arab households usually need 17:30 or later once activity commitments and the bus are accounted for; central districts can hold earlier. Gulf Standard Time is the reference, Ramadan timings are planned for in advance rather than improvised, and the slot moves rather than lapses.

process.title: Review on evidence, in writing
process.description: Every few sessions the tutor writes a note against the specific components being targeted, with the student's own marked work attached. If marks are not moving, that is reported plainly. Switching tutor, narrowing to one subject or stopping are all normal conclusions from a review rather than signs of failure.

whyPoints.title: Anchored to this emirate, not to Dubai
whyPoints.description: The regulator here is the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, the Diploma cohorts are small, and the option blocks are tight. Every section of this page is written from those facts rather than from generic UAE copy, because a plan built on a Dubai timeline misses the weeks this emirate actually has.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and level
whyPoints.description: Removing travel from the match is what makes a Higher Level chemistry or physics specialist reachable from the northern emirates. A request is matched against everyone qualified to teach that subject at that level rather than against the handful who could drive to Al Hamra by six o'clock.

whyPoints.title: Internal assessment handled properly
whyPoints.description: A large share of each Diploma grade is settled before the examination room. Sessions on an exploration, investigation, commentary or essay coach method and respond to the student's own drafts, and the tutor keeps a written record of what was done so the school can be told exactly what happened.

whyPoints.title: Dates we have not verified are not published
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page are taken from the boards' own published key-dates documents and attributed. IB session and results dates are not stated, because they must be confirmed with your school's coordinator or the IB directly, and restating an unverified date across many pages is how errors scale.

whyPoints.title: No regulator, board or school claims
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, any other emirate regulator, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, operates no UAE office or centre, and names schools and universities only as context for the local picture.

whyPoints.title: Rates in dirhams, with sources
whyPoints.description: Market bands are published here with the competitor or rate table each figure comes from, and with the date of the source. Our own plan price is settled after the free trial lesson, because subject, level and weeks remaining change it enough that a single advertised number would be misleading.

faqs.question: Why does a small Diploma cohort in Ras Al Khaimah limit my child's subject choices?
faqs.answer: Because each subject runs once. A Diploma student takes one subject from each of six groups, three at Higher Level, and on a large campus a popular subject appears in two or three timetable blocks so most combinations fit. A cohort in the tens supports one teaching set per subject, so any two subjects sharing a block become mutually exclusive. Ask the school for the written option blocks and for which degree routes the resulting combination closes. Then decide whether to argue for a small set against a study period or to cover the gap deliberately across the year.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school in Ras Al Khaimah, and what can it actually decide?
faqs.answer: The Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge. The federal portal states that it regulates private education in the emirate, and that the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That covers fee changes, programme additions and changes to how a year group is assessed, so there is an accountable route beyond the school office. Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain schools to the Department of Education and Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah schools to the federal Ministry of Education.

faqs.question: My child was put in Standard Level physics but needs Higher Level for engineering. What now?
faqs.answer: Name the gap in content terms and decide early. Ask the school in writing whether a Higher Level set can run against a study period, because small schools sometimes can. Ask each target university what it actually requires, since some accept a Standard Level subject with a strong overall profile. If the Standard Level place stands and the route still matters, the additional Higher Level content has to be covered deliberately across a year rather than crammed in a term. That is one of the commonest pieces of work we take on from this emirate, and it needs a specialist in the subject.

faqs.question: How much of a Diploma grade is decided before the examinations?
faqs.answer: A meaningful share in every subject, and the exact proportion is published in your school's course outline. The mathematics exploration, the sciences investigation, economics commentaries, the English individual oral and the computer science solution with documentation are all marked in school and moderated by the IB. For a student in a small cohort this is the part of the grade least affected by class size and most affected by whether the criteria were explained. It is also where coaching has the highest return, because the usual failures are structural and visible in a first draft.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work on my child's Extended Essay without crossing the IB's honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary that has to be kept precisely. A tutor may teach subject content, explain how the criteria are applied, interrogate a research question until it is answerable in four thousand words, point out a missing method section, ask what the evidence supports, and respond in writing to a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply text or content, rewrite passages to a standard the student could not reach, or produce any part of the essay. Keep dated drafts in the student's own files and tell the supervisor outside support is being used. Declaring it early removes the problem.

faqs.question: Do you publish the IB examination and results dates for the May session?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is specific. The IB's site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and restating an unverified date across many pages is how a single error becomes hundreds. Confirm every IB date with your school's coordinator or on the IB's own pages. Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page are different: they come from the boards' own published key-dates documents and are attributed, which is why the Cambridge March 2027 window appears here and an IB window does not.

faqs.question: When should the internal assessment work actually be finished?
faqs.answer: Against the school's internal deadlines, which sit months before anything is uploaded, and ideally earlier than those. In a small Ras Al Khaimah cohort one supervisor may be carrying a dozen Extended Essays alongside marking a subject's internal assessment, so an early draft gets real attention and a late one gets less. The autumn term of Year 13 is where this work should land. Treating a school deadline as negotiable spends the only period in the two years with genuine slack, and spring term has none to lend.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change how a Diploma student should plan revision?
faqs.answer: Materially, and planning for it beats improvising. The school day compresses and the usable evening moves, so families who shift sessions to a post-iftar slot in advance keep their weekly rhythm and families who do not lose a month of it. Shorter and more frequent works better than long sessions in these weeks. Mark the Ramadan period on the school calendar alongside the mock window, exam leave and public holidays before building a plan, because what remains after those four is the capacity the plan can actually use.

faqs.question: What does a Ras Al Khaimah family pay for Diploma tutoring?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours: specialist IB and IGCSE tutoring is advertised at roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table giving 200 to 450 and above. A qualified subject tutor online sits around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Premium named tutors go higher, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Scarcity moves the figure here more than anywhere: a Higher Level science request in the northern emirates draws on a thin pool. We quote after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Does my child need a Ministry of Education equivalency certificate for a UAE university?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is the family's process to complete rather than a school's or a tutor's. Start before results, because attestation takes time and university windows do not wait. The British-curriculum rules were clarified in July 2026 reporting: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No IB points figure is published here because we have not read one on the ministry's own site. Ask the ministry directly.

faqs.question: Can my child study for the Diploma at a university inside Ras Al Khaimah afterwards?
faqs.answer: Degree options exist within the emirate, which changes the planning for some families. The American University of Ras Al Khaimah, RAK Medical and Health Sciences University and University of Stirling RAK operate here, and each publishes its own admission requirements. The detail worth checking early is mathematics: engineering and health-science routes frequently expect Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation, and that decision is made at the start of Year 12. We name these institutions as context for route planning, with no relationship of any kind implied.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our villa in Al Hamra or Al Marjan Island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. Diploma lessons for Ras Al Khaimah families run one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen and a document both sides can write on. The reason is availability rather than cost. The number of people qualified to teach Higher Level chemistry or physics who are also willing to drive to the southern coast by six o'clock on a weekday is very small, and matching on subject instead of distance is what makes a specialist reachable here.

faqs.question: Our teacher left mid-year and the set has a cover teacher. Is that a tutoring problem?
faqs.answer: It is a continuity problem, and tutoring addresses part of it. Ask the school two questions in writing: who now marks and moderates the internal assessment for that subject, and what the plan is until the set is staffed. Those answers determine the real risk, which is usually the internally assessed component rather than the taught content. Where the gap is genuine, a subject specialist focused on the internal assessment and on the components the cover teacher is least able to mark is the highest-value hour available. A whole parallel course is rarely necessary.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for support in more than one Diploma subject at once?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the arithmetic usually settles it. A Diploma student in this emirate commutes, carries three Higher Levels plus the core, and has a finite number of usable evenings. Two weekly tutored subjects plus homework plus internal assessment work tends to produce worse results than one, because the hours between sessions are where learning happens and they get squeezed first. Pick the subject where a grade is both most at risk and most load-bearing for the university route, support that one properly, and revisit after a defined block.

faqs.question: What happens if you cannot find a tutor for the subject we need?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date. Higher Level sciences at short notice in a busy term are the requests that most often cannot be filled immediately in the northern emirates. In that case we will either name when a matched specialist becomes available, offer a tutor for an adjacent component where that is honestly useful, or say the request cannot be served well and suggest you look locally. No competitor in the researched set publishes a coverage limit at all, and hiding one costs a family a term that cannot be recovered.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-diploma-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the option blocks and the last marked piece of work
ras-al-khaimah/ib-diploma-tutor.closingBody: A Diploma problem in Ras Al Khaimah is usually a timetable problem wearing a subject's clothes. Before buying any hours, get the written option blocks, find out who marks and moderates the internal assessment in the subject that worries you, and read the last marked paper rather than the report comment. If after that a specific subject at a specific level still needs a specialist, send those documents and take the free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach the course. You will get a written opinion on the cause, a defined block with an end date, and an honest answer if another weekly hour is not what will move the grade.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-english-a-language-.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach group one English for the Diploma, which is a narrower job than teaching English well. Paper 1 rewards one thing, the comparative essay rewards another, and the oral is marked against a four-criterion rubric that has nothing to do with confidence.

intro.heading: Four options on the table, and a parent deciding between them in October
paragraphs: A Ras Al Khaimah family usually arrives at this search after a report card rather than after a crisis. The comment says the writing is fluent but descriptive, or that the response to unseen texts lacks analysis, and a grade five has appeared where a six or seven was assumed. From that point a parent is choosing between four things at once, and the choice is often made badly because nobody lays them out side by side.

The first option is to change course. English A: Language and Literature and English A: Literature are different subjects with different reading lists and different papers, and a student who dislikes advertisements, speeches and political cartoons may genuinely be better served by the literature course. The second is to change level, or to move out of group one altogether into English B, which is a language-acquisition course and a different qualification signal to a university. The third is to wait for the school's English department, which in a small Ras Al Khaimah cohort may be one teacher covering both group one courses. The fourth is to bring in outside support.

Each of those has a real cost and a real deadline. Course changes are usually possible only in the first weeks of Diploma year one, and almost never after the Individual Oral has been recorded. A level change from Higher to Standard removes the Higher Level essay but also removes a 20% component the student may have been doing well in. English B looks like relief and can close doors at admission. Doing nothing has a cost too, because the oral is recorded once and the mark does not get a second attempt.

This page is built as that comparison rather than as a sales pitch. Three tables set out the course differences, the level differences and what each delivery option costs in this market, with the published source for every dirham figure. The subject detail that follows is specific to Ras Al Khaimah because the school set here is small: two campuses carry most of the emirate's Diploma students, cohorts of eight or ten are normal, and there is rarely a second group one specialist in the building to give an independent reading of a draft.

On delivery, the position is plain. IB Gram does not run a centre in Ras Al Khaimah and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for families in Al Hamra, Al Nakheel, Mina Al Arab or Al Dhait are one-to-one and online, over live video, with the student's own marked script or draft shared on screen and annotated during the session. The argument for that here is availability rather than price: a specialist who has marked these four criteria is not necessarily someone who lives half an hour from your road.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-english-a-language-.programmesIntro: Group one English is a Diploma course, but a Ras Al Khaimah student arrives at it from one of three places, and the alternative a parent should be considering depends on which.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Language and Literature is one of two group one routes. Students study literary works alongside a body of non-literary material — journalism, advertising, speeches, photography, graphic texts — and are assessed on Paper 1, Paper 2, the Individual Oral and, at Higher Level, a written essay. The non-literary half is what distinguishes it, and it is the half most students have never been taught to read closely.
programmes.countryNote: Ras Al Khaimah Diploma cohorts are small enough that a school may run only one group one course. Where both run, the sets may share a teacher, which is why an independent reading of a Paper 2 draft is hard to obtain inside the emirate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Language and literature in the Middle Years Programme is assessed on four criteria covering analysis, organisation, producing text and language use. A student who consistently scored higher on producing text than on analysing it is already showing the profile that produces a descriptive Diploma essay two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Two campuses in the emirate run the Middle Years Programme to year five. Students arriving into the Diploma from the Indian or British streams instead have usually never met criterion-referenced marking, and read a grade five as a near-miss rather than as a description of what the writing did.

programmes.name: IGCSE English as the route in
programmes.description: Most Ras Al Khaimah students who enter group one English come from Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE English Language and Literature. Those courses reward accurate reading and controlled writing. The Diploma asks for evaluation of how a text positions a reader, which is a different instruction, and the shift catches out students who were comfortable at IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: An A or A star at IGCSE English is not a prediction of a seven in Language and Literature. The students who struggle most in Diploma year one here are frequently the ones whose IGCSE grade told them, reasonably, that English was already handled.

programmes.name: The Diploma core alongside it
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay sit on top of group one English, and for a student who writes well they tend to be registered in English. That concentrates the writing load into the same terms as the Individual Oral and the Higher Level essay.
programmes.countryNote: In a small cohort the same teacher may supervise the group one course and several Extended Essays. Families here should check in September which term holds the oral recording window, since it rarely moves.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-english-a-language-.subjectsIntro: The components below are what a group one grade is actually made of, listed with the level they apply to. Reading them as a single subject is how students end up strong at one and weak at another without noticing.

subjects.name: Paper 1: guided textual analysis
subjects.levels: SL one text, HL two texts
subjects.description: An unseen non-literary text with a guiding question. Standard Level analyses one in 1 hour 15; Higher Level analyses two in 2 hours 15. Worth 35% at both levels. Marks are lost in the first twelve minutes, when a student decides what the text is doing.

subjects.name: Paper 2: comparative essay
subjects.description: Four unseen general questions; the student answers one on two literary works studied, from memory and without the texts. Worth 35% at Standard Level and 25% at Higher. The common failure is two separate essays stapled together rather than one comparison.

subjects.name: Individual Oral
subjects.description: A fifteen-minute oral on a global issue, using one literary and one non-literary extract of up to 40 lines each. Marked out of 40 across four criteria. Worth 30% at Standard Level and 20% at Higher. Recorded once.

subjects.name: Higher Level essay
subjects.description: A 1,200 to 1,500 word essay on one literary work or one non-literary body of work studied, developed from a line of inquiry. Marked out of 20. Worth 20% of the Higher Level grade and the component students start latest.

subjects.name: The learner portfolio
subjects.description: Compulsory and not assessed, which is why it gets neglected. It is where the lines of inquiry that become the Higher Level essay and the global issue for the oral are supposed to be developed and recorded.

subjects.name: Non-literary bodies of work
subjects.description: Advertising campaigns, political cartoons, speeches, photojournalism, travel writing, infographics. Students who read fiction confidently often have no vocabulary for how a layout or an image argues, and Paper 1 is drawn entirely from this territory.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: The alternative group one course. Literary works only, with a different Paper 1 and a Higher Level essay drawn from literature. It suits a student who reads novels and plays willingly and finds the non-literary material arbitrary.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A group two language-acquisition course, not a group one course. Appropriate for genuine second-language learners. Moving a strong English speaker into it to protect a grade changes the qualification a university sees, which is why it deserves a conversation rather than a form.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Shares assessment vocabulary with group one English and competes for the same weeks. A student whose Theory of Knowledge essay is going badly is often having the same problem as in Paper 2: claims asserted rather than argued.

sections.heading: Alternative one: Language and Literature, Literature, or English B
paragraphs: These three are not interchangeable and a parent is often presented with them as if they were. Language and Literature studies literary works alongside non-literary material: advertising, journalism, speeches, cartoons, photography. Literature studies literary works only. English B is not a group one course at all — it sits in group two as a language-acquisition subject, and a university reading a transcript can tell the difference.

The reason this matters for a Ras Al Khaimah student is availability. In a cohort of eight or ten, a school may timetable only one group one course, so the choice is sometimes made by the timetable rather than by the student. Where both exist, the decision should turn on what the student can actually do. A reader who engages willingly with novels and plays and finds the analysis of a government poster arbitrary will do better in Literature. A student who is sharp about how media works and finds nineteenth-century prose a slog will do better in Language and Literature.

Moving a competent English speaker into English B to protect a grade is the decision most likely to be regretted. It is designed for second-language learners, and for a student educated in English since primary it will usually produce a high mark that says less to an admissions reader than a six in group one. There are students for whom it is genuinely the right course, and a bilingual household in this emirate is not by itself one of them.

Timing closes these doors quickly. Course and level changes are generally possible in the first weeks of Diploma year one and become impractical once texts have been studied and the oral extracts chosen. If this decision is live for your family, it is a September and October conversation with the Diploma coordinator, not a February one.

sections.heading: Alternative two: Higher Level or Standard Level, and the four real differences
paragraphs: Level is the second decision and it is widely misunderstood as reading more books. The number of literary works does rise — at least four at Standard Level, at least six at Higher — but three other differences matter more to a grade.

Paper 1 changes shape. Standard Level students analyse one unseen non-literary text in 1 hour 15 minutes. Higher Level students analyse two in 2 hours 15, which is not simply double: it demands a reliable method that can be executed twice under time pressure, and it punishes a student who reads slowly before deciding what to say. The paper is worth 35% at both levels, so the Higher Level version carries the same weight for harder work.

The Higher Level essay is the component that appears only at Higher Level, worth 20%, running 1,200 to 1,500 words on a single literary work or non-literary body of work. It is written outside examination conditions, which should make it the most reliable mark on the course. In practice it is the one students start last, because the learner portfolio that is supposed to generate its line of inquiry was treated as optional.

The weightings redistribute rather than increase. At Standard Level the oral carries 30% and Paper 2 carries 35%. At Higher Level the oral and Paper 2 drop to 20% and 25% to make room for the essay. A student who performs well orally and poorly in written examinations is therefore better served, arithmetically, by Standard Level — a point no school option sheet makes.

sections.heading: Alternative three: the school's own department, and what it structurally cannot do
paragraphs: The cheapest option is the school, and for many problems it is also the right one. A student who has missed lessons, or who has not read the second comparative text properly, needs the teacher and a reading schedule rather than a tutor. Clinic time, departmental revision sessions and a direct conversation with the group one teacher should be used first, and they cost nothing.

There are two things the school cannot structurally provide in a cohort this size, and they are worth naming without criticising anyone. The first is an independent second reading. When one teacher sets the task, teaches the text, approves the global issue and marks the draft, there is no second professional view available inside the building. On a component marked against criteria rather than right answers, a second reading is often what identifies the problem.

The second is unlimited one-to-one time. A teacher with two group one sets, several Extended Essay supervisions and a Theory of Knowledge allocation has a fixed number of hours. Twenty minutes on a Paper 2 draft is a generous slice of a department's week and is not enough to change a student's habit of writing two parallel essays instead of one comparison.

The honest sequence, then, is to exhaust the school first and bring in outside support for the specific thing the school cannot give: an independent marker, working one-to-one, on the student's own script, repeatedly, until the shape changes. That is a narrower claim than most tutoring pages make and it is the one worth paying for.

sections.heading: Alternative four: a visiting tutor in this emirate, priced as it actually is
paragraphs: Published hourly rates for one-to-one tuition in the UAE span a factor of ten, and most pages in this market publish none at all. The table below sets out bands that providers published themselves, with the provider named and the month they were read, so you can see what each figure is. None of them is an IB Gram price: our quote follows the free trial, because it depends on level, frequency and how close the recording window or the May session is.

Two features of Ras Al Khaimah push in-home figures up rather than down. Distance is the first: a tutor driving from the city side to Al Marjan Island or out to Digdaga absorbs close to an hour of unpaid travel, and that is inside the rate whether it appears on the invoice or not. Supply is the second. There is a workable pool of general English tutors in the emirate and a very small pool of people who have marked Diploma group one criteria. Scarcity in a thin market does not produce a discount.

IB Gram does not operate premises in Ras Al Khaimah and does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tuition is something we offer only in India. Lessons for families here are one-to-one and online over live video, with scripts and drafts shared on screen. The case for it in this emirate is access to a specialist rather than cost, although it is usually cheaper as well.

One practical note on paying anyone, including an independent tutor. An individual giving paid private lessons in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and those working without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask to see it; a tutor who holds one will not mind being asked.

sections.heading: Paper 1 in twelve minutes: why strong readers stall on the unseen text
paragraphs: Paper 1 gives a student a non-literary text and a guiding question, and asks for a focused analysis. It is worth 35% at both levels. The students who stall are rarely weak readers; they are usually students who read well and then write a description of what the text says rather than an argument about what it does.

The first twelve minutes decide the mark. In that window a student has to identify the text type and its conventions, work out the intended audience and the effect being sought, and settle on a controlling idea that the guiding question can be answered through. A script that starts writing before that is settled produces a tour of features — a simile here, a statistic there — with no line of argument for the examiner to follow, which is exactly what the analysis and evaluation criterion penalises.

Non-literary conventions are the gap that shows up most in this emirate, because IGCSE English rarely drills them. A political cartoon argues through caricature, juxtaposition, labelling and scale. An advertisement argues through the relationship between image and copy, through what is cropped out, through the register of a single verb. A speech argues through structure and repetition as much as through content. Students who have no vocabulary for these produce literary analysis of a non-literary text and wonder why the mark is mid-band.

At Higher Level the same method has to run twice in 2 hours 15. That makes timing a separate trainable skill rather than a by-product of competence. In lessons it is drilled as such: the twelve-minute planning phase first, against the clock, repeatedly, before any whole paper is attempted.
