sections.heading: The Individual Oral: a global issue, two extracts of forty lines, forty marks
paragraphs: The Individual Oral is fifteen minutes long, marked out of 40 across four criteria, and worth 30% at Standard Level or 20% at Higher. The student speaks for ten minutes on a global issue, drawing on one literary work and one non-literary body of work studied, using an extract of no more than 40 lines from each, and then answers five minutes of questions from the teacher.

The global issue is where most of the mark is won or lost, long before the recording. It has to be of genuine wide significance, transnational, and visible in the everyday. It also has to be narrow enough to be argued in ten minutes. Students pick themes rather than issues — identity, power, the environment — and then speak generally for ten minutes because a theme gives nothing to argue. A workable global issue sounds specific enough to be contestable, and the five fields of inquiry in the guide are a starting point rather than a menu to copy.

Extract choice is the second failure. An extract must be rich enough to sustain close analysis for several minutes and must actually show the global issue at work rather than merely mention it. Forty lines is both a limit and a hint: the examiner expects close work on the extract, not a summary of the whole work with the extract as an excuse. Choosing a passage because it is memorable is how students end up with nothing to analyse.

The oral is recorded once, and that single fact should change how a family plans. There is no retake for a weak recording in the way there is for a weak practice essay. Preparation blocks are therefore timed to the school's recording window, and rehearsal is done against the four criteria rather than against nervousness. The student's plan stays the student's; a tutor can question it, test it and mark a rehearsal, and should not supply it.

sections.heading: The Higher Level essay, and the portfolio nobody marks
paragraphs: The Higher Level essay is 1,200 to 1,500 words on one literary work or one non-literary body of work studied, marked out of 20 and worth 20% of the Higher Level grade. It is written away from examination conditions with access to the text, which should make it the most dependable mark on the course. For a large number of students it is the weakest, and the reason is almost always the same.

The essay grows out of a line of inquiry, and the line of inquiry is supposed to grow out of the learner portfolio. The portfolio is compulsory and not assessed, which in practice means it is maintained for the first term and abandoned. A student with no portfolio arrives at the essay with no developed question, invents one in a week, and writes 1,400 words of general commentary on a text they have not reread with a question in mind.

A good line of inquiry is narrow, arguable and answerable within 1,500 words. It names something specific about the work — a technique, a pattern, a structural decision — and asks what it achieves. A bad one asks how a theme is presented, which produces description. The difference is identifiable in a single tutorial, which is why this component responds well to one-to-one work earlier in the year rather than later.

What outside support may legitimately do here is bounded by IB academic honesty rules and we state it rather than leaving it vague. A tutor may teach the criteria, interrogate a line of inquiry, point at a paragraph that asserts instead of arguing, and mark a draft against the rubric. A tutor may not supply the line of inquiry, add sentences to the essay, or edit it to completion. The essay has to be the student's own work, and in a market that contains providers selling finished coursework that boundary is worth stating in plain words.

sections.heading: How lessons actually run for a Ras Al Khaimah household
paragraphs: Sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The student's own marked script, draft or chosen extract is shared on screen and annotated during the hour, which is the part that makes the difference: a student who watches their own paragraph taken apart twice begins doing it themselves before submitting. Sessions are recorded so an annotated script can be re-watched the night before a mock.

Scheduling here is set by geography and the school calendar rather than by preference. Students in Khuzam and Al Mairid can realistically start at 4pm. Students travelling back from the southern campuses to Al Marjan Island or Digdaga cannot, and an evening slot after dinner is both more realistic and more productive. During Ramadan the usable window moves to after Iftar, and a 5pm slot commonly becomes 9pm for the month; essay and oral work adapts to that better than most subjects because it needs concentration rather than equipment.

Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies are mandatory in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated in 40-minute lesson units and minimum weekly totals to be met. That is real timetable space, and for a group one student it often collides with the term that holds the oral recording window, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay deadline. Mapping those dates in September is what creates room later.

If no group one English specialist is free in the window you need, we tell you before you pay, with a realistic date. Where the available specialist is based outside the UAE, that is disclosed too, along with what it means for timing. Several providers in this market route UAE families to a contact number that implies local delivery and does not provide it; a thin market is a fact about this emirate and stating it is more useful than concealing it.

process.title: Send one marked script and two facts
process.description: The two facts are level and which component is causing the problem. The marked script matters more than any description of it: a Paper 1 response with a teacher's annotations usually shows the diagnosis directly, whether that is feature-spotting, weak audience awareness or no controlling idea.

process.title: We confirm a group one specialist is genuinely free
process.description: Before a slot is offered we check that a Diploma group one English specialist is available in your window on Gulf Standard Time. If one is not, you get a date rather than a substitute. A capable general English tutor will not fix a four-criterion oral problem.

process.title: A free trial lesson on real work
process.description: The trial runs on your child's own script, draft or chosen extract rather than a sample text. It should end with a named problem — the first twelve minutes of Paper 1, a global issue that is actually a theme, a line of inquiry that invites description — not a general impression.

process.title: A written plan with the weightings attached
process.description: You receive a plan naming the component being targeted and what it is worth, so you can see where the money is going. A Standard Level student with a 30% oral and a Higher Level student with a 20% essay deserve different plans, and usually get the same one elsewhere.

process.title: Weekly sessions, each with a written note
process.description: Every session ends with a short note on what moved and what did not, which makes progress checkable against the school's own marks rather than against impressions. The note names the criterion, not the effort level.

process.title: A six-week review against school marks
process.description: At six weeks we look at marked school work. If the targeted criterion has not moved, either the plan changes or the tutor does. That conversation is cheaper in November than in April, and the oral recording window is usually the hard deadline that decides which.

whyPoints.title: The decision laid out before the lesson is sold
whyPoints.description: Three of the four options on this page are not us. Changing course, changing level and using the school's own department are real answers for real students, and a family that picks one of them after reading this has been served properly.

whyPoints.title: Group one specialists, not general English teachers
whyPoints.description: Paper 1 rewards a repeatable twelve-minute method, Paper 2 rewards comparison rather than two essays, the oral is marked against four criteria. Those are technical tasks. Improving a student's prose and leaving the criteria untouched is the common outcome elsewhere.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every dirham figure on this page is attributed to the provider who published it and the month it was read. Most pages in this market publish no figure at all, and two of the ones that do quote a currency UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty boundary in plain words
whyPoints.description: Our tutors teach the criteria, question a line of inquiry and mark a draft. They do not supply global issues, write paragraphs or edit an essay to completion. This search results page contains providers who sell finished work; the distinction is the point.

whyPoints.title: Built for a small emirate
whyPoints.description: Ras Al Khaimah has few Diploma group one specialists and long drives between its communities. Online one-to-one is not second best here; it is the route to a specialist that does not depend on who lives near your road.

whyPoints.title: No dates we cannot verify
whyPoints.description: We publish no IB examination or results dates, because the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically and a second-hand date on a page like this would be a liability. Your Diploma coordinator holds the confirmed oral and submission windows.

faqs.question: Should my child move from Language and Literature to English A Literature?
faqs.answer: Only if the reason is the material rather than the mark. Literature studies literary works only; Language and Literature adds non-literary bodies of work such as advertising, speeches and cartoons, and Paper 1 is drawn from that territory. A student who reads novels willingly and finds the analysis of a poster arbitrary is often better placed in Literature. A student struggling with analysis itself will struggle in both. The window is practically the first weeks of Diploma year one, before texts are studied and extracts chosen, so this is a September conversation with the coordinator.

faqs.question: Is moving my child into English B a reasonable way to protect the Diploma grade?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it should not be done on a form. English B sits in group two as a language-acquisition course, not in group one, and an admissions reader can see the difference on a transcript. For a genuine second-language learner it is the right course. For a student schooled in English since primary it usually produces a high mark that says less than a six in group one would. A bilingual household in this emirate is not by itself a reason. Discuss it with the coordinator and with whoever is advising on university applications.

faqs.question: How many literary works does my child read at Standard Level compared with Higher Level?
faqs.answer: At least four at Standard Level and at least six at Higher Level, alongside non-literary bodies of work at both. The number is the least important difference. Paper 1 changes from one unseen text in 1 hour 15 to two in 2 hours 15 while staying worth 35%, and Higher Level adds a 1,200 to 1,500 word essay worth 20% that Standard Level does not sit. The extra reading is manageable; the extra component and the longer paper are what decide whether the level was the right choice.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 1 go badly when my child's English is clearly strong?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 1 is not a test of reading well. It gives an unseen non-literary text and a guiding question, and rewards an argument about what the text does to a reader. Strong readers often write an elegant description of what the text says, list several devices, and never commit to a controlling idea. The mark then sits mid-band in the analysis and evaluation criterion. The fix is the first twelve minutes: text type, audience, intended effect and one controlling idea settled before any sentence is written.

faqs.question: What exactly is a global issue for the Individual Oral, and how narrow should it be?
faqs.answer: Narrow enough to argue in ten minutes and significant enough to matter beyond one country. The guide offers five fields of inquiry as a starting point, covering areas such as culture and identity, beliefs and values, politics and power, art and imagination, and science and environment. Students commonly choose a theme instead — identity, power, the environment — and then speak generally, because a theme gives nothing to contest. A usable global issue is specific enough that a reasonable person could disagree with the student's claim about it.

faqs.question: How long can the two Individual Oral extracts be?
faqs.answer: Up to 40 lines each: one from a literary work studied and one from a non-literary body of work studied. The limit is also an instruction. The examiner expects close analysis of the extracts rather than a summary of the whole work, so a passage must be rich enough to support several minutes of detailed work and must show the global issue operating rather than simply mentioning it. Students who choose a memorable passage rather than an analysable one find themselves with ten minutes to fill and nothing in the text to fill it with.

faqs.question: If the oral recording goes badly, can it be done again?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a single attempt. The oral is recorded once and submitted, and it carries 30% of a Standard Level grade or 20% at Higher Level. That one fact should shape how a family plans the year: preparation is timed to the school's recording window rather than spread thinly, rehearsals are run against the four criteria rather than against nerves, and the global issue is settled weeks earlier than most students settle it. Ask the Diploma coordinator in September when the recording window falls, because it rarely moves.

faqs.question: What makes a comparative essay in Paper 2 score well?
faqs.answer: Comparison rather than coverage. The paper gives four general questions and the student answers one on two literary works studied, without the texts in front of them. The commonest mid-band script is two competent essays joined by a paragraph of transition. A strong script runs one argument through both works at once, moving between them inside paragraphs, with quotations held accurately from memory. That is a planning habit rather than a knowledge problem, which is why building plans for four question types beats memorising a model answer.

faqs.question: What should go into the learner portfolio if it is not marked?
faqs.answer: The work that becomes the two components students most often rush. The portfolio is compulsory and unassessed, and it exists to develop lines of inquiry and candidate global issues as the course goes along. A student who maintains it arrives at the Higher Level essay with three possible questions already tested against the text, and at the oral with a global issue that has been narrowed. A student who abandoned it in term one invents both in a single week, which is exactly how a 20% component becomes the weakest mark on the course.

faqs.question: How do I tell a good Higher Level essay line of inquiry from a weak one?
faqs.answer: A good one is narrow, arguable and answerable in 1,500 words. It names something specific in the work — a structural decision, a recurring technique, a pattern in how a campaign addresses its audience — and asks what it achieves. A weak one asks how a theme is presented, which can only be answered with description. The test is whether a reasonable reader could argue the other side. This is usually identifiable in one tutorial, which is why the essay responds better to support in term two than in the fortnight before submission.

faqs.question: What may a tutor legitimately do on the Higher Level essay or the oral?
faqs.answer: Teach the criteria, interrogate a line of inquiry or a global issue, point out where a paragraph asserts rather than argues, and mark a draft or a rehearsal against the rubric. What a tutor may not do is supply the inquiry question, write or rewrite sentences, edit to completion, or script an oral. IB academic honesty rules make that an expulsion risk for the student, and some providers in this market sell completed work outright. We teach it, question it and mark it; your child writes and speaks it.

faqs.question: Can my child's own English teacher in Ras Al Khaimah tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Assume not. The MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring a holder from tutoring students affiliated with their own school, and Abu Dhabi's regulator has published professional-ethics rules prohibiting school staff from paid private tutoring of their own enrolled students. The practical objection matters as much as the rule: the value of outside support on a criterion-marked component is an independent reading, and the person who set the task, taught the text and approved the extract cannot give you one.

faqs.question: Does a visiting English tutor come to Mina Al Arab or Al Hamra Village?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Ras Al Khaimah families are one-to-one over live video with scripts and extracts shared on screen. Independent visiting tutors do work in the emirate, and the published market band for an in-home hour runs roughly AED 180-500 including travel, but very few people within driving distance of these communities have marked Diploma group one criteria, which is the thing you are actually buying.

faqs.question: What does group one English tuition cost in this market?
faqs.answer: Published bands, which are not our prices, run roughly: AED 45-150 an hour for general online tutoring, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject teacher online, AED 180-500 for an in-home visit with travel included, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB subject specialist. EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate published those figures themselves. Monthly packages advertised here include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Our quote follows the free trial, because it depends on level, frequency and how close the recording window is.

faqs.question: It is twelve weeks to the May papers. Is the Higher Level essay still worth working on?
faqs.answer: If it has not been submitted, it is the best-value hour available, because it is the one component written with the text open and without a clock. Twelve weeks is also enough to change Paper 1 behaviour, since the twelve-minute planning phase is a drillable habit rather than new knowledge. What twelve weeks will not do is add two literary works to a student who has not read them, or re-record an oral. Spend the time on what is still movable and be honest about what is not.

faqs.question: What happens if no group one English specialist is free when we ask?
faqs.answer: You are told before paying, with a realistic date. We will not put a general English tutor in front of a four-criterion oral problem and describe it as the same service. Where the available specialist is based outside the UAE, that is disclosed too, along with what it means for scheduling against Gulf Standard Time. Several providers in this market imply local delivery through a contact number and deliver from elsewhere. Ras Al Khaimah is a thin market for Diploma group one English, and saying so is more useful than a confident booking.

ras-al-khaimah/ib-dp-english-a-language-.closingBody: If the live question in your household is whether your child should be in Language and Literature at all, settle that with the Diploma coordinator before buying any hours, because the window closes early in Diploma year one. If the course is right and the component is the problem, send one marked script and tell us the level. A group one specialist can usually name the issue before the first lesson — twelve-minute planning on Paper 1, a global issue that is really a theme, a line of inquiry that invites description, or a comparative essay written as two separate ones. The trial lesson is free and runs on that script. If nobody suitable is free in your window, we will tell you and give you a date.
